definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A group of cells that fluoresce for dopamine and are distributed in clusters that, in the primate, are ventral and medial to the mammillothalamic tract of the hypothalamus; a few extend into the reuniens nucleus of the thalamus (Felten-1983). In the mouse A13 is located ventral to the mammillothalamic tract of the thalamus in the zona incerta (adapted from Brain Info).
description_en: A group of cells that fluoresce for dopamine and are distributed in clusters that, in the primate, are ventral and medial to the mammillothalamic tract of the hypothalamus; a few extend into the reuniens nucleus of the thalamus (Felten-1983). In the mouse A13 is located ventral to the mammillothalamic tract of the thalamus in the zona incerta (adapted from Brain Info).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The subdivision of the vertebrate body between the thorax and pelvis. The ventral part of the abdomen contains the abdominal cavity and visceral organs. The dorsal part includes the abdominal section of the vertebral column.
description_en: The subdivision of the vertebrate body between the thorax and pelvis. The ventral part of the abdomen contains the abdominal cavity and visceral organs. The dorsal part includes the abdominal section of the vertebral column.

description_en: abdominal aortic nerve plexus

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bone that is part of an abdominal segment of trunk [Automatically generated definition].
description_en: A bone that is part of an abdominal segment of trunk [Automatically generated definition].

description_en: abductor digiti minimi (hand)

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The fourth stomach of ruminating animals, which is an elongated pear-shaped sac lying on the floor of the abdomen, on the right-hand side, and roughly between the seventh and twelfth ribs. It leads to the beginning of the small intestine. (Adapted From Black's Veterinary Dictionary, 17th ed).
description_en: The fourth stomach of ruminating animals, which is an elongated pear-shaped sac lying on the floor of the abdomen, on the right-hand side, and roughly between the seventh and twelfth ribs. It leads to the beginning of the small intestine. (Adapted From Black's Veterinary Dictionary, 17th ed).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Paired, additional vertebral articulations located medial to the intervertebral space, adjacent to the vertebral centrum.
description_en: Paired, additional vertebral articulations located medial to the intervertebral space, adjacent to the vertebral centrum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bone which does not occur frequently in the body but is still present in a significantly large number of organisms.
description_en: A bone which does not occur frequently in the body but is still present in a significantly large number of organisms.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): accessory hemi-azygos vein
description_en: accessory hemi-azygos vein

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An accessory bone of the pes that occasionally develops abnormally in front of the ankle towards the inside of the pes. This bone may be present in approximately 2.5% of the general population and is usually asymptomatic.
description_en: An accessory bone of the pes that occasionally develops abnormally in front of the ankle towards the inside of the pes. This bone may be present in approximately 2.5% of the general population and is usually asymptomatic.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Neural arch that is located posterior to the neurocranium and anterior to neural arch 1. The accessory neural arch is not associated with a vertebral centrum.
description_en: Neural arch that is located posterior to the neurocranium and anterior to neural arch 1. The accessory neural arch is not associated with a vertebral centrum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A lower continuation of the vertebral vein and vertebral venous plexus that passes through the foramen of the transverse process of the 7th cervical vertebra and empties into the brachiocephalic vein.
description_en: A lower continuation of the vertebral vein and vertebral venous plexus that passes through the foramen of the transverse process of the 7th cervical vertebra and empties into the brachiocephalic vein.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that is located lateral to vomer off midline of palate. Accessory vomerine tooth plate bears teeth and may be present as one or more pairs.
description_en: Dermal bone that is located lateral to vomer off midline of palate. Accessory vomerine tooth plate bears teeth and may be present as one or more pairs.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The spinal accessory nucleus lies within the cervical spinal cord (C1-C5) in the ventral horn. The nucleus ambiguus is classically said to provide the 'cranial component' of the accessory nerve. However, the very existence of this cranial component has been recently questioned and seen as contributing exclusively to the vagus nerve. The terminology continues to be used in describing both human anatomy, and that of other animals.
description_en: The spinal accessory nucleus lies within the cervical spinal cord (C1-C5) in the ventral horn. The nucleus ambiguus is classically said to provide the 'cranial component' of the accessory nerve. However, the very existence of this cranial component has been recently questioned and seen as contributing exclusively to the vagus nerve. The terminology continues to be used in describing both human anatomy, and that of other animals.

english: spinal part of the accessory nerve
translation_uz: spinal part of the accessory nerve (Suyak)
definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): spinal part of the accessory nerve
description_en: spinal part of the accessory nerve

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Mineralized bone tissue that has terminally differentiated osteoblasts but lacks osteocytes.
description_en: Mineralized bone tissue that has terminally differentiated osteoblasts but lacks osteocytes.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Acetabular part of the hip bone: the socket formed by ischium, ilium, and pubis, rimmed by the labrum and articulating via the lunate surface.
description_en: Acetabular part of the hip bone: the socket formed by ischium, ilium, and pubis, rimmed by the labrum and articulating via the lunate surface.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Vertebral centrum with flat ends. Between successive vertebrae there is a fibrocartilaginous intervertebral body with a gel-like core, the nucleus pulposus, which is derived from the embryonic notochord. Acoelous vertebrae seem especially suited to receive and distribute compressive forces within the vertebral column.
description_en: Vertebral centrum with flat ends. Between successive vertebrae there is a fibrocartilaginous intervertebral body with a gel-like core, the nucleus pulposus, which is derived from the embryonic notochord. Acoelous vertebrae seem especially suited to receive and distribute compressive forces within the vertebral column.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Any joint connecting the acromonion of the scapula and clavicle.
description_en: Any joint connecting the acromonion of the scapula and clavicle.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Region of the scapula where the latter meets with the clavicle: attachment point of the clavicle to the scapula in some taxa.
description_en: Region of the scapula where the latter meets with the clavicle: attachment point of the clavicle to the scapula in some taxa.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Acromiotrapezius is the middle trapezius muscle. It covers the dorsal and lateral surfaces of the scapula. Its origin is the neural spines of the cervical vertebrae and its insertion is in the metacromion process and fascia of the clavotrapezius. Its action is to draw the scapula to the dorsal, and hold the two scapula together.
description_en: Acromiotrapezius is the middle trapezius muscle. It covers the dorsal and lateral surfaces of the scapula. Its origin is the neural spines of the cervical vertebrae and its insertion is in the metacromion process and fascia of the clavotrapezius. Its action is to draw the scapula to the dorsal, and hold the two scapula together.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The subdivision of the skeleton that consists of all the skeletal elements at the distalmost end of the autopodium - i.e. the bones of the digits or their cartilaginous precursors[VSAO,modified].
description_en: The subdivision of the skeleton that consists of all the skeletal elements at the distalmost end of the autopodium - i.e. the bones of the digits or their cartilaginous precursors[VSAO,modified].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that bears part of the supraorbital canal and usually covers a large area of the neurocranium occupying part of the ethmoidal, orbitosphenoid, and otic regions. Commonly, the frontal bone articulates with its antimere medially, with lateral ethmoid, orbitosphenoid and pterosphenoid ventrolaterally, with supraorbital bone(s), autosphenotic and pterotic laterally, and with parietal posteriorly.[TAO].
description_en: Dermal bone that bears part of the supraorbital canal and usually covers a large area of the neurocranium occupying part of the ethmoidal, orbitosphenoid, and otic regions. Commonly, the frontal bone articulates with its antimere medially, with lateral ethmoid, orbitosphenoid and pterosphenoid ventrolaterally, with supraorbital bone(s), autosphenotic and pterotic laterally, and with parietal posteriorly.[TAO].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Fibrous joint connecting the actinopterygian frontal bone to the actinopterygian parietal bone.
description_en: Fibrous joint connecting the actinopterygian frontal bone to the actinopterygian parietal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that covers the otic region and may articulate with its antimere medially, with the frontal bone anteriorly, the pterotic laterally, the supraoccipital medio-posteriorly, and the epiotic and extrascapula latero-posteriorly. The parietal is a paired bone.[TAO].
description_en: Dermal bone that covers the otic region and may articulate with its antimere medially, with the frontal bone anteriorly, the pterotic laterally, the supraoccipital medio-posteriorly, and the epiotic and extrascapula latero-posteriorly. The parietal is a paired bone.[TAO].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An adductor muscle that attaches to the pelvic bone and the femur. In humans, the adductor magnus is a large triangular muscle, situated on the medial side of the thigh. The portion which arises from the ischiopubic ramus (a small part of the inferior ramus of the pubis, and the inferior ramus of the ischium) is called the 'adductor magnesius portion', and the portion arising from the tuberosity of the ischium is called the 'hamstring portion'. The hamstring portion is not considered part of the hamstring group of muscles, but it is adjacent to it.[WP,generalized].
description_en: An adductor muscle that attaches to the pelvic bone and the femur. In humans, the adductor magnus is a large triangular muscle, situated on the medial side of the thigh. The portion which arises from the ischiopubic ramus (a small part of the inferior ramus of the pubis, and the inferior ramus of the ischium) is called the 'adductor magnesius portion', and the portion arising from the tuberosity of the ischium is called the 'hamstring portion'. The hamstring portion is not considered part of the hamstring group of muscles, but it is adjacent to it.[WP,generalized].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A muscle in the manus that functions to adduct the thumb. It has two heads: transverse and oblique. It is a fleshy, flat, triangular, and fan-shaped muscle deep in the thenar compartment beneath the long flexor tendons and the lumbrical muscles at the center of the palm. It overlies the metacarpal bones and the interosseous muscles[WP].
description_en: A muscle in the manus that functions to adduct the thumb. It has two heads: transverse and oblique. It is a fleshy, flat, triangular, and fan-shaped muscle deep in the thenar compartment beneath the long flexor tendons and the lumbrical muscles at the center of the palm. It overlies the metacarpal bones and the interosseous muscles[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An alisphenoid bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.
description_en: An alisphenoid bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A manual digit found in Aves that is the most preaxial position and is morphologically similar to digit 1 in the standard tetrapod configuration and develops from embryonic digit 2, with contributions from embryonic digit 1.
description_en: A manual digit found in Aves that is the most preaxial position and is morphologically similar to digit 1 in the standard tetrapod configuration and develops from embryonic digit 2, with contributions from embryonic digit 1.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): In contrast to tubular glands, in the second main variety of gland, the secretory portion is enlarged and the lumen variously increased in size. These are termed alveolar glands (or saccular glands, or acinar glands, or acinous glands). Some sources draw a clear distinction between acinar and alveolar glands, based upon the shape of the lumen. A further complication in the case of the alveolar glands may occur in the form of still smaller saccular diverticuli growing out from the main sacculi. These are termed alveoli. The term 'tubulo-alveolar' (or 'tubulo-acinar', or 'compound tubulo-acinar', or 'compound tubulo-alveolar') is used to describe glands that start out as branched tubular, and branch further to terminate in alveoli. This type of gland is found in the salivary glands, esophagus, and mammary glands. The term 'racemose gland' is used to describe a 'compound alveolar gland' or 'compound acinar gland'.
description_en: In contrast to tubular glands, in the second main variety of gland, the secretory portion is enlarged and the lumen variously increased in size. These are termed alveolar glands (or saccular glands, or acinar glands, or acinous glands). This type of gland is found in the salivary glands, esophagus, and mammary glands. The term 'racemose gland' is used to describe a 'compound alveolar gland' or 'compound acinar gland'.

description_en: The thickened ridge of bone that contains the tooth sockets on the maxilla.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The thickened ridge of bone that contains the tooth sockets on the mandible.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The thickened ridge of bone that contains the tooth sockets on the premaxilla.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Spherical outcropping of the respiratory bronchioles and primary site of gas exchange with the blood. Alveoli are particular to mammalian lungs. Different structures are involved in gas exchange in other vertebrates[WP].
description_en: Spherical outcropping of the respiratory bronchioles and primary site of gas exchange with the blood. Alveoli are particular to mammalian lungs. Different structures are involved in gas exchange in other vertebrates[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Ectochordal, biconcave or terminally flat vertebral centrum. This design seems to allow limited motion in most directions. An intervertebral body (which may or may not be independent from the adjacent centra) fills the cavity between successive centra. The intervertebral body usually is formed by soft material that may be derived, at least in part, from the embryonic notochord.
description_en: Ectochordal, biconcave or terminally flat vertebral centrum. This design seems to allow limited motion in most directions. An intervertebral body (which may or may not be independent from the adjacent centra) fills the cavity between successive centra. The intervertebral body usually is formed by soft material that may be derived, at least in part, from the embryonic notochord.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The ampullae of Lorenzini are special sensing organs called electroreceptors, forming a network of jelly-filled pores. Each ampulla consists of a canal opening to the surface by a pore in the skin and ending blindly in a cluster of small pockets full of special jelly. The ampullae are mostly clustered into groups inside the body, each cluster having ampullae connecting with different parts of the skin, but preserving a left-right symmetry. The canal lengths vary from animal to animal, but the distribution of the pores is generally specific to each species. The ampullae pores are plainly visible as dark spots in the skin. They provide fish with a sixth sense capable of detecting electromagnetic fields as well as temperature gradients[WP].

Each ampulla consists of a canal opening to the surface by a pore in the skin and ending blindly in a cluster of small pockets full of special jelly. The canal lengths vary from animal to animal, but the distribution of the pores is generally specific to each species. The ampullae pores are plainly visible as dark spots in the skin. They provide fish with a sixth sense capable of detecting electromagnetic fields as well as temperature gradients[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Anal fin radial element that is composed of bone tissue.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that is located posterior to the dentary and lateral to the articular and retroarticular bones of the lower jaw. The angular forms the outer dermal sheet of the posterior part of the lower jaw. The angular bears a portion of the mandibular sensory canal. The angular is a paired bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Bone formed from the fusion of angular and surangular bones. Found in snakes.
description_en: Bone formed from the fusion of angular and surangular bones. Found in snakes.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone of anuran lower jaw investing lingual and ventral surfaces of Meckel's cartilage; forming coronoid process and articulating with palatoquadrate posteriorly.
description_en: Dermal bone of anuran lower jaw investing lingual and ventral surfaces of Meckel's cartilage; forming coronoid process and articulating with palatoquadrate posteriorly.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Secondary growth centers occurring as rings at the periphery of the superior and inferior surfaces of the vertebral body.
description_en: Secondary growth centers occurring as rings at the periphery of the superior and inferior surfaces of the vertebral body.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A ring of fibrous or fibrocartilaginous tissue (as of an intervertebral disk or surrounding an orifice of the heart).
description_en: A ring of fibrous or fibrocartilaginous tissue (as of an intervertebral disk or surrounding an orifice of the heart).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The ring of fibrocartilage and fibrous tissue forming the circumference of the intervertebral disc; surrounds the nucleus pulposus, which is prone to herniation when the annulus fibrosus is compromised.
description_en: The ring of fibrocartilage and fibrous tissue forming the circumference of the intervertebral disc; surrounds the nucleus pulposus, which is prone to herniation when the annulus fibrosus is compromised.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone of pectoral girdle that is dorsal to and articulates with the cleithrum.
description_en: Dermal bone of pectoral girdle that is dorsal to and articulates with the cleithrum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): One of a pair of thin sheets of smooth muscle inserting on the rectum, having a tendinous origin largely on sacral vertebrae.
description_en: One of a pair of thin sheets of smooth muscle inserting on the rectum, having a tendinous origin largely on sacral vertebrae.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Stegochordal slightly biconcave or flat terminally vertebral centrum. Each intervertebral cartilage is subdivided anteriorly and posteriorly, producing a free intervertebral element between adjacent vertebrae. This element subsequently ossifies and remains free.
description_en: Stegochordal slightly biconcave or flat terminally vertebral centrum. Each intervertebral cartilage is subdivided anteriorly and posteriorly, producing a free intervertebral element between adjacent vertebrae. This element subsequently ossifies and remains free.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Anterior cartilage of palatine - cartilage that caps the anterior end of the autopalatine bone. It is typically present in adults.

description_en: A vein that is a tributary of the superior ophthalmic vein and drains blood from the ciliary body of the eye.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony element (anterior coronoid bone) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.
description_en: A bony element (anterior coronoid bone) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The floor of the anterior fossa is formed by the orbital plates of the frontal, the cribriform plate of the ethmoid, and the small wings and front part of the body of the sphenoid; it is limited behind by the posterior borders of the small wings of the sphenoid and by the anterior margin of the chiasmatic groove. The lesser wings of the sphenoid separate the anterior and middle fossae.

description_en: foramina ethmoidalia anterius

description_en: anterior inferior iliac spine (volume)

description_en: A venous plexus that is tributary of the basivertebral veins and internal vertebral veins, draining blood from the vertebrae and spinal cord. The anterior internal vertebral venous plexus is located within the vertebral canal.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Indentation on the posterior margin of the pedicel. When two vertebrae articulate, the anterior notch of one vertebra and the posterior notch of the other create a bilateral intervertebral space.

description_en: anterior external jugular vein

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Process that is the anterior and medially directed portion of ceratobranchial 5 bone part of ceratobranchial 5 bone.
description_en: Process that is the anterior and medially directed portion of ceratobranchial 5 bone part of ceratobranchial 5 bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A ligament running the length of the anterior surface of the spinal column and thereby interconnects all the vertebral bodies.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The anterior aspect of the tympanum.
description_en: The anterior aspect of the tympanum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The anterior or rostral end of the zygomatic arch, which includes the temporal process of the zygomatic bone, but also including some of the body of the zygomatic bone. It may also include the zygomatico-temporal suture and the most rostral portion of the zygomatic process of the temporal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that is part of the scapular complex in placoderm fishes.
description_en: Dermal bone that is part of the scapular complex in placoderm fishes.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A muscle slip arising from the lingual surface of the mandible on the anterior portion of the bone. The fibers pass anteriorly, parallel to the mandible, and attach upon the ventral surface of the m. submentalis (Tyler, 1971).
description_en: A muscle slip arising from the lingual surface of the mandible on the anterior portion of the bone. The fibers pass anteriorly, parallel to the mandible, and attach upon the ventral surface of the m. submentalis (Tyler, 1971).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that is part of the scapular complex in placoderms, located in the ventral armour adjacent to the interolateral (IL) and anterior ventrolateral (AVL) plates.
description_en: Dermal bone that is part of the scapular complex in placoderms, located in the ventral armour adjacent to the interolateral (IL) and anterior ventrolateral (AVL) plates.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A ramus of the celithrum that descend along the girdle. Its rounded outer surface forms the articulation surface for the clavicle while its anterior surface overlaps with the anterior process of the scapulocoracoid.
description_en: A ramus of the celithrum that descend along the girdle. Its rounded outer surface forms the articulation surface for the clavicle while its anterior surface overlaps with the anterior process of the scapulocoracoid.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Highly vascular skin called velvet that covers the antler whilst it grows, supplying oxygen and nutrients to the growing bone.
description_en: Highly vascular skin called velvet that covers the antler whilst it grows, supplying oxygen and nutrients to the growing bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone positioned as the first bone of the infraorbital series. The antorbital articulates with the lacrimal or infraorbital 1 anteroventrally and the supraorbital posterodorsally. The antorbital is a paired bone.
description_en: Dermal bone positioned as the first bone of the infraorbital series. The antorbital articulates with the lacrimal or infraorbital 1 anteroventrally and the supraorbital posterodorsally. The antorbital is a paired bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The antorbital notch is a prominence of bone located anterolaterally of the antorbital fenestra.
description_en: The antorbital notch is a prominence of bone located anterolaterally of the antorbital fenestra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): annular ligament of radius
description_en: annular ligament of radius

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Orifice at the opposite end of an animal's digestive tract from the mouth. Its function is to expel feces, unwanted semi-solid matter produced during digestion, which, depending on the type of animal, may be one or more of: matter which the animal cannot digest, such as bones; food material after all the nutrients have been extracted, for example cellulose or lignin; ingested matter which would be toxic if it remained in the digestive tract; and dead or excess gut bacteria and other endosymbionts.
description_en: Orifice at the opposite end of an animal's digestive tract from the mouth. Its function is to expel feces, unwanted semi-solid matter produced during digestion, which, depending on the type of animal, may be one or more of: matter which the animal cannot digest, such as bones; food material after all the nutrients have been extracted, for example cellulose or lignin; ingested matter which would be toxic if it remained in the digestive tract; and dead or excess gut bacteria and other endosymbionts.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The spiral septum that separates the truncus arteriosus into a ventral pulmonary trunk and the dorsal aorta[MP]. The aorticopulmonary septum is developmentally formed from neural crest, specifically the cardiac neural crest, and actively separates the aorta and pulmonary arteries and fuses with the interventricular septum within the heart during development. The actual mechanism of septation of the outflow tract is poorly understood, but is recognized as a dynamic process with contributions from contractile, hemodynamic, and extracellular matrix interactions.
description_en: The spiral septum that separates the truncus arteriosus into a ventral pulmonary trunk and the dorsal aorta[MP]. The aorticopulmonary septum is developmentally formed from neural crest, specifically the cardiac neural crest, and actively separates the aorta and pulmonary arteries and fuses with the interventricular septum within the heart during development. The actual mechanism of septation of the outflow tract is poorly understood, but is recognized as a dynamic process with contributions from contractile, hemodynamic, and extracellular matrix interactions.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The dilated structure that is lined by endothelial cells and located at the arterial pole of the heart just above (distal to) the truncus arteriosus in mammalian embryos; it is the primordial vascular channel from which the aortic arches (and eventually the dorsal aortae) arise; the aortic sac is homologous to the ventral aorta of gill-bearing vertebrates.
description_en: The dilated structure that is lined by endothelial cells and located at the arterial pole of the heart just above (distal to) the truncus arteriosus in mammalian embryos; it is the primordial vascular channel from which the aortic arches (and eventually the dorsal aortae) arise; the aortic sac is homologous to the ventral aorta of gill-bearing vertebrates.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The palmar aponeurosis is a fibrotendinous complex that functions as the tendinous extension of the palmaris longus, when present, and as a strong stabilizing structure for the palmar skin of the hand. It has five longitudinal slips that project into the base of each digit and a deeper transverse portion that crosses the palm at the proximal end of the metacarpals bones (from Wikipedia).
description_en: The palmar aponeurosis is a fibrotendinous complex that functions as the tendinous extension of the palmaris longus, when present, and as a strong stabilizing structure for the palmar skin of the hand. It has five longitudinal slips that project into the base of each digit and a deeper transverse portion that crosses the palm at the proximal end of the metacarpals bones (from Wikipedia).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Ossicle that is part of the appendicular skeleton.
description_en: Ossicle that is part of the appendicular skeleton.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The ventral element in the priapium of the Phallostethidae on which articulate the ctenactinia (q.v.). Also called aproctal or pelvic bone.
description_en: The ventral element in the priapium of the Phallostethidae on which articulate the ctenactinia (q.v.). Also called aproctal or pelvic bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vertebral arch that is part of the first cervical vertebra.
description_en: A vertebral arch that is part of the first cervical vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An arch-shaped structure of the vertebra that extends dorsally (neural arch) or ventrally (hemal arch) from the vertebral centrum.
description_en: An arch-shaped structure of the vertebra that extends dorsally (neural arch) or ventrally (hemal arch) from the vertebral centrum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Pectoral girdle in which the epicoracoid cartilages are elaborated into posteriorly directed epicoracoid horns. Most arciferal pectoral girdles are characterized by fusion of the epicoracoid cartilages in the interclavicle region. Posterior to the clavicles, the epicoracoids usually are free and overlapping.
description_en: Pectoral girdle in which the epicoracoid cartilages are elaborated into posteriorly directed epicoracoid horns. Most arciferal pectoral girdles are characterized by fusion of the epicoracoid cartilages in the interclavicle region. Posterior to the clavicles, the epicoracoids usually are free and overlapping.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The arcuate artery of the foot (metatarsal artery) arises a little anterior to the lateral tarsal artery; it passes lateralward, over the bases of the metatarsal bones, beneath the tendons of the Extensor digitorum brevis, its direction being influenced by its point of origin; and its anastomoses with the lateral tarsal and lateral plantar arteries. This vessel gives off the second, third, and fourth dorsal metatarsal arteries. It is not present in all individuals.
description_en: The arcuate artery of the foot (metatarsal artery) arises a little anterior to the lateral tarsal artery; it passes lateralward, over the bases of the metatarsal bones, beneath the tendons of the Extensor digitorum brevis, its direction being influenced by its point of origin; and its anastomoses with the lateral tarsal and lateral plantar arteries. This vessel gives off the second, third, and fourth dorsal metatarsal arteries. It is not present in all individuals.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The bone of the upper arm, the humerus connects the shoulder to the elbow and provides the attachment points for muscles of the shoulder and arm that enable a wide range of upper limb movement. Proximally it articulates with the scapula at the glenohumeral joint, and distally with the radius and ulna at the elbow. Its surface landmarks include the greater and lesser tubercles, the deltoid tuberosity, and the medial and lateral epicondyles. Fractures of the surgical neck are common in elderly patients, while midshaft fractures may damage the radial nerve and cause wrist drop. In children, supracondylar fractures are the most common fractures at the elbow.
description_en: The bone of the upper arm, the humerus connects the shoulder to the elbow and provides the attachment points for muscles of the shoulder and arm that enable a wide range of upper limb movement. Proximally it articulates with the scapula at the glenohumeral joint, and distally with the radius and ulna at the elbow. Its surface landmarks include the greater and lesser tubercles, the deltoid tuberosity, and the medial and lateral epicondyles. Fractures of the surgical neck are common in elderly patients, while midshaft fractures may damage the radial nerve and cause wrist drop. In children, supracondylar fractures are the most common fractures at the elbow.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An artery that branches from the maxillary artery and supplies blood to structures in the auditory tube, tympanic cavity, and upper pharynx. The artery of the pterygoid canal courses through the pterygoid canal, a small bony canal located in the sphenoid bone of the skull.
description_en: An artery that branches from the maxillary artery and supplies blood to structures in the auditory tube, tympanic cavity, and upper pharynx. The artery of the pterygoid canal courses through the pterygoid canal, a small bony canal located in the sphenoid bone of the skull.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An insect gland dorsal to the insect gut, with a function analogous to that of the vertebrate liver. It is a storage organ for fats, glycogen and protein and is a major site of intermediary metabolism.
description_en: An insect gland dorsal to the insect gut, with a function analogous to that of the vertebrate liver. It is a storage organ for fats, glycogen and protein and is a major site of intermediary metabolism.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Digestive gland of crustaceans with functions approximately analogous to liver and pancreas of vertebrates - enzyme secretion, food absorption and storage.
description_en: Digestive gland of crustaceans with functions approximately analogous to liver and pancreas of vertebrates - enzyme secretion, food absorption and storage.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Ventral portion of a segment of an arthropod thorax or abdomen. In insects, the sterna are usually single, large sclerites, and external. However, they can sometimes be divided in two or more, in which case the subunits are called sternites, and may also be modified on the terminal abdominal segments so as to form part of the functional genitalia, in which case they are frequently reduced in size and development, and may become internalized and/or membranous.
description_en: Ventral portion of a segment of an arthropod thorax or abdomen. In insects, the sterna are usually single, large sclerites, and external. However, they can sometimes be divided in two or more, in which case the subunits are called sternites, and may also be modified on the terminal abdominal segments so as to form part of the functional genitalia, in which case they are frequently reduced in size and development, and may become internalized and/or membranous.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Endochondral bone that is located posterior to the dentary, medial to the angular and antero-dorsal to the retroarticular forming the lower jaw. The articular bears a dorso-posterior articular facet for the condyle of the quadrate. The articular is a paired bone.
description_en: Endochondral bone that is located posterior to the dentary, medial to the angular and antero-dorsal to the retroarticular forming the lower jaw. The articular bears a dorso-posterior articular facet for the condyle of the quadrate. The articular is a paired bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Cartilage of the lower jaw that give rise to a portion of the anguloarticular compound bone.
description_en: Cartilage of the lower jaw that give rise to a portion of the anguloarticular compound bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A thin layer of cartilage, usually hyaline, on the articular surface of bones in synovial joints.
description_en: A thin layer of cartilage, usually hyaline, on the articular surface of bones in synovial joints.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The ascending aorta is the portion of the aorta in a two-pass circulatory system that lies between the heart and the arch of aorta[GO]. A portion of the aorta commencing at the upper part of the base of the left ventricle, on a level with the lower border of the third costal cartilage behind the left half of the sternum; it passes obliquely upward, forward, and to the right, in the direction of the heart's axis, as high as the upper border of the second right costal cartilage, describing a slight curve in its course, and being situated, about 6 cm behind the posterior surface of the sternum. The total length is about 5 cm in length [Wikipedia].
description_en: The ascending aorta is the portion of the aorta in a two-pass circulatory system that lies between the heart and the arch of aorta[GO]. A portion of the aorta commencing at the upper part of the base of the left ventricle, on a level with the lower border of the third costal cartilage behind the left half of the sternum; it passes obliquely upward, forward, and to the right, in the direction of the heart's axis, as high as the upper border of the second right costal cartilage, describing a slight curve in its course, and being situated, about 6 cm behind the posterior surface of the sternum. The total length is about 5 cm in length [Wikipedia].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The ascending cervical artery is a small branch which arises from the inferior thyroid artery as that vessel is passing behind the carotid sheath; it runs up on the anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the cervical vertebrC& in the interval between the Scalenus anterior and Longus capitis. To the muscles of the neck it gives twigs which anastomose with branches of the vertebral, and it sends one or two spinal branches into the vertebral canal through the intervertebral foramina to be distributed to the medulla spinalis and its membranes, and to the bodies of the vertebrC&, in the same manner as the spinal branches from the vertebral. It anastomoses with the ascending pharyngeal and occipital arteries.
description_en: The ascending cervical artery is a small branch which arises from the inferior thyroid artery as that vessel is passing behind the carotid sheath; it runs up on the anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the cervical vertebrC& in the interval between the Scalenus anterior and Longus capitis. To the muscles of the neck it gives twigs which anastomose with branches of the vertebral, and it sends one or two spinal branches into the vertebral canal through the intervertebral foramina to be distributed to the medulla spinalis and its membranes, and to the bodies of the vertebrC&, in the same manner as the spinal branches from the vertebral. It anastomoses with the ascending pharyngeal and occipital arteries.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Process that is the dorsally directed portion of ceratobranchial 5 bone.
description_en: Process that is the dorsally directed portion of ceratobranchial 5 bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony dorsal extension of the clavicle.
description_en: A bony dorsal extension of the clavicle.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Foramen housing the root of the spinal nerve seen in the neural arch of the first vertebrae (atlas). (see Edwards 1976).
description_en: Foramen housing the root of the spinal nerve seen in the neural arch of the first vertebrae (atlas). (see Edwards 1976).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): articulatio atlanto-occipitalis
description_en: articulatio atlanto-occipitalis

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Ring-shaped and unusual in lacking both a vertebral body and a spinous process, the atlas is the first cervical vertebra and supports the skull. Its structure consists of anterior and posterior arches joined by two lateral masses. The concave superior articular facets of these masses cradle the occipital condyles at the atlanto-occipital joint, an arrangement that permits nodding movements, the flexion and extension of the head. Axial loading of the vertebra can produce a Jefferson fracture, a burst fracture of the ring, while atlanto-occipital dislocation is usually fatal. Among congenital anomalies, assimilation of the atlas describes its fusion with the occipital bone, a condition known as occipitalization.
description_en: Ring-shaped and unusual in lacking both a vertebral body and a spinous process, the atlas is the first cervical vertebra and supports the skull. Its structure consists of anterior and posterior arches joined by two lateral masses. The concave superior articular facets of these masses cradle the occipital condyles at the atlanto-occipital joint, an arrangement that permits nodding movements, the flexion and extension of the head. Axial loading of the vertebra can produce a Jefferson fracture, a burst fracture of the ring, while atlanto-occipital dislocation is usually fatal. Among congenital anomalies, assimilation of the atlas describes its fusion with the occipital bone, a condition known as occipitalization.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The intercentrum unit of the atlas vertebra.
description_en: The intercentrum unit of the atlas vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A hollow bony structure on the ventral, posterior portion of the skull of placental mammals that encloses parts of the middle and inner ear. In most species, it is formed by the tympanic part of the temporal bone.
description_en: A hollow bony structure on the ventral, posterior portion of the skull of placental mammals that encloses parts of the middle and inner ear. In most species, it is formed by the tympanic part of the temporal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): One of 3 small bones contained within the middle ear space and serve to transmit sounds from the air to the fluid-filled labyrinth. The absence of the auditory ossicles would constitute a moderate-to-severe hearing loss. The term 'ossicles' literally means 'tiny bones' and commonly refers to the auditory ossicles, though the term may refer to any small bone throughout the body. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: One of 3 small bones contained within the middle ear space and serve to transmit sounds from the air to the fluid-filled labyrinth. The absence of the auditory ossicles would constitute a moderate-to-severe hearing loss. The term 'ossicles' literally means 'tiny bones' and commonly refers to the auditory ossicles, though the term may refer to any small bone throughout the body. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony element (auditory ossicle cartilage element) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.
description_en: A bony element (auditory ossicle cartilage element) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony element (auditory ossicle endochondral element) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.
description_en: A bony element (auditory ossicle endochondral element) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony element (auditory ossicle pre-cartilage element) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.
description_en: A bony element (auditory ossicle pre-cartilage element) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Endochondral bone that is part of the antero-lateral region of the palate. Commonly, it articulates with the maxilla anterolaterally and with the ethmoidal region medially. It may also articulate with the dermopalatine ventro-laterally and with the entopterygoid posteriorly. The autopalatine is paired.
description_en: Endochondral bone that is part of the antero-lateral region of the palate. Commonly, it articulates with the maxilla anterolaterally and with the ethmoidal region medially. It may also articulate with the dermopalatine ventro-laterally and with the entopterygoid posteriorly. The autopalatine is paired.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Joint that articulates the autopalatine and lateral ethmoid and bones. Autopalatine-lateral ethmoid joint is paired.
description_en: Joint that articulates the autopalatine and lateral ethmoid and bones. Autopalatine-lateral ethmoid joint is paired.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Joint that articulates the autopalatine cartilage or bone and maxilla.
description_en: Joint that articulates the autopalatine cartilage or bone and maxilla.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Joint that articulates autopalatine and vomer bones. Autopalatine-vomer joint is paired.
description_en: Joint that articulates autopalatine and vomer bones. Autopalatine-vomer joint is paired.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bone that is part of a autopod region. Note that this incudes the carpal and tarsal bones.
description_en: A bone that is part of a autopod region. Note that this incudes the carpal and tarsal bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A subdivision of the autopod that corresponds to one or more bones arranged in series branching from the main limb axis.
description_en: A subdivision of the autopod that corresponds to one or more bones arranged in series branching from the main limb axis.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony element (avian scapholunar bone) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.
description_en: A bony element (avian scapholunar bone) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): One of the skeletal muscles of the head and neck, spine, and ribs.
description_en: One of the skeletal muscles of the head and neck, spine, and ribs.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Musculature of the head and neck, spine, and ribs.
description_en: Musculature of the head and neck, spine, and ribs.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Ossicle that is part of the axial skeleton.
description_en: Ossicle that is part of the axial skeleton.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Subdivision of skeleton which consists of cranial skeleton, set of all vertebrae, set of all ribs and sternum[FMA, modified].
description_en: Subdivision of skeleton which consists of cranial skeleton, set of all vertebrae, set of all ribs and sternum[FMA, modified].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The second cervical vertebra, the axis provides the pivot around which the head rotates. Its defining feature is the dens, or odontoid process, a tooth-like projection that extends superiorly from the body to articulate with the anterior arch of the atlas above it. This arrangement accounts for roughly half of the rotation available in the cervical spine. Odontoid fractures are common cervical injuries, particularly in elderly patients, and a hangman's fracture involves bilateral fractures of the pars interarticularis of C2. Atlantoaxial instability, in which the joint between the atlas and axis becomes abnormally mobile, is associated with rheumatoid arthritis and Down syndrome.
description_en: The second cervical vertebra, the axis provides the pivot around which the head rotates. Its defining feature is the dens, or odontoid process, a tooth-like projection that extends superiorly from the body to articulate with the anterior arch of the atlas above it. This arrangement accounts for roughly half of the rotation available in the cervical spine. Odontoid fractures are common cervical injuries, particularly in elderly patients, and a hangman's fracture involves bilateral fractures of the pars interarticularis of C2. Atlantoaxial instability, in which the joint between the atlas and axis becomes abnormally mobile, is associated with rheumatoid arthritis and Down syndrome.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The intercentrum unit of the axis vertebra. .
description_en: The intercentrum unit of the axis vertebra. .

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The basal vein is formed at the anterior perforated substance by the union of (a) a small anterior cerebral vein which accompanies the anterior cerebral artery and supplies the medial surface of the frontal lobe by the fronto-basal vein. (b) the deep middle cerebral vein (deep Sylvian vein), which receives tributaries from the insula and neighboring gyri, and runs in the lower part of the lateral cerebral fissure, and (c) the inferior striate veins, which leave the corpus striatum through the anterior perforated substance. The basal vein passes backward around the cerebral peduncle, and ends in the internal cerebral vein; it receives tributaries from the interpeduncular fossa, the inferior horn of the lateral ventricle, the hippocampal gyrus, and the mid-brain.
description_en: The basal vein is formed at the anterior perforated substance by the union of (a) a small anterior cerebral vein which accompanies the anterior cerebral artery and supplies the medial surface of the frontal lobe by the fronto-basal vein. (b) the deep middle cerebral vein (deep Sylvian vein), which receives tributaries from the insula and neighboring gyri, and runs in the lower part of the lateral cerebral fissure, and (c) the inferior striate veins, which leave the corpus striatum through the anterior perforated substance. The basal vein passes backward around the cerebral peduncle, and ends in the internal cerebral vein; it receives tributaries from the interpeduncular fossa, the inferior horn of the lateral ventricle, the hippocampal gyrus, and the mid-brain.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Basibranchial bone that is ventral, median, and associated with branchial arch 1 (pharyngeal arch 3). Typically develops in the anterior copula cartilage.
description_en: Basibranchial bone that is ventral, median, and associated with branchial arch 1 (pharyngeal arch 3). Typically develops in the anterior copula cartilage.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Basibranchial bone that is ventral, median, and associated with branchial arch 2 (pharyngeal arch 4). Typically develops in the anterior copula cartilage.
description_en: Basibranchial bone that is ventral, median, and associated with branchial arch 2 (pharyngeal arch 4). Typically develops in the anterior copula cartilage.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Pharyngeal tooth plate that lies dorsal to basibranchial 2 bone.
description_en: Pharyngeal tooth plate that lies dorsal to basibranchial 2 bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Basibranchial bone that is ventral, median, and associated with branchial arch 3 (pharyngeal arch 5). Typically develops in the anterior copula cartilage.
description_en: Basibranchial bone that is ventral, median, and associated with branchial arch 3 (pharyngeal arch 5). Typically develops in the anterior copula cartilage.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Basibranchial bone that is ventral, median, and associated with branchial arch 4 (pharyngeal arch 6). Develops in posterior copula cartilage or basibranchial 4 cartilage.
description_en: Basibranchial bone that is ventral, median, and associated with branchial arch 4 (pharyngeal arch 6). Develops in posterior copula cartilage or basibranchial 4 cartilage.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Pharyngeal tooth plate that lies dorsal to basibranchial 4 bone.
description_en: Pharyngeal tooth plate that lies dorsal to basibranchial 4 bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Basibranchial bone that is ventral, median, and associated with branchial arch 5 (pharyngeal arch 7). Develops in posterior copula cartilage or basibranchial 5 cartilage.
description_en: Basibranchial bone that is ventral, median, and associated with branchial arch 5 (pharyngeal arch 7). Develops in posterior copula cartilage or basibranchial 5 cartilage.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A basibranchial element that is bone. Basibranchial elements are ventral, median, and associated with a single pharyngeal arch in the pharyngeal arch 3-7 skeleton.
description_en: A basibranchial element that is bone. Basibranchial elements are ventral, median, and associated with a single pharyngeal arch in the pharyngeal arch 3-7 skeleton.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Replacement bone that is median and is the anterior-most bone of the ventral hyoid arch.
description_en: Replacement bone that is median and is the anterior-most bone of the ventral hyoid arch.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): lingual process of basihyoid
description_en: lingual process of basihyoid

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Pharyngeal tooth plate that lies dorsal to the basihyal cartilage or bone.
description_en: Pharyngeal tooth plate that lies dorsal to the basihyal cartilage or bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): One of the bones of the occiput, the part of the skull which articulates with the spine. The basioccipital is located (if present) ventral to the foramen magnum. It often rests on or articulates with the basisphenoid, as well as meeting the exoccipitals. The basioccipital usually forms most (sometimes all) of the occipital condyle(s) and the ventral margin of the foramen magnum.
description_en: One of the bones of the occiput, the part of the skull which articulates with the spine. The basioccipital is located (if present) ventral to the foramen magnum. It often rests on or articulates with the basisphenoid, as well as meeting the exoccipitals. The basioccipital usually forms most (sometimes all) of the occipital condyle(s) and the ventral margin of the foramen magnum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A basioccipital bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.
description_en: A basioccipital bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Endochondral bone which is the posterodorsal region of the basioccipital bone.
description_en: Endochondral bone which is the posterodorsal region of the basioccipital bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A small bone in the fetus between the basilar process and the basisphenoid.
description_en: A small bone in the fetus between the basilar process and the basisphenoid.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Basipterygium element that is composed of bone tissue.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A blastema is a mass of cells capable of growth and regeneration into organs or body parts. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The brachiocephalicus is a long and flat, complex of muscles that extends from the lower half of the humeral shaft to the head and neck. The muscle divides into two parts at the clavicular intersection. This is also the point of origin for all the muscles that make up the brachiocephalicus. This point is situated just cranial to the shoulder. The two main sections are the cleidobrachialis which is distal to the clavicular intersection and the cleidocephalicus which extends proximally to the clavivular intersection. The cleidocephalicus can also be divided into the pars cervicalis, which inserts on the broad aponeurosis, over the fibrous raphe of the cranial half of the neck. The other part, the pars mastoideus inserts on the mastoid process of the temporal bone via a strong tendon. The cleidobrachialis extends distally from the clavicular intersection and inserts on the cranial edge of the distal half of the humerus. The tendon that inserts the cleidobrachialis lies between the brachialis muscle and the biceps brachii. As a result of the brachiocephalicus spanning a large region it has the ability to provide a number of actions. These include extending the shoulder joint, protracts the limb, provides lateral movement of the head and allows the neck to be depressed.

The muscle divides into two parts at the clavicular intersection. This is also the point of origin for all the muscles that make up the brachiocephalicus. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The term area 4 of Brodmann-1909 refers to a cytoarchitecturally defined portion of the frontal lobe of the guenon. It is located predominantly in the precentral gyrus. Brodmann-1909 regarded it as topographically and cytoarchitecturally homologous to the human gigantopyramidal area 4 and noted that it occupies a much greater fraction of the frontal lobe in the monkey than in the human. Distinctive features (Brodmann-1905): the cortex is unusually thick; the layers are not distinct; the cells are relatively sparsely distributed; giant pyramidal (Betz) cells are present in the internal pyramidal layer (V); lack of an internal granular layer (IV) such that the boundary between the external pyramidal layer (III) and the internal pyramidal layer (V) is indistinct; lack of a distinct external granular layer (II); a gradual transition from the multiform layer (VI) to the subcortical white matter.
description_en: The term area 4 of Brodmann-1909 refers to a cytoarchitecturally defined portion of the frontal lobe of the guenon. It is located predominantly in the precentral gyrus. Brodmann-1909 regarded it as topographically and cytoarchitecturally homologous to the human gigantopyramidal area 4 and noted that it occupies a much greater fraction of the frontal lobe in the monkey than in the human. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Brodmann area 43 is a subdivision of the cerebral cortex of the guenon defined on the basis of cytoarchitecture. It was described (but not labeled) on the map of cortical areas in Brodmann-1909, and it was regarded as cytoarchitecturally homologous to area 30 of Mauss in 1908 in the guenon and subcentral area 43 of the human (Brodmann-1909). The Vogts found no distinctive architectonic area of the corresponding location in the guenon (Vogts-1919).
description_en: Brodmann area 43 is a subdivision of the cerebral cortex of the guenon defined on the basis of cytoarchitecture. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Brodmann area 46, or BA46, is part of the frontal cortex in the human brain. It is between BA10 and BA45. BA46 is known as middle frontal area 46. In the human it occupies approximately the middle third of the middle frontal gyrus and the most rostral portion of the inferior frontal gyrus. Brodmann area 46 roughly corresponds with the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), although the borders of area 46 are based on cytoarchitecture rather than function. The DLPFC also encompasses part of granular frontal area 9, directly adjacent on the dorsal surface of the cortex. Cytoarchitecturally, BA46 is bounded dorsally by the granular frontal area 9, rostroventrally by the frontopolar area 10 and caudally by the triangular area 45 (Brodmann-1909). There is some discrepancy between the extent of BA8 (Brodmann-1905) and the same area as described by Walker (1940).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Retrosubicular area 48 is a subdivision of the cytoarchitecturally defined hippocampal region of the cerebral cortex. In the human it is located on the medial surface of the temporal lobe. Cytoarchitectually it is bounded rostrally by the perirhinal area 35 and medially by the presubiculum. While described by Brodmann (Brodmann-1909), it was not included in his areal maps of human cortex (Brodmann-1909; Brodmann-1910).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Brodmann area 9, or BA9, refers to a cytoarchitecturally defined portion of the frontal cortex in the brain of humans and other primates. It contributes to the dorsolateral and medial prefrontal cortex and plays a role in executive functions such as working memory, planning, inhibition, decision-making, and reasoning. Its cytoarchitecture is referred to as granular due to the concentration of granule cells in layer IV. Its internal pyramidal layer (V) is divisible into two sublayers, an outer layer 5a of densely distributed medium-size ganglion cells that partially merges with layer IV, and an inner, clearer, cell-poor layer 5b; the pyramidal cells of sublayer 3b of the external pyramidal layer (III) are smaller and sparser in distribution; the external granular layer (II) is narrow, with small numbers of sparsely distributed granule cells.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that is ventral to the preopercle and bears a portion of the preopercular sensory canal.
description_en: Dermal bone that is ventral to the preopercle and bears a portion of the preopercular sensory canal.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A smooth, rounded eminence on the lateral portion of the articular surface of the humerus. It articulates with the cupshaped depression on the head of the radius, and is limited to the front and lower part of the bone.
description_en: A smooth, rounded eminence on the lateral portion of the articular surface of the humerus. It articulates with the cupshaped depression on the head of the radius, and is limited to the front and lower part of the bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Convex articular facet of the vertebral centrum for the articulation with the adjacent centrum.
description_en: Convex articular facet of the vertebral centrum for the articulation with the adjacent centrum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dorsal subdivision of turtle shell, consisting of the animal's ribcage combined with dermal bone[WP, modified].
description_en: Dorsal subdivision of turtle shell, consisting of the animal's ribcage combined with dermal bone[WP, modified].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Fused dorsal element constituting the carapace of a turtle shell.
description_en: Fused dorsal element constituting the carapace of a turtle shell.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Any of the four veins in the developing vertebrate embryo which run along each side of the vertebral column.
description_en: Any of the four veins in the developing vertebrate embryo which run along each side of the vertebral column.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An extension of the sternum (breastbone) which runs axially along the midline of the sternum and extends outward, perpendicular to the plane of the ribs[WP].
description_en: An extension of the sternum (breastbone) which runs axially along the midline of the sternum and extends outward, perpendicular to the plane of the ribs[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): On the interior surface of the temporal bone, behind the rough surface of the apex, is the large circular aperture of the carotid canal, which ascends at first vertically, and then, making a bend, runs horizontally forward and medialward. It transmits into the cranium, the internal carotid artery, and the carotid plexus of nerves. Sympathetics to the head also pass through the carotid canal. They have several motor functions: raise the eyelid (superior tarsal muscle), dilate pupil, innervate sweat glands of face and scalp and constricts blood vessels in head[WP].
description_en: On the interior surface of the temporal bone, behind the rough surface of the apex, is the large circular aperture of the carotid canal, which ascends at first vertically, and then, making a bend, runs horizontally forward and medialward. It transmits into the cranium, the internal carotid artery, and the carotid plexus of nerves. Sympathetics to the head also pass through the carotid canal. They have several motor functions: raise the eyelid (superior tarsal muscle), dilate pupil, innervate sweat glands of face and scalp and constricts blood vessels in head[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bone that is part of the carpal skeleton. Examples: scaphoid, lunate, capitate[cjm].
description_en: A bone that is part of the carpal skeleton. Examples: scaphoid, lunate, capitate[cjm].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A mesopodium that is part of a manus. Includes as parts the carpal skeleton and associated tissues[cjm]. The anatomical region surrounding the carpus including the distal parts of the bones of the forearm and the proximal parts of the metacarpus or five metacarpal bones and the series of joints between these bones, thus referred to as wrist joints. This region also includes the carpal tunnel, the anatomical snuff box, the flexor retinaculum, and the extensor retinaculum[WP,unvetted].
description_en: A mesopodium that is part of a manus. Includes as parts the carpal skeleton and associated tissues[cjm]. The anatomical region surrounding the carpus including the distal parts of the bones of the forearm and the proximal parts of the metacarpus or five metacarpal bones and the series of joints between these bones, thus referred to as wrist joints. This region also includes the carpal tunnel, the anatomical snuff box, the flexor retinaculum, and the extensor retinaculum[WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The carpometacarpal joints (CMC) are joints in the wrist that articulates the distal row of carpal bones and the proximal bases of the metacarpal bones.
description_en: The carpometacarpal joints (CMC) are joints in the wrist that articulates the distal row of carpal bones and the proximal bases of the metacarpal bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The carpometacarpus is the fusion of the carpal and metacarpal bone, essentially a single fused bone between the wrist and the knuckles. It is a smallish bone in most birds, generally flattened and with a large hole in the middle. In flightless birds, however, its shape may be slightly different, or it might be absent entirely.
description_en: The carpometacarpus is the fusion of the carpal and metacarpal bone, essentially a single fused bone between the wrist and the knuckles. It is a smallish bone in most birds, generally flattened and with a large hole in the middle. In flightless birds, however, its shape may be slightly different, or it might be absent entirely.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A cartilaginous condensation that has the potential to develop into a carpal bone.
description_en: A cartilaginous condensation that has the potential to develop into a carpal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A carpus bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.
description_en: A carpus bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A pre-cartilage condensation that has the potential to develop into a carpal bone.
description_en: A pre-cartilage condensation that has the potential to develop into a carpal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Any portion of cartilage tissue that is part of the sternum.
description_en: Any portion of cartilage tissue that is part of the sternum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Nonsynovial joint in which the articulating bones or cartilages are connected by cartilage. Examples: Spheno-occipital synchondrosis, first sternocostal joint, pubic symphysis.[FMA].
description_en: Nonsynovial joint in which the articulating bones or cartilages are connected by cartilage. Examples: Spheno-occipital synchondrosis, first sternocostal joint, pubic symphysis.[FMA].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): One of the cartilaginous structures surrounding the embryonic spinal cord, formed by the dorsal growth of the dorsolateral arcualia; it is the primordium of the vertebral arch.
description_en: One of the cartilaginous structures surrounding the embryonic spinal cord, formed by the dorsal growth of the dorsolateral arcualia; it is the primordium of the vertebral arch.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): cartilaginous chondocranium
description_en: cartilaginous chondocranium

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Cartilaginous form of a vertebral centrum, a skeletal element that functionally replaces the notochord[VSAP,modified].
description_en: Cartilaginous form of a vertebral centrum, a skeletal element that functionally replaces the notochord[VSAP,modified].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The cauda equina is a structure within the lower end of the spinal column of most vertebrates, that consists of nerve roots and rootlets from above. The space in which the cerebrospinal fluid is present is actually an extension of the subarachnoid space.
description_en: The cauda equina is a structure within the lower end of the spinal column of most vertebrates, that consists of nerve roots and rootlets from above. The space in which the cerebrospinal fluid is present is actually an extension of the subarachnoid space.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that is located anterior to the caudal fin procurrent rays. Caudal fin stays are unpaired median bones.
description_en: Dermal bone that is located anterior to the caudal fin procurrent rays. Caudal fin stays are unpaired median bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Caudal procurrent ray that forms part of the anterior ventral series of lepidotrichia of the caudal fin that may be associated with a neural spine or a epural or an uroneural (dorsal series) and with a hemal spine of a preural vertebra (ventral series). A caudal procurrent ray is an unpaired median bone.
description_en: Caudal procurrent ray that forms part of the anterior ventral series of lepidotrichia of the caudal fin that may be associated with a neural spine or a epural or an uroneural (dorsal series) and with a hemal spine of a preural vertebra (ventral series). A caudal procurrent ray is an unpaired median bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Muscle that is associated with tail flexion. Orginates on one of the first post sacral vertebrae posteriorly and inserts on the posterior edge of the m.puboischiotibialis. (modified from Duellman and Trueb 1994).
description_en: Muscle that is associated with tail flexion. Orginates on one of the first post sacral vertebrae posteriorly and inserts on the posterior edge of the m.puboischiotibialis. (modified from Duellman and Trueb 1994).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Caudal fin lepidotrichium that is adjacent to a branched ray. Caudal principal rays may be segmented but unbranched and the main element forming the dorsal or ventral leading margin of the caudal fin or a ray that may be only segmented-and-branched and forms part of the middle-posterior region of the fin. A caudal principal ray is an unpaired median bone.
description_en: Caudal fin lepidotrichium that is adjacent to a branched ray. Caudal principal rays may be segmented but unbranched and the main element forming the dorsal or ventral leading margin of the caudal fin or a ray that may be only segmented-and-branched and forms part of the middle-posterior region of the fin. A caudal principal ray is an unpaired median bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Anatomical cluster including all segmented-and-branched rays plus one unbranched but segmented ray located at the leading margin in each lobe of the caudal fin (Hubbs and Lagler, 1947) and that associates with endoskeletal elements such as hypurals and hemal spines of preural centra 1 and 2 (Arratia, 2008). Caudal principal rays are counted from the dorsalmost one ventrally. Caudal principal rays are unpaired median bones.
description_en: Anatomical cluster including all segmented-and-branched rays plus one unbranched but segmented ray located at the leading margin in each lobe of the caudal fin (Hubbs and Lagler, 1947) and that associates with endoskeletal elements such as hypurals and hemal spines of preural centra 1 and 2 (Arratia, 2008). Caudal principal rays are counted from the dorsalmost one ventrally. Caudal principal rays are unpaired median bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Caudal fin lepidotrichium that form part of the anterior dorsal and ventral series of lepidotrichia of the caudal fin that may be associated with a neural spine or an epural or an uroneural (dorsal series) and with a haemal spine of a preural vertebra (ventral series). Caudal procurrent rays are shorter than the caudal principal rays. A caudal procurrent ray is an unpaired median bone.
description_en: Caudal fin lepidotrichium that form part of the anterior dorsal and ventral series of lepidotrichia of the caudal fin that may be associated with a neural spine or an epural or an uroneural (dorsal series) and with a haemal spine of a preural vertebra (ventral series). Caudal procurrent rays are shorter than the caudal principal rays. A caudal procurrent ray is an unpaired median bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An anatomical cluster of short rays, shorter than the principal ones, which form the anterior dorsal and ventral series of lepidotrichia of the caudal fin that may be associated with neural spines, epurals and uroneurals (dorsal series) and haemal spines of preural vertebrae (ventral series) (Arratia, 2008). The anteriormost procurrent rays are commonly unsegmented, but the posteriormost ones are usually segmented. The procurrent rays are numbered from caudal to rostral direction. The caudal procurrent ray series is an unpaired median series.
description_en: An anatomical cluster of short rays, shorter than the principal ones, which form the anterior dorsal and ventral series of lepidotrichia of the caudal fin that may be associated with neural spines, epurals and uroneurals (dorsal series) and haemal spines of preural vertebrae (ventral series) (Arratia, 2008). The anteriormost procurrent rays are commonly unsegmented, but the posteriormost ones are usually segmented. The procurrent rays are numbered from caudal to rostral direction. The caudal procurrent ray series is an unpaired median series.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Subdivision of vertebral column that corresponds to the caudal subdivision of the body, containing the caudal vertebrae.
description_en: Subdivision of vertebral column that corresponds to the caudal subdivision of the body, containing the caudal vertebrae.

description_en: Subdivision of vertebral column that is posterior to the sacral region and anterior to the caudal region.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The caudofemoralis (from the latin cauda, tail and femur, thighbone) is a muscle found in the pelvic limb of mostly all animals possessing a tail, since it is a synapomorphy appeared on the Archosauria clade. It is thus found in felids (cats) and Mustela ('Weasels'), but also on crocodiles and birds.
description_en: The caudofemoralis (from the latin cauda, tail and femur, thighbone) is a muscle found in the pelvic limb of mostly all animals possessing a tail, since it is a synapomorphy appeared on the Archosauria clade. It is thus found in felids (cats) and Mustela ('Weasels'), but also on crocodiles and birds.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The cavernous sinus (or lateral sellar compartment), within the human head, is a large collection of thin-walled veins creating a cavity bordered by the temporal bone of the skull and the sphenoid bone, lateral to the sella turcica.
description_en: The cavernous sinus (or lateral sellar compartment), within the human head, is a large collection of thin-walled veins creating a cavity bordered by the temporal bone of the skull and the sphenoid bone, lateral to the sella turcica.

description_en: An organ cavity that surrounded_by a bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A complex network of nerves located in the abdomen behind the stomach. The celiac plexus is located near where the celiac trunk, superior mesenteric artery, and renal arteries branch from the abdominal aorta. It is behind the stomach and the omental bursa and in front of the crura of the diaphragm, on the level of the first lumbar vertebra, L1. The plexus is formed (in part) by the greater and lesser splanchnic nerves of both sides, and also parts of the right vagus nerve. The celiac plexus proper consists of the celiac ganglia with a network of interconnecting fibers. The aorticorenal ganglia are often considered to be part of the celiac ganglia, and thus, part of the plexus. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: A complex network of nerves located in the abdomen behind the stomach. The celiac plexus is located near where the celiac trunk, superior mesenteric artery, and renal arteries branch from the abdominal aorta. It is behind the stomach and the omental bursa and in front of the crura of the diaphragm, on the level of the first lumbar vertebra, L1. The plexus is formed (in part) by the greater and lesser splanchnic nerves of both sides, and also parts of the right vagus nerve. The celiac plexus proper consists of the celiac ganglia with a network of interconnecting fibers. The aorticorenal ganglia are often considered to be part of the celiac ganglia, and thus, part of the plexus. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Anatomical structure that is an aggregation of similar cells from which cartilages and bones form, and from which chondrogenesis and osteogenesis are initiated during repair and/or regeneration. (Hall and Miyake 1995).
description_en: Anatomical structure that is an aggregation of similar cells from which cartilages and bones form, and from which chondrogenesis and osteogenesis are initiated during repair and/or regeneration. (Hall and Miyake 1995).

description_en: Mineralized bone tissue that always includes non-terminally differentiated osteoblasts and osteocytes.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Odontoid tissue that is deposited by cementoblasts onto dentine tissue and functions to attach teeth, odontodes and other odontogenic derivatives to bone tissue and the integument.
description_en: Odontoid tissue that is deposited by cementoblasts onto dentine tissue and functions to attach teeth, odontodes and other odontogenic derivatives to bone tissue and the integument.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A small bone occasionally found at the dorsal aspect of the wrist between the scaphoid, capitate, and trapezoid; it is developed as an independent cartilage in early foetal life but usually becomes fused with the scaphoid; it occurs normally in most monkeys.
description_en: A small bone occasionally found at the dorsal aspect of the wrist between the scaphoid, capitate, and trapezoid; it is developed as an independent cartilage in early foetal life but usually becomes fused with the scaphoid; it occurs normally in most monkeys.
