definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The central nervous system is the core nervous system that serves an integrating and coordinating function. In vertebrates it consists of the neural tube derivatives: the brain and spinal cord. In invertebrates it includes central ganglia plus nerve cord.
description_en: The central nervous system is the core nervous system that serves an integrating and coordinating function. In vertebrates it consists of the neural tube derivatives: the brain and spinal cord. In invertebrates it includes central ganglia plus nerve cord.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The central sulcus is a fold in the cerebral cortex of brains in vertebrates. Also called the central fissure, it was originally called the fissure of Rolando or the Rolandic fissure, after Luigi Rolando. The central sulcus is a prominent landmark of the brain, separating the parietal lobe from the frontal lobe and the primary motor cortex from the primary somatosensory cortex. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: The central sulcus is a fold in the cerebral cortex of brains in vertebrates. Also called the central fissure, it was originally called the fissure of Rolando or the Rolandic fissure, after Luigi Rolando. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The flat bone at the center of the anterior chest wall, the sternum shields the heart and great vessels and anchors the costal cartilages of the upper seven ribs and the clavicles; its interior is a site of red bone marrow production. It is built from three parts: the manubrium above, the body in the middle, and the xiphoid process below. The jugular notch lies at the superior border of the manubrium, and the sternal angle, or angle of Louis, marks the junction of the manubrium and body at the level of the second rib. Direct trauma, such as a steering-wheel impact, can fracture it. Median sternotomy is the standard surgical approach to the heart, and sternal marrow aspiration and biopsy are common diagnostic procedures.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The chorioallantoic membrane is a vascular membrane found in eggs of some amniotes, such as birds and reptiles. It is formed by the fusion of the mesodermal layers of two developmental structures: the allantois and the chorion. Three different layers compose the chorioallantoic membrane; these are called the chorionic epithelium, the mesenchyme and the allantoic epithelium. Blood capillaries and sinuses are found between epithelial cells of the chorionic layer, allowing close contact (within 0.2 N<m) with air found in pores of the shell membrane of the egg. As a result, the chorioallantoic membrane allows exchange of gases, such as oxygen, to developing embryos. During embryonic development of birds, the chorioallantoic membrane also plays an essential role in bone formation by transporting calcium into the embryo from the eggshell. Chorioalloantoic membranes from developing chicken eggs are routinely used in biological and biomedical research to investigate development, angiogenesis, tumors, and to propagate and investigate viruses or helminths.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A chorionic villus that provides structural support to the villous tree. A chorionic stem villus is characterized by a condensed fibrous stroma in which fetal arteries, veins, arterioles, and venules are embedded. It represents a distributing framework for fetal chorionic circulation, supplying the floating villi. It can exhibit a diameter ranging from approximately 3000 μm (trunci near the chorionic plate) to 80 μm (smallest ramuli chorii).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Ciaccio's glands are small tubular accessory lacrimal glands (glandulae lacrimales accessoriae) found in the lacrimal caruncle of the eyelid. They are located in the upper border of the tarsus, approximately in the middle between the extremities of the tarsal glands. Sometimes they are situated slightly above the tarsus. There are usually 2 to 5 of these glands in the upper eyelid, and their function is to produce tears which are secreted onto the surface of the conjunctiva. They are named after Italian anatomist Giuseppe Vincenzo Ciaccio (1824b1901), who described these glands in 1874. They are sometimes called Wolfring's glands after Polish ophthalmologist Emilj von Wolfring (1832-1906), who described them during the same time period as did Ciaccio. Another type of accessory lacrimal gland are Krause's glands, which are smaller, more numerous than Ciaccio's glands and are found along the superior and inferior fornices of the conjunctival sac.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Slender and S-shaped, the clavicle forms the anterior part of the shoulder girdle, extending horizontally from the sternum to the acromion of the scapula. It acts as a strut that holds the upper limb away from the trunk, allowing free movement, and transmits forces from the limb to the axial skeleton. Its medial two-thirds are convex anteriorly and the lateral third concave. Developmentally, it is the first bone to ossify, by intramembranous ossification, yet the last to complete ossification. The clavicle is the most commonly fractured bone, usually at the junction of the middle and lateral thirds, where the break may injure the subclavian vessels or the brachial plexus. Sternoclavicular dislocations are uncommon but potentially dangerous.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The cleidomastoideus is a thick, strap-like muscle that together with the cleidocervicalis forms the proximal part of the brachiocephalicus. It lies beneath the cleidocervicalis. Its origin is the clavicular tendon with its insertion being at the mastoid process of the temporal bone. It is distinctly narrow and is united with the cleidocervicalis and cleidobrachialis by the clavicular tendon. Together with the other two components of the brachiocephalicus muscle, its primary function is to advance the free limb, however, it can also act as an shoulder extensor. Acting bilaterally, it fixes and depresses the neck, while by its unilateral action, it allows the head and neck to be drawn to the side. Its blood supply is the inferior cervical, carotid and vertebral arteries and its nerve supply is the spinal accessory, cervical and axillary nerves.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Part of the cranium, the clivus is a shallow depression behind the dorsum sellC& that slopes obliquely backward. It forms a gradual sloping process at the anterior most portion of the basilar occipital bone at its junction with the sphenoid bone. On axial planes, it sits just posterior to the sphenoid sinuses. Just lateral to the clivus bilaterally is the foramen lacerum which contains the internal carotid artery, proximal to its anastamosis with the Circle of Willis. Posterior to the clivus is the basilar artery. The clivus supports the upper part of the pons.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The vestigial tailbone, the coccyx forms from the fusion of three to five coccygeal vertebrae into a small triangular bone at the inferior end of the vertebral column. It provides attachment for ligaments and muscles of the pelvic floor and serves as a weight-bearing structure during sitting. Superiorly it articulates with the sacrum at the sacrococcygeal joint, and its coccygeal cornua project upward to meet the sacral cornua. Coccydynia, or tailbone pain, tends to follow falls or prolonged sitting on hard surfaces, and fractures and dislocations of the bone can occur during childbirth. On rare occasions, pilonidal cysts develop in the sacrococcygeal region overlying it.

Its core component is the Organ of Corti, the sensory organ of hearing, which is distributed along the partition separating fluid chambers in the coiled tapered tube of the cochlea. [WP,modified].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A nerve in the head that carries signals from the cochlea of the inner ear to the brain. It is part of the vestibulocochlear nerve, the 8th cranial nerve which is found in higher vertebrates; the other portion of the 8th cranial nerve is the vestibular nerve which carries spatial orientation information from the semicircular canals. The cochlear nerve is a sensory nerve, one which conducts to the brain information about the environment, in this case acoustic energy impinging on the tympanic membrane. The cochlear nerve arises from within the cochlea and extends to the brainstem, where its fibers make contact with the cochlear nucleus, the next stage of neural processing in the auditory system[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The common iliac arteries are two large arteries, about 4cm long in adults but more than a centimetre in diameter, that originate from the aortic bifurcation. The arteries run inferolaterally, along the medial border of the psoas muscles to the pelvic brim, where they bifurcate into the external iliac artery and internal iliac artery. The common iliac artery, and all of its branches, exist as paired structures (that is to say, there is one on the left side and one on the right). The distribution of the common iliac artery is basically the pelvis and lower limb on the corresponding side. Both common iliac arteries are accompanied along their course by common iliac veins. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The conus medullaris is the terminal end of the spinal cord. It occurs near lumbar vertebral levels 1 (L1) and 2 (L2). After the spinal cord tapers out, the spinal nerves continue as dangling nerve roots called cauda equina. This terminal nerve root tail is referred to as the filum terminale. The upper end of the conus medullaris is usually not well defined.

They consist of between 1 and 4 nerve cells with axons, each with 2 cilia, surrounded by up to 7 sheath cells. The cilia extend into a protrusion of the basal lamina which surrounds each corpuscle. The axonal process contributes to the rostral nerve.

The axonal process contributes to the rostral nerve.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Islands of eosinic cells found on the lateroventral surface of the kidney. Function is thought to be that of the parathyroid gland in other vertebrates, which are lacking in fishes. These cells secrete hypocalcin (teleocalcin) to regulate calcium metabolism.
description_en: Islands of eosinic cells found on the lateroventral surface of the kidney. Function is thought to be that of the parathyroid gland in other vertebrates, which are lacking in fishes. These cells secrete hypocalcin (teleocalcin) to regulate calcium metabolism.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The outer or sperficial part of a bone of the manus.
description_en: The outer or sperficial part of a bone of the manus.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Multi-tissue integumentary element composed of enamel or enameloid, dentine and lamellar bone, and characterized by pore-canal system.
description_en: Multi-tissue integumentary element composed of enamel or enameloid, dentine and lamellar bone, and characterized by pore-canal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The costal margin, sometimes referred to as the costal arch, is the medial margin formed by the false ribs, which in humans is from the eighth rib to the tenth rib.
description_en: The costal margin, sometimes referred to as the costal arch, is the medial margin formed by the false ribs, which in humans is from the eighth rib to the tenth rib.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The nonvascular, resilient, flexible hyaline connective tissue that connects the end of a true rib to the sternum or the end of a false rib with the with the lower border of the costal cartilage above it.
description_en: The nonvascular, resilient, flexible hyaline connective tissue that connects the end of a true rib to the sternum or the end of a false rib with the with the lower border of the costal cartilage above it.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The domain of the diaphragm that is a thin domed sheet of muscle composed of a radial array of myofibers extending laterally from the ribs and medially to a central tendon.
description_en: The domain of the diaphragm that is a thin domed sheet of muscle composed of a radial array of myofibers extending laterally from the ribs and medially to a central tendon.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Costocervical trunk: subclavian branch dividing into the deep cervical and supreme intercostal arteries behind the first two rib necks.
description_en: Costocervical trunk: subclavian branch dividing into the deep cervical and supreme intercostal arteries behind the first two rib necks.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bars of hyaline cartilage located between the distal part of a rib and a costal cartilage, connecting the ribs to the sternum .
description_en: A bars of hyaline cartilage located between the distal part of a rib and a costal cartilage, connecting the ribs to the sternum .

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Costotransverse joint: plane synovial articulation of rib tubercle with thoracic transverse process, keeping ribs parallel in breathing.
description_en: Costotransverse joint: plane synovial articulation of rib tubercle with thoracic transverse process, keeping ribs parallel in breathing.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The costovertebral joints are the articulations that connect the heads of the ribs with the bodies of the thoracic vertebrae. Joining of ribs to the vertebrae occurs at two places, the head and the tubercle of the rib. Two convex facets from the head attach to two adjacent vertebrae. This forms a trochoid joint, which is strengthened by the ligament of the head and the intercapital ligament. Articulation of the tubercle is to the transverse process of the adjacent vertebrae. This articulation is reinforced by the dorsal costotransverse ligament. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: The costovertebral joints are the articulations that connect the heads of the ribs with the bodies of the thoracic vertebrae. Joining of ribs to the vertebrae occurs at two places, the head and the tubercle of the rib. Two convex facets from the head attach to two adjacent vertebrae. This forms a trochoid joint, which is strengthened by the ligament of the head and the intercapital ligament. Articulation of the tubercle is to the transverse process of the adjacent vertebrae. This articulation is reinforced by the dorsal costotransverse ligament. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A cup shaped articular surface on a bone.
description_en: A cup shaped articular surface on a bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bone that is part of a cranium.
description_en: A bone that is part of a cranium.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Neural crest cells (NCCs) originating in the anterior part of the developing embryo and residing between the mid-diencephalon and the forming hindbrain; cranial NCCs migrate dorsolaterally to form the craniofacial mesenchyme that differentiates into various craniofacial cartilages and bones, cranial neurons, glia, and connective tissues of the face; these cells enter the pharyngeal pouches and arches where they give rise to thymic cells, bones of the middle ear and jaw (mandible), and the odontoblasts of the tooth primordia; like their counterparts in the trunk, cranial NCCs also contribute to the developing peripheral nervous system, along with the pigmented cell (i.e. melanocyte) lineage.
description_en: Neural crest cells (NCCs) originating in the anterior part of the developing embryo and residing between the mid-diencephalon and the forming hindbrain; cranial NCCs migrate dorsolaterally to form the craniofacial mesenchyme that differentiates into various craniofacial cartilages and bones, cranial neurons, glia, and connective tissues of the face; these cells enter the pharyngeal pouches and arches where they give rise to thymic cells, bones of the middle ear and jaw (mandible), and the odontoblasts of the tooth primordia; like their counterparts in the trunk, cranial NCCs also contribute to the developing peripheral nervous system, along with the pigmented cell (i.e. melanocyte) lineage.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Fibrous joint in which the articulating bones or cartilages of the skull are connected by sutural ligaments (scant amount of collagenous dense connective tissue). Examples: sagittal suture, frontal suture.
description_en: Fibrous joint in which the articulating bones or cartilages of the skull are connected by sutural ligaments (scant amount of collagenous dense connective tissue). Examples: sagittal suture, frontal suture.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A ridge or similar projection connected to the temporal lines and nuchal crest on the squamous part of the occipital bone. It bounds the posteroventral part of the temporal fossa.
description_en: A ridge or similar projection connected to the temporal lines and nuchal crest on the squamous part of the occipital bone. It bounds the posteroventral part of the temporal fossa.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The anteriormost subdivision of the body that includes the head, jaws, pharyngeal region and the neck (if present). In vertebrates this is the subdivision that includes the cervical vertebrae.
description_en: The anteriormost subdivision of the body that includes the head, jaws, pharyngeal region and the neck (if present). In vertebrates this is the subdivision that includes the cervical vertebrae.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Any suture between cranial and/or facial bones.
description_en: Any suture between cranial and/or facial bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The craniopharyngeal canal, is an anatomical feature sometimes found in the sphenoid bone opening to the sella turcica. It is a canal (a passage or channel) sometimes found extending from the anterior part of the fossa hypophyseos of the sphenoid bone to the under surface of the skull, and marks the original position of Rathke's pouch; while at the junction of the septum of the nose with the palate traces of the stomodeal end are occasionally present.
description_en: The craniopharyngeal canal, is an anatomical feature sometimes found in the sphenoid bone opening to the sella turcica. It is a canal (a passage or channel) sometimes found extending from the anterior part of the fossa hypophyseos of the sphenoid bone to the under surface of the skull, and marks the original position of Rathke's pouch; while at the junction of the septum of the nose with the palate traces of the stomodeal end are occasionally present.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A zone of the ethmoid that is received into the ethmoidal notch of the frontal bone and roofs in the nasal cavities. [WP,modified].
description_en: A zone of the ethmoid that is received into the ethmoidal notch of the frontal bone and roofs in the nasal cavities. [WP,modified].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Ridge on the dorsal surface of the vomer that runs from the anterior to the postchoanal processes of the vomer; it takes part in the fixation of the bone to the lateral margin of the solum nasi.
description_en: Ridge on the dorsal surface of the vomer that runs from the anterior to the postchoanal processes of the vomer; it takes part in the fixation of the bone to the lateral margin of the solum nasi.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The crotaphion refers to two points on the skull at the tips of the greater wing of sphenoid bone. It is near the pterion.
description_en: The crotaphion refers to two points on the skull at the tips of the greater wing of sphenoid bone. It is near the pterion.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A joint that connects the bones of the crus to the proximal tarsal bones.
description_en: A joint that connects the bones of the crus to the proximal tarsal bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The domain of the diaphragm that is located dorsally and attaches to the vertebrae and surrounds the esophagus and aorta.
description_en: The domain of the diaphragm that is located dorsally and attaches to the vertebrae and surrounds the esophagus and aorta.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Crypts of Henle are microscopic pockets found in scattered sections of the conjunctiva around the eyeball. They are responsible for secreting mucin, a proteinous substance that makes up the inner layer of tears. It coats the cornea to provide a hydrophilic layer that allows for even distribution of the tear film. The layer of mucin allows tears to glide evenly across the eye's surface[WP].
description_en: Crypts of Henle are microscopic pockets found in scattered sections of the conjunctiva around the eyeball. They are responsible for secreting mucin, a proteinous substance that makes up the inner layer of tears. It coats the cornea to provide a hydrophilic layer that allows for even distribution of the tear film. The layer of mucin allows tears to glide evenly across the eye's surface[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A tarsal bone that is formed from distal tarsals 4 and 5. [WP,modified].
description_en: A tarsal bone that is formed from distal tarsals 4 and 5. [WP,modified].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Facet on the anterior surface of the calcaneus (as called calcaneum) for the articulation of the cuboid bone.
description_en: Facet on the anterior surface of the calcaneus (as called calcaneum) for the articulation of the cuboid bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Scale that is smooth-edged, round or oval and composed of acellular dermal bone lacking small spines on the posterior exposed edge. (from http://www.briancoad.com/Dictionary/introduction.htm).
description_en: Scale that is smooth-edged, round or oval and composed of acellular dermal bone lacking small spines on the posterior exposed edge. (from http://www.briancoad.com/Dictionary/introduction.htm).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The deep artery of the penis (artery to the corpus cavernosum), one of the terminal branches of the internal pudendal, arises from that vessel while it is situated between the two fascia of the urogenital diaphragm (deep perineal pouch). It pierces the inferior fascia, and, entering the crus penis obliquely, runs forward in the center of the corpus cavernosum penis, to which its branches are distributed.
description_en: The deep artery of the penis (artery to the corpus cavernosum), one of the terminal branches of the internal pudendal, arises from that vessel while it is situated between the two fascia of the urogenital diaphragm (deep perineal pouch). It pierces the inferior fascia, and, entering the crus penis obliquely, runs forward in the center of the corpus cavernosum penis, to which its branches are distributed.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The deep cervical fascia (or fascia colli in older texts) lies under cover of the Platysma, and invests the neck; it also forms sheaths for the carotid vessels, and for the structures situated in front of the vertebral column. Its attachment to the hyoid bone prevents the formation of a dewlap. The investing portion of the fascia is attached behind to the ligamentum nucha and to the spinous process of the seventh cervical vertebra. The 'alar fascia' is a portion of deep cervical fascia.
description_en: The deep cervical fascia (or fascia colli in older texts) lies under cover of the Platysma, and invests the neck; it also forms sheaths for the carotid vessels, and for the structures situated in front of the vertebral column. Its attachment to the hyoid bone prevents the formation of a dewlap. The investing portion of the fascia is attached behind to the ligamentum nucha and to the spinous process of the seventh cervical vertebra. The 'alar fascia' is a portion of deep cervical fascia.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein that is tributary of a vertebral vein and drains the suboccipital region, adjacent vertebral column, and deep muscles of the neck.
description_en: A vein that is tributary of a vertebral vein and drains the suboccipital region, adjacent vertebral column, and deep muscles of the neck.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The deep circumflex iliac artery (or deep iliac circumflex artery) is an artery in the pelvis that travels along the iliac crest of the pelvic bone.
description_en: The deep circumflex iliac artery (or deep iliac circumflex artery) is an artery in the pelvis that travels along the iliac crest of the pelvic bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): arteria pudenda externa profunda
description_en: arteria pudenda externa profunda

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Deep fascia (or 'investing fascia') is a layer of fascia which can surround individual muscles, and divide groups of muscles into compartments. This is the dense fibrous connective tissue that interpenetrates and surrounds the muscles, bones, nerves and blood vessels of the body. It provides connection and communication in the form of aponeuroses, ligaments, tendons, retinacula, joint capsules, and septa. The deep fasciae envelop all bone; cartilage, and blood vessels and become specialized in muscles and nerves. The high density of collagen fibers is what gives the deep fascia its strength and integrity. The amount of elastin fiber determines how much extensibility and resilience it will have.
description_en: Deep fascia (or 'investing fascia') is a layer of fascia which can surround individual muscles, and divide groups of muscles into compartments. This is the dense fibrous connective tissue that interpenetrates and surrounds the muscles, bones, nerves and blood vessels of the body. It provides connection and communication in the form of aponeuroses, ligaments, tendons, retinacula, joint capsules, and septa. The deep fasciae envelop all bone; cartilage, and blood vessels and become specialized in muscles and nerves. The high density of collagen fibers is what gives the deep fascia its strength and integrity. The amount of elastin fiber determines how much extensibility and resilience it will have.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein that is tributary of the lingual vein and drains blood from the tongue.
description_en: A vein that is tributary of the lingual vein and drains blood from the tongue.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): anterior deep temporal artery
description_en: anterior deep temporal artery

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dense connective tissue is mainly composed of collagen type I. Crowded between the collagen fibers are rows of fibroblasts, fiber-forming cells, that manufacture the fibers. Dense connective tissue forms strong, rope-like structures such as tendons and ligaments. Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones; ligaments connect bones to bones at joints. Ligaments are more stretchy and contain more elastic fibers than tendons. Dense connective tissue also make up the lower layers of the skin (dermis), where it is arranged in sheets.
description_en: Dense connective tissue is mainly composed of collagen type I. Crowded between the collagen fibers are rows of fibroblasts, fiber-forming cells, that manufacture the fibers. Dense connective tissue forms strong, rope-like structures such as tendons and ligaments. Tendons attach skeletal muscles to bones; ligaments connect bones to bones at joints. Ligaments are more stretchy and contain more elastic fibers than tendons. Dense connective tissue also make up the lower layers of the skin (dermis), where it is arranged in sheets.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A sac containing the developing tooth and its odontogenic organ. The dental follicle (DF) differentiates into the periodontal ligament. In addition, it may be the precursor of other cells of the periodontium, including osteoblasts, cementoblasts and fibroblasts. They develop into the alveolar bone, the cementum with Sharpey's fibers and the periodontal ligament fibers respectively.
description_en: A sac containing the developing tooth and its odontogenic organ. The dental follicle (DF) differentiates into the periodontal ligament. In addition, it may be the precursor of other cells of the periodontium, including osteoblasts, cementoblasts and fibroblasts. They develop into the alveolar bone, the cementum with Sharpey's fibers and the periodontal ligament fibers respectively.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The dentary is a dermal bone that forms the antero-lateral part of the lower jaw in fishes and amphibians, extending to the whole lower jaw in mammals[VHOG,modified].
description_en: The dentary is a dermal bone that forms the antero-lateral part of the lower jaw in fishes and amphibians, extending to the whole lower jaw in mammals[VHOG,modified].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Skeletal element that forms superficially in the organism, usually in association with the ectoderm[VSAO].
description_en: Skeletal element that forms superficially in the organism, usually in association with the ectoderm[VSAO].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that is thin, flexible, and platelike, and that develops in overlapping skinfolds that cover the body and often the head of fish and the bases of the fins.
description_en: Dermal bone that is thin, flexible, and platelike, and that develops in overlapping skinfolds that cover the body and often the head of fish and the bases of the fins.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Subdivision of skeleton that includes all dermal bones in the cranial skeleton[ZFA,modified].
description_en: Subdivision of skeleton that includes all dermal bones in the cranial skeleton[ZFA,modified].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone of the dorsal surface of the olfactory region. Dermethmoid can be paired or median.
description_en: Dermal bone of the dorsal surface of the olfactory region. Dermethmoid can be paired or median.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Infraorbital that is the last bone of the infraorbital series, carrying the infraorbital canal, and sometimes also the supraorbital, temporal, and/or preopercular canals. The dermosphenotic is sometimes sutured or fused completely to the skull, e.g. to the autosphenotic.
description_en: Infraorbital that is the last bone of the infraorbital series, carrying the infraorbital canal, and sometimes also the supraorbital, temporal, and/or preopercular canals. The dermosphenotic is sometimes sutured or fused completely to the skull, e.g. to the autosphenotic.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The diaphragma sellae or sellar diaphragm is the circular fold of dura mater that almost completely roofs the fossa hypophyseos in the sphenoid bone of the skull. It retains the pituitary gland in the fossa hypophyseos, with only the infundibulum of the pituitary gland passing through it.
description_en: The diaphragma sellae or sellar diaphragm is the circular fold of dura mater that almost completely roofs the fossa hypophyseos in the sphenoid bone of the skull. It retains the pituitary gland in the fossa hypophyseos, with only the infundibulum of the pituitary gland passing through it.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Subdivision of long bone which forms the part of the bone between the two epiphyses, excluding the metaphyses[FMA,modified].
description_en: Subdivision of long bone which forms the part of the bone between the two epiphyses, excluding the metaphyses[FMA,modified].

description_en: A diaphysis that is part of a metacarpal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Subdivision of long bone which forms the part of the bone between two metaphyses. Note that the diaphysis includes the metaphyses, but the diaphysis proper excludes these.
description_en: Subdivision of long bone which forms the part of the bone between two metaphyses. Note that the diaphysis includes the metaphyses, but the diaphysis proper excludes these.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Paired processes that arise near the midpoint of the neural arch lamina, for the attachment of the tuberculum of two-headed ribs. Also called transverse processes. In anurans, the term diapophysis is used in reference to the modified transverse processes of the sacral vertebra elaborated for support of the pelvic girdle.
description_en: Paired processes that arise near the midpoint of the neural arch lamina, for the attachment of the tuberculum of two-headed ribs. Also called transverse processes. In anurans, the term diapophysis is used in reference to the modified transverse processes of the sacral vertebra elaborated for support of the pelvic girdle.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A neural crest that has_potential_to_developmentally_contribute_to a diencephalon.
description_en: A neural crest that has_potential_to_developmentally_contribute_to a diencephalon.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A placenta in which the chorionic sac meets the uterine endometrium over its entire surface. The villi of the chorion are distributed evenly throughout the surface of the chorion, and they extend into processes in the uterine endometrium.
description_en: A placenta in which the chorionic sac meets the uterine endometrium over its entire surface. The villi of the chorion are distributed evenly throughout the surface of the chorion, and they extend into processes in the uterine endometrium.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bone that is part of a the digitopodium skeleton - i.e. the acropodial skeleton or the metapodial skeleton.
description_en: A bone that is part of a the digitopodium skeleton - i.e. the acropodial skeleton or the metapodial skeleton.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Fossa located on the neurocranium that is formed from portions of the sphenotic, frontal and pterotic bones.
description_en: Fossa located on the neurocranium that is formed from portions of the sphenotic, frontal and pterotic bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Vertebral column in which the first seven vertebrae have holochordal centra and the intervertebral cartilages are posteriorly subdivided in the procoelous manner. The eighth presacral vertebra has a holochordal centrum and the intervertebral cartilage is subdivided in the opisthocoelous manner. Thus, the first seven presacral vertebrae are concave anteriorly and convex posteriorly, whereas the eighth is biconcave.
description_en: Vertebral column in which the first seven vertebrae have holochordal centra and the intervertebral cartilages are posteriorly subdivided in the procoelous manner. The eighth presacral vertebra has a holochordal centrum and the intervertebral cartilage is subdivided in the opisthocoelous manner. Thus, the first seven presacral vertebrae are concave anteriorly and convex posteriorly, whereas the eighth is biconcave.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A distal phalanx that is part of a digit 3. In odd-toes ungulates (Perissodactyla e.g. horses) this is called the coffin bone. In even-toed ungulates (Artiodactyla e.g cattle) this is associated with the medial claw.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A segment of a digit containing the distal phalanx, and overlapping the distal interphalangeal joint[CJM]. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Sense organ in vertebrates that is specialized for the detection of sound, and the maintenance of balance. Includes the outer ear and middle ear, which collect and transmit sound waves; and the inner ear, which contains the organs of balance and (except in fish) hearing. Also includes the pinna, the visible part of the outer ear, present in some mammals.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A palatal bone which -- like many palatal bones -- may originally have developed as a dermal bone replacing part of the palatoquadrate, the primitive upper jaw. Like the palatine (also called dermopalatine), the ectopterygoid replaces the middle part of the autopalatine. It may be serially homologous with the palatine(s), but is somewhat specialized, being the last (most posterior in palatal view) of the series and bordering the fossa for the jaw muscles. In a typical tetrapod it abuts the palatine anteriorly, the maxilla laterally, the pterygoid or the fossa mandubuaris medially, and the fossa posteriorly.
description_en: A palatal bone which -- like many palatal bones -- may originally have developed as a dermal bone replacing part of the palatoquadrate, the primitive upper jaw. Like the palatine (also called dermopalatine), the ectopterygoid replaces the middle part of the autopalatine. It may be serially homologous with the palatine(s), but is somewhat specialized, being the last (most posterior in palatal view) of the series and bordering the fossa for the jaw muscles. In a typical tetrapod it abuts the palatine anteriorly, the maxilla laterally, the pterygoid or the fossa mandubuaris medially, and the fossa posteriorly.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The elbow is the region surrounding the elbow-joint-the ginglymus or hinge joint in the middle of the arm. Three bones form the elbow joint: the humerus of the upper arm, and the paired radius and ulna of the forearm. The bony prominence at the very tip of the elbow is the olecranon process of the ulna, and the inner aspect of the elbow is called the antecubital fossa. [WP,unvetted,human-specific].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): From the posterior wall of the saccule a canal, the ductus endolymphaticus, is given off; this duct is joined by the ductus utriculosaccularis, and then passes along the aquaeductus vestibuli and ends in a blind pouch, the endolymphatic sac, on the posterior surface of the petrous portion of the temporal bone, where it is in contact with the dura mater. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An endostyle is a longitudinal ciliated groove on the ventral wall of the pharynx which produces mucus to gather food particles. It is found in urochordates and cephalochordates, and in the larvae of lampreys. It aids in transporting food to the esophagus. It is also called the hypopharyngeal groove. The endostyle in larval lampreys (ammocetes) metamorphoses into the thyroid gland in adults, and is regarded as being homologous to the thyroid gland in vertebrates. However, Dumont, et al. question whether the endostyle in ammocetes is homologous with that of the urochordates and cephalochordates. Since the endostyle is found in the three branches of chordates, it is presumed to have arisen in the common ancestor of these taxa, along with a shift to internal feeding for extracting suspended food from the water.
description_en: An endostyle is a longitudinal ciliated groove on the ventral wall of the pharynx which produces mucus to gather food particles. It is found in urochordates and cephalochordates, and in the larvae of lampreys. It aids in transporting food to the esophagus. It is also called the hypopharyngeal groove. The endostyle in larval lampreys (ammocetes) metamorphoses into the thyroid gland in adults, and is regarded as being homologous to the thyroid gland in vertebrates. However, Dumont, et al. question whether the endostyle in ammocetes is homologous with that of the urochordates and cephalochordates. Since the endostyle is found in the three branches of chordates, it is presumed to have arisen in the common ancestor of these taxa, along with a shift to internal feeding for extracting suspended food from the water.

description_en: Epibranchial cartilage that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial 3 cartilage or bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Joint that articulates the epibranchial 3 cartilage or bone and pharyngobranchial 3 cartilage or bone. Epibranchial 3-pharyngobranchial 3 joint is paired.
description_en: Joint that articulates the epibranchial 3 cartilage or bone and pharyngobranchial 3 cartilage or bone. Epibranchial 3-pharyngobranchial 3 joint is paired.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Joint that articulates the epibranchial 3 cartilage or bone and pharyngobranchial 4 cartilage or bone. Epibranchial 3-pharyngobranchial 4 joint is paired.
description_en: Joint that articulates the epibranchial 3 cartilage or bone and pharyngobranchial 4 cartilage or bone. Epibranchial 3-pharyngobranchial 4 joint is paired.

description_en: Epibranchial bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial 4 cartilage or bone and medially with pharyngobranchial cartilage or bone.

description_en: Epibranchial uncinate process that is part of epibranchial 4 bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Pharyngeal cartilage that is part of and at the distal end of epibranchial bone 4 uncinate process. Epibranchial bone 4 uncinate process cartilage is paired.
description_en: Pharyngeal cartilage that is part of and at the distal end of epibranchial bone 4 uncinate process. Epibranchial bone 4 uncinate process cartilage is paired.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Epibranchial cartilage that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial 4 cartilage or bone.
description_en: Epibranchial cartilage that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial 4 cartilage or bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Joint that articulates the epibranchial 4 cartilage or bone and upper pharyngeal toothplate. Epibranchial 4-upper pharyngeal toothplate joint is paired.
description_en: Joint that articulates the epibranchial 4 cartilage or bone and upper pharyngeal toothplate. Epibranchial 4-upper pharyngeal toothplate joint is paired.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Epibranchial cartilage that is bilaterally paired and located at the articulation of epibranchial 4 cartilage or bone and the posterior tip of ceratobranchial 4 cartilage or bone.
description_en: Epibranchial cartilage that is bilaterally paired and located at the articulation of epibranchial 4 cartilage or bone and the posterior tip of ceratobranchial 4 cartilage or bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dorsal branchial arch bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial cartilage or bone and medially with pharyngobranchial cartilage or bone.
description_en: Dorsal branchial arch bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial cartilage or bone and medially with pharyngobranchial cartilage or bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Epibranchials 1-3 in adults are compound elements formed by the fusion of epibranchial cartilages and the so-called uncinate processes. Posteromedially directed uncinate processes develop on the posterior edge of epibranchials 1-3. These appear as separate centers of chondrification (6.2 mm) that later fuse laterally to the posterior edges of the epibranchial cartilages (6.8 mm).
description_en: Epibranchials 1-3 in adults are compound elements formed by the fusion of epibranchial cartilages and the so-called uncinate processes. Posteromedially directed uncinate processes develop on the posterior edge of epibranchials 1-3. These appear as separate centers of chondrification (6.2 mm) that later fuse laterally to the posterior edges of the epibranchial cartilages (6.8 mm).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Pharyngeal arch cartilage that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial cartilage or bone.
description_en: Pharyngeal arch cartilage that is bilaterally paired and articulates laterally with ceratobranchial cartilage or bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Intermuscular bone that articulates with the vertebral centrum.
description_en: Intermuscular bone that articulates with the vertebral centrum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Vertebral centrum that originates from ossification of the dorsal portion of the perichordal tube; the resulting element tends to be depressed in cross section.
description_en: Vertebral centrum that originates from ossification of the dorsal portion of the perichordal tube; the resulting element tends to be depressed in cross section.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Radial found above the vertebral column.
description_en: Radial found above the vertebral column.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Paired, flat cartilaginous arches that compose the central portion of the zonal area, unites the clavicle and coracoid of each half of the pectoral girdle, and form the medial margins of the pectoral fenestrae.
description_en: Paired, flat cartilaginous arches that compose the central portion of the zonal area, unites the clavicle and coracoid of each half of the pectoral girdle, and form the medial margins of the pectoral fenestrae.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A pair of cartilaginous expansions (one from each epicoracoid cartilage) that project anteriorly. They articulate anteriorly with the omosternum.
description_en: A pair of cartilaginous expansions (one from each epicoracoid cartilage) that project anteriorly. They articulate anteriorly with the omosternum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A pair of cartilaginous expansions (one from each epicoracoid cartilage) that project posteriorly. They articulate with the sternum by means of grooves, pouches or fossae in the dorsal surface of the sternum and provide a site for the insertion of a pair of muscles derived from the m. rectus abdominis.
description_en: A pair of cartilaginous expansions (one from each epicoracoid cartilage) that project posteriorly. They articulate with the sternum by means of grooves, pouches or fossae in the dorsal surface of the sternum and provide a site for the insertion of a pair of muscles derived from the m. rectus abdominis.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The galea aponeurotica (epicranial aponeurosis, aponeurosis epicranialis) is a tough layer of dense fibrous tissue which covers the upper part of the cranium; behind, it is attached, in the interval between its union with the Occipitales, to the external occipital protuberance and highest nuchal lines of the occipital bone; in front, it forms a short and narrow prolongation between its union with the Frontales. On either side it gives origin to the Auriculares anterior and superior; in this situation it loses its aponeurotic character, and is continued over the temporal fascia to the zygomatic arch as a layer of laminated areolar tissue. It is closely connected to the integument by the firm, dense, fibro-fatty layer which forms the superficial fascia of the scalp: it is attached to the pericranium by loose cellular tissue, which allows the aponeurosis, carrying with it the integument to move through a considerable distance.
description_en: The galea aponeurotica (epicranial aponeurosis, aponeurosis epicranialis) is a tough layer of dense fibrous tissue which covers the upper part of the cranium; behind, it is attached, in the interval between its union with the Occipitales, to the external occipital protuberance and highest nuchal lines of the occipital bone; in front, it forms a short and narrow prolongation between its union with the Frontales. On either side it gives origin to the Auriculares anterior and superior; in this situation it loses its aponeurotic character, and is continued over the temporal fascia to the zygomatic arch as a layer of laminated areolar tissue. It is closely connected to the integument by the firm, dense, fibro-fatty layer which forms the superficial fascia of the scalp: it is attached to the pericranium by loose cellular tissue, which allows the aponeurosis, carrying with it the integument to move through a considerable distance.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The outermost part of the spinal canal. It is the space within the canal (formed by the surrounding vertebrae) lying outside the dura mater.
description_en: The outermost part of the spinal canal. It is the space within the canal (formed by the surrounding vertebrae) lying outside the dura mater.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Joint that articulates the epihyal and branchiostegal ray bones. Epihyal-branchiostegal ray joint is paired.
description_en: Joint that articulates the epihyal and branchiostegal ray bones. Epihyal-branchiostegal ray joint is paired.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Joint that articulates the epihyal and ceratohyal bones. Epihyal-ceratohyal joint is paired.
description_en: Joint that articulates the epihyal and ceratohyal bones. Epihyal-ceratohyal joint is paired.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Some or all epineural bones ossify free from the neural arches in most teleosts. In some lower teleosts, e.g., Leptolepis, Hiodon, elopiforms and albuliforms, ossification proceeds from the attachment point of the ligament to the arch, and the epineural is a process of the neural arch. In many lower teleosts epineurals are forked proximally.
description_en: Some or all epineural bones ossify free from the neural arches in most teleosts. In some lower teleosts, e.g., Leptolepis, Hiodon, elopiforms and albuliforms, ossification proceeds from the attachment point of the ligament to the arch, and the epineural is a process of the neural arch. In many lower teleosts epineurals are forked proximally.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Endochondral bone that borders that medial edge of the posttemporal fossa. The epiotics are sutured to parietals and supraoccipital dorsally, the exoccipitals ventrally and the pterotics laterally. The epiotic is a paired bone.
description_en: Endochondral bone that borders that medial edge of the posttemporal fossa. The epiotics are sutured to parietals and supraoccipital dorsally, the exoccipitals ventrally and the pterotics laterally. The epiotic is a paired bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at each end of a long bone. The plate is found in children and adolescents; in adults, who have stopped growing, the plate is replaced by an epiphyseal line.
description_en: A hyaline cartilage plate in the metaphysis at each end of a long bone. The plate is found in children and adolescents; in adults, who have stopped growing, the plate is replaced by an epiphyseal line.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An epiphyseal plate that is part of a radius bone.
description_en: An epiphyseal plate that is part of a radius bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The head of a long bone that articulates with a neighboring skeletal element and is separated from the shaft by the epiphyseal plate until bone growth stops. At that time, the plate disappears and the head and shaft are united[MESH,modified].
description_en: The head of a long bone that articulates with a neighboring skeletal element and is separated from the shaft by the epiphyseal plate until bone growth stops. At that time, the plate disappears and the head and shaft are united[MESH,modified].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Epipleurals lie below the horizontal septum and are posteroventrally directed. There are ossified epipleurals in certain ostariophysans. In many lower elopocephalan teleosts including ostariophysans the epipleural bones develop an anterodorsal branch so that they are forked proximally.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): One of a pair of bones running antero-laterally from the centre of the pubis in marsupials and some other mammals.
description_en: One of a pair of bones running antero-laterally from the centre of the pubis in marsupials and some other mammals.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Most dorsal part of the thalamus, comprising the pineal gland and habenular nuclei in most vertebrates. In a few vertebrates, it also includes the parietal eye. (Butler and Hodos, Comparative Vertebrate Neuroanatomy, 2nd ed, 2005, pg. 345-346.
description_en: Most dorsal part of the thalamus, comprising the pineal gland and habenular nuclei in most vertebrates. In a few vertebrates, it also includes the parietal eye. (Butler and Hodos, Comparative Vertebrate Neuroanatomy, 2nd ed, 2005, pg. 345-346.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A free, modified neural spine of a preural or a ural vertebra that is placed between the last developed neural spine of a preural centrum and the dorsal axis (= anterior margin of first uroneural) of the caudal skeleton . An epural commonly supports one or more dorsal procurrent rays. An epural is an unpaired median perichondrally ossified bone.
description_en: A free, modified neural spine of a preural or a ural vertebra that is placed between the last developed neural spine of a preural centrum and the dorsal axis (= anterior margin of first uroneural) of the caudal skeleton . An epural commonly supports one or more dorsal procurrent rays. An epural is an unpaired median perichondrally ossified bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Lies on the palmar aspect of the coffin joint between the second phalanx and third phalanx. articulates closely with the distal phalanx, to which it is connected by the impar ligament of the navicular bone. The impar ligament is very strong and permits relatively little motion between the navicular bone and the distal phalanx.
description_en: Lies on the palmar aspect of the coffin joint between the second phalanx and third phalanx. articulates closely with the distal phalanx, to which it is connected by the impar ligament of the navicular bone. The impar ligament is very strong and permits relatively little motion between the navicular bone and the distal phalanx.

description_en: A splint bone in the metacarpal region.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A splint bone in the metatarsal region.
description_en: A splint bone in the metatarsal region.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The splint bones sit either side of the equine cannon bone. Homologous to metapodium bones 2 or 4.
description_en: The splint bones sit either side of the equine cannon bone. Homologous to metapodium bones 2 or 4.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bundle of muscles and tendons that is paired and runs more or less vertically. It extends throughout the lumbar, thoracic and cervical regions, and lies in the groove to the side of the vertebral column.
description_en: A bundle of muscles and tendons that is paired and runs more or less vertically. It extends throughout the lumbar, thoracic and cervical regions, and lies in the groove to the side of the vertebral column.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein that is tributary of the azygos vein and drains blood from the esophagus.
description_en: A vein that is tributary of the azygos vein and drains blood from the esophagus.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bone in the skull that separates the nasal cavity from the brain. As such, it is located at the roof of the nose, between the two orbits. The cubical bone is lightweight due to a spongy construction. The ethmoid bone is one of the bones that makes up the orbit of the eye[WP].
description_en: A bone in the skull that separates the nasal cavity from the brain. As such, it is located at the roof of the nose, between the two orbits. The cubical bone is lightweight due to a spongy construction. The ethmoid bone is one of the bones that makes up the orbit of the eye[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony element (ethmoid bone primordium) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.
description_en: A bony element (ethmoid bone primordium) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Sensory canal that traverses the rostral bone.
description_en: Sensory canal that traverses the rostral bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An bone foramen in the ethmoid bone.
description_en: An bone foramen in the ethmoid bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A suture between the orbital surface of the body of the maxilla with the orbital plate of the ethmoid bone.
description_en: A suture between the orbital surface of the body of the maxilla with the orbital plate of the ethmoid bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The ethmo-palatine cartilage (EPC) is a distinct body situated between the posterior surface of the upper arm of the premaxilla and the anterior margin of the palatine. There is usually only a single cartilage mass lying between these bones, although that cartilage is apparently subdivided into two units in some taxa (e.g., the Old World characiform family Citharinidae, Vari, 1979:294). Vari 1989a.
description_en: The ethmo-palatine cartilage (EPC) is a distinct body situated between the posterior surface of the upper arm of the premaxilla and the anterior margin of the palatine. There is usually only a single cartilage mass lying between these bones, although that cartilage is apparently subdivided into two units in some taxa (e.g., the Old World characiform family Citharinidae, Vari, 1979:294). Vari 1989a.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Region consisitng of the ethmoid and sphenoid bones.
description_en: Region consisitng of the ethmoid and sphenoid bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A synovial joint that connects a vertebral bone 1 and connects a exoccipital bone.
description_en: A synovial joint that connects a vertebral bone 1 and connects a exoccipital bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Paired cartilage bone that bears a large foramen (lateral occipital foramen). Contacts the supraoccipital dorsally, the epiotic laterally and the basioccipital ventrally. Forms the posterior hind margin of the cranium and borders the lateral and posterior margins of the forum (foramen) magnum.
description_en: Paired cartilage bone that bears a large foramen (lateral occipital foramen). Contacts the supraoccipital dorsally, the epiotic laterally and the basioccipital ventrally. Forms the posterior hind margin of the cranium and borders the lateral and posterior margins of the forum (foramen) magnum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An exoccipital bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.
description_en: An exoccipital bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Endochondral bone which is the posterodorsal region of the exoccipital bone.
description_en: Endochondral bone which is the posterodorsal region of the exoccipital bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): extensor carpi radialis longus
description_en: extensor carpi radialis longus

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A muscle that originates via thin tendons from the distal and dorsal aspects of the neural spines. The tendons course proximomedially to distolaterally and give rise to fleshy fibers that insert onto the lateral aspect of the neural arches of each of the vertebrae it crosses. The m. extensor caudae medialis is a continuation of m. semispinalis dorsi into the tail.
description_en: A muscle that originates via thin tendons from the distal and dorsal aspects of the neural spines. The tendons course proximomedially to distolaterally and give rise to fleshy fibers that insert onto the lateral aspect of the neural arches of each of the vertebrae it crosses. The m. extensor caudae medialis is a continuation of m. semispinalis dorsi into the tail.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An intercostal muscle that aids in quiet and forced inhalation via elevation of the ribs, and expanding the transverse dimensions of the thoracic cavity.
description_en: An intercostal muscle that aids in quiet and forced inhalation via elevation of the ribs, and expanding the transverse dimensions of the thoracic cavity.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein that is tributary of the angular vein and drains blood from the superficial tissues and skin of the dorsum (bridge) and ala (wings) of the nose.
description_en: A vein that is tributary of the angular vein and drains blood from the superficial tissues and skin of the dorsum (bridge) and ala (wings) of the nose.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Near the middle of the occipital squama is the external occipital protuberance, and extending lateralward from it on either side is the superior nuchal line, and above this the faintly marked highest nuchal line. It is less pronounced in females. The inion is the highest point of the external occipital protuberance. a projection on the external surface of the squamous part of the occipital bone in the midline.
description_en: Near the middle of the occipital squama is the external occipital protuberance, and extending lateralward from it on either side is the superior nuchal line, and above this the faintly marked highest nuchal line. It is less pronounced in females. The inion is the highest point of the external occipital protuberance. a projection on the external surface of the squamous part of the occipital bone in the midline.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): plexus venosus vertebralis externus
description_en: plexus venosus vertebralis externus

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Narrow bone that lies ventral to the level of insertion of the pectoral fin and is sutured to the posterior edges of both the clavicle and cleithrum. Based on Forey 1998.
description_en: Narrow bone that lies ventral to the level of insertion of the pectoral fin and is sutured to the posterior edges of both the clavicle and cleithrum. Based on Forey 1998.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A multicellular anatomical structure that is associated with an embryo and derived from the zygote from which it develops, but which does not contribute to the embryo proper or to structures that are part of the same organism after embryogenesis.
description_en: A multicellular anatomical structure that is associated with an embryo and derived from the zygote from which it develops, but which does not contribute to the embryo proper or to structures that are part of the same organism after embryogenesis.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Portion of tissue that is contiguous with the embryo and is comprised of portions of tissue or cells that will not contribute to the embryo.
description_en: Portion of tissue that is contiguous with the embryo and is comprised of portions of tissue or cells that will not contribute to the embryo.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal canal-bearing bone placed at the dorso-posterior region of the skull roof, lying on the posterior region of the pterotic and parietals, or the pterotic and epioccipital, or on the pterotic, epioccipital and occipital bones.
description_en: Dermal canal-bearing bone placed at the dorso-posterior region of the skull roof, lying on the posterior region of the pterotic and parietals, or the pterotic and epioccipital, or on the pterotic, epioccipital and occipital bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Extratemporal bone: Skull bone in the posterior half of the cranium, bordering the squamosal and opercular.
description_en: Extratemporal bone: Skull bone in the posterior half of the cranium, bordering the squamosal and opercular.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A chiasma of facial muscles held together by fibrous tissue, located lateral and slightly superior to each angle of the mouth. It is important in moving the mouth, facial expression and in dentistry. It derives its motor nerve supply from the facial nerve, and its blood supply from labial branches of the facial artery. It is contributed to by the following muscles: orbicularis oris, buccinator, levator anguli oris, depressor anguli oris, zygomaticus major, risorius quadratus labii superioris, quadratus labii inferioris.
description_en: A chiasma of facial muscles held together by fibrous tissue, located lateral and slightly superior to each angle of the mouth. It is contributed to by the following muscles: orbicularis oris, buccinator, levator anguli oris, depressor anguli oris, zygomaticus major, risorius quadratus labii superioris, quadratus labii inferioris.

It is located within the middle ear region, according to its shape it is divided into three main segments: the labyrinthine, the tympanic, and the mastoidal segment .

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Longest and strongest bone in the human body, the femur bears the body's weight and anchors the powerful muscles of the thigh, transmitting weight from the hip to the tibia during standing and locomotion. It extends from the hip joint to the knee. Its proximal end carries the femoral head, neck, and the greater and lesser trochanters; the shaft is bowed slightly forward; and the distal end forms the medial and lateral condyles that articulate with the tibia. Femoral neck fractures are common in elderly patients with osteoporosis, whereas shaft fractures usually follow high-energy trauma. The femoral head is vulnerable to avascular necrosis when its blood supply is interrupted.
description_en: Longest and strongest bone in the human body, the femur bears the body's weight and anchors the powerful muscles of the thigh, transmitting weight from the hip to the tibia during standing and locomotion. It extends from the hip joint to the knee. Its proximal end carries the femoral head, neck, and the greater and lesser trochanters; the shaft is bowed slightly forward; and the distal end forms the medial and lateral condyles that articulate with the tibia. Femoral neck fractures are common in elderly patients with osteoporosis, whereas shaft fractures usually follow high-energy trauma. The femoral head is vulnerable to avascular necrosis when its blood supply is interrupted.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The slender lateral bone of the leg, the fibula bears little weight but provides attachment for muscles and ligaments and forms part of the ankle joint through its lateral malleolus, which stabilizes the ankle on its lateral side. It lies lateral to the tibia and is connected to it by the interosseous membrane; the fibular head articulates with the lateral condyle of the tibia, and the lateral malleolus extends further inferiorly than the medial malleolus, adding to ankle stability. Fractures of the lateral malleolus are the most common ankle fractures, and the Weber classification grades ankle fractures by the level of the fibular break relative to the syndesmosis. The bone is frequently harvested as a graft donor site.
description_en: The slender lateral bone of the leg, the fibula bears little weight but provides attachment for muscles and ligaments and forms part of the ankle joint through its lateral malleolus, which stabilizes the ankle on its lateral side. It lies lateral to the tibia and is connected to it by the interosseous membrane; the fibular head articulates with the lateral condyle of the tibia, and the lateral malleolus extends further inferiorly than the medial malleolus, adding to ankle stability. Fractures of the lateral malleolus are the most common ankle fractures, and the Weber classification grades ankle fractures by the level of the fibular break relative to the syndesmosis. The bone is frequently harvested as a graft donor site.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A muscle located in the lower limb that arises from the lower third of the anterior surface of the fibula; from the lower part of the interosseous membrane; and from an intermuscular septum between it and the peroneus brevis and inserted into the dorsal surface of the base of the metatarsal bone of the 5th digit. It is innervated by the deep fibular nerve. Its action is that of weak dorsiflexion of the ankle joint and to evert the foot at the ankle joint.
description_en: A muscle located in the lower limb that arises from the lower third of the anterior surface of the fibula; from the lower part of the interosseous membrane; and from an intermuscular septum between it and the peroneus brevis and inserted into the dorsal surface of the base of the metatarsal bone of the 5th digit. The midzonal length of the girdle is shorter than that of an arciferal girdle, but pre- and postzonal elements tend to be longer.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The frontal crest of the frontal bone ends below in a small notch which is converted into a foramen, the foramen cecum, by articulation with the ethmoid. This foramen varies in size in different subjects, and is frequently impervious; when open, it transmits a vein from the nose to the superior sagittal sinus. This has clinical importance in that infections of the nose and nearby areas can be transmitted to the meninges and brain from what is known as the danger triangle of the face.

Apart from the transmission of the medulla oblongata and its membranes, the foramen magnum transmits the Spinal Accessory nerve, vertebral arteries, the anterior and posterior spinal arteries, the membrana tectoria and alar ligaments. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The part of the face above the eyes[MESH]. In human anatomy, the forehead is the fore part of the head. It is, formally, an area of the head bounded by three features, two of the skull and one of the scalp. The top of the forehead is marked by the hairline, the edge of the area where hair on the scalp grows. The bottom of the forehead is marked by the supraorbital ridge, the bone feature of the skull above the eyes. The two sides of the forehead are marked by the temporal ridge, a bone feature that links the supraorbital ridge to the coronal suture line and beyond[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Great Cardiac Vein (left coronary vein) begins at the apex of the heart and ascends along the anterior longitudinal sulcus to the base of the ventricles.
