description_en: A saddle-shaped area that includes the nasal root and the lateral aspects of the nose. It lies between the glabella and the inferior boundary of the nasal bone, and extends laterally to the inner canth[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): One of the conchae of the ethmoid bone, which occupy the caudal part of the nasal fossae and form the lateral and superior portions of the turbinate bones in mammals[MP]. The ethmoturbinals are associated with the cribiform plate. They are covered with olfactory epithelium. Primarily, they serve to increase the surface area over which olfactory receptor neurons can come in contact with respiratory air. These olfactory receptor nerves then synapse with the mitral cells of the olfactory lobes through the cribiform plate in the manner described above[Palaeos].
description_en: One of the conchae of the ethmoid bone, which occupy the caudal part of the nasal fossae and form the lateral and superior portions of the turbinate bones in mammals[MP]. The ethmoturbinals are associated with the cribiform plate. They are covered with olfactory epithelium. Primarily, they serve to increase the surface area over which olfactory receptor neurons can come in contact with respiratory air. These olfactory receptor nerves then synapse with the mitral cells of the olfactory lobes through the cribiform plate in the manner described above[Palaeos].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony projection of the premaxilla that extends cadually and separates the nasal bones.
description_en: A bony projection of the premaxilla that extends cadually and separates the nasal bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A suture joining a nasal bone to another bone.
description_en: A suture joining a nasal bone to another bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The intersection of the frontal and two nasal bones of the human skull. Its manifestation on the visible surface of the face is a distinctly depressed area directly between the eyes, just superior to the bridge of the nose.
description_en: The intersection of the frontal and two nasal bones of the human skull. Its manifestation on the visible surface of the face is a distinctly depressed area directly between the eyes, just superior to the bridge of the nose.

english: articulation of the nasal bone with maxilla
translation_uz: articulation of the nasal bone with maxilla (Suyak)
definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A cranial suture that connects a nasal bone and connects a maxilla.
description_en: A cranial suture that connects a nasal bone and connects a maxilla.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A compound bone consisting of premaxilla, nasal and sometimes septomaxilla in adult members of Caeciliidae and Typhlonectidae.
description_en: A compound bone consisting of premaxilla, nasal and sometimes septomaxilla in adult members of Caeciliidae and Typhlonectidae.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The oval-shaped tarsal bone found between the talus and the 3 cuneiform bones.
description_en: The oval-shaped tarsal bone found between the talus and the 3 cuneiform bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A fluid-filled sac that lies between the navicular bone and the deep digital flexor muscle.
description_en: A fluid-filled sac that lies between the navicular bone and the deep digital flexor muscle.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An organism subdivision that extends from the head to the pectoral girdle, encompassing the cervical vertebral column.
description_en: An organism subdivision that extends from the head to the pectoral girdle, encompassing the cervical vertebral column.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bone that is part of a neck [Automatically generated definition].
description_en: A bone that is part of a neck [Automatically generated definition].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The neck region of a bone organ.
description_en: The neck region of a bone organ.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The femur neck or neck of the femur is a flattened pyramidal process of bone, connecting the femoral head with the femoral shaft, and forming with the latter a wide angle opening medialward.
description_en: The femur neck or neck of the femur is a flattened pyramidal process of bone, connecting the femoral head with the femoral shaft, and forming with the latter a wide angle opening medialward.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Neck of rib: the flattened 2.5 cm segment lateral to the head, bearing the crista colli costae and the articular and non-articular tubercle.
description_en: Neck of rib: the flattened 2.5 cm segment lateral to the head, bearing the crista colli costae and the articular and non-articular tubercle.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The neck of talus is directed forward and medialward, and comprises the constricted portion of the bone between the body and the oval head. Its upper and medial surfaces are rough, for the attachment of ligaments; its lateral surface is concave and is continuous below with the deep groove for the interosseous talocalcaneal ligament.
description_en: The neck of talus is directed forward and medialward, and comprises the constricted portion of the bone between the body and the oval head. Its upper and medial surfaces are rough, for the attachment of ligaments; its lateral surface is concave and is continuous below with the deep groove for the interosseous talocalcaneal ligament.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Opening and/or passageway for nerve(s) in bone.
description_en: Opening and/or passageway for nerve(s) in bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The cervical nerves are the spinal nerves from the cervical vertebrae. Although there are seven cervical vertebrae (C1-C7), there are eight cervical nerves (C1-C8). All nerves except C8 emerge above their corresponding vertebrae, while the C8 nerve emerges below the C7 vertebra. (In the other portions of the spine, the nerve emerges below the vertebra with the same name. Dorsal (posterior) distribution includes the greater occipital (C2) and third occipital (C3). Ventral (anterior) distribution includes the cervical plexus (C1-C4) and brachial plexus (C5-C8) [WP,unvetted].
description_en: The cervical nerves are the spinal nerves from the cervical vertebrae. Although there are seven cervical vertebrae (C1-C7), there are eight cervical nerves (C1-C8). All nerves except C8 emerge above their corresponding vertebrae, while the C8 nerve emerges below the C7 vertebra. (In the other portions of the spine, the nerve emerges below the vertebra with the same name. Dorsal (posterior) distribution includes the greater occipital (C2) and third occipital (C3). Ventral (anterior) distribution includes the cervical plexus (C1-C4) and brachial plexus (C5-C8) [WP,unvetted].

latin: nerve to stylopharyngeus from glossopharyngeal nerve
english: branch of glossopharyngeal nerve to stylopharyngeus
translation_uz: branch of glossopharyngeal nerve to stylopharyngeus (Suyak)
definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The stylopharyngeal branch of glossopharyngeal nerve is distributed to the Stylopharyngeus.
description_en: The stylopharyngeal branch of glossopharyngeal nerve is distributed to the Stylopharyngeus.

latin: network of trabecular spaces in bone tissue
definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Tissue cavity consisting of intercommunicating trabecular spaces in the cancellous bone.
description_en: Tissue cavity consisting of intercommunicating trabecular spaces in the cancellous bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Posterior part of a vertebra that consists of a pair of pedicles and a pair of laminae, and supports seven processes: four articular processes, two transverse processes one spinous process[WP]. ZFA: A neural arch encloses the neural canal and typically meets its partner to form a neural spine.
description_en: Posterior part of a vertebra that consists of a pair of pedicles and a pair of laminae, and supports seven processes: four articular processes, two transverse processes one spinous process[WP]. ZFA: A neural arch encloses the neural canal and typically meets its partner to form a neural spine.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Anatomical cluster that consists of supraneural 2 bone and supraneural 3 bone and their extensions, and which is part of the Weberian apparatus.
description_en: Anatomical cluster that consists of supraneural 2 bone and supraneural 3 bone and their extensions, and which is part of the Weberian apparatus.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Neural lamina is a median, vertical ridge or bony septum between neural spine 3 and neural spine 4 on the dorsal side of the Weberian vertebra. Neural lamina is unpaired.
description_en: Neural lamina is a median, vertical ridge or bony septum between neural spine 3 and neural spine 4 on the dorsal side of the Weberian vertebra. Neural lamina is unpaired.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): One of a series of plates on the dorsal midline of the turtle shell, posterior to the nuchal bone.
description_en: One of a series of plates on the dorsal midline of the turtle shell, posterior to the nuchal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Neural spine that is associated with the first vertebra.
description_en: Neural spine that is associated with the first vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Neural spine that is associated with the second vertebra.
description_en: Neural spine that is associated with the second vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Neural spine that is associated with the third vertebra.
description_en: Neural spine that is associated with the third vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Neural spine that is associated with the fourth vertebra.
description_en: Neural spine that is associated with the fourth vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Neural spine that is associated with the fifth vertebra.
description_en: Neural spine that is associated with the fifth vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Neural spine that is associated with the sixth vertebra.
description_en: Neural spine that is associated with the sixth vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Neural spine that is associated with the seventh vertebra.
description_en: Neural spine that is associated with the seventh vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): In the developing vertebrate, the neural tube is the embryo's precursor to the central nervous system, which comprises the brain and spinal cord. The neural groove gradually deepens as the neural folds become elevated, and ultimately the folds meet and coalesce in the middle line and convert the groove into a closed tube, the neural tube or neural canal (which strictly speaking is the center of the neural tube), the ectodermal wall of which forms the rudiment of the nervous system. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: In the developing vertebrate, the neural tube is the embryo's precursor to the central nervous system, which comprises the brain and spinal cord. The neural groove gradually deepens as the neural folds become elevated, and ultimately the folds meet and coalesce in the middle line and convert the groove into a closed tube, the neural tube or neural canal (which strictly speaking is the center of the neural tube), the ectodermal wall of which forms the rudiment of the nervous system. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bone that is part of a neurocranium [Automatically generated definition].
description_en: A bone that is part of a neurocranium [Automatically generated definition].

latin: neuron projection bundle connecting eye with brain
definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A neuron projection bundle that connects the retina or its analog in the eye with the brain. This includes the vertebrate optic nerve (not truly a nerve) as well as analogous structures such as the Bolwig nerve in Drosophila.
description_en: A neuron projection bundle that connects the retina or its analog in the eye with the brain. This includes the vertebrate optic nerve (not truly a nerve) as well as analogous structures such as the Bolwig nerve in Drosophila.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Joint in which the articulating bones or cartilages are connected by ligaments or fibrocartilage without an intervening synovial cavity. Examples: sagittal suture, inferior tibiofibular syndesmosis, costochondral joint, pubic symphysis.
description_en: Joint in which the articulating bones or cartilages are connected by ligaments or fibrocartilage without an intervening synovial cavity. Examples: sagittal suture, inferior tibiofibular syndesmosis, costochondral joint, pubic symphysis.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vertebra that does not have a transverse process.
description_en: A vertebra that does not have a transverse process.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony element (non-Weberian precaudal vertebra) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.
description_en: A bony element (non-Weberian precaudal vertebra) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The olfactory organ of vertebrates, consisting of nares, olfactory epithelia and the structures and skeletal framework of the nasal cavity.
description_en: The olfactory organ of vertebrates, consisting of nares, olfactory epithelia and the structures and skeletal framework of the nasal cavity.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A flexible rod-shaped body found in embryos of all chordates. It is composed of cells derived from the mesoderm and defines the primitive axis of the embryo. In some chordates, it persists throughout life as the main axial support of the body, while in most vertebrates it becomes the nucleus pulposus of the intervertebral disc. The notochord is found ventral to the neural tube.
description_en: A flexible rod-shaped body found in embryos of all chordates. It is composed of cells derived from the mesoderm and defines the primitive axis of the embryo. In some chordates, it persists throughout life as the main axial support of the body, while in most vertebrates it becomes the nucleus pulposus of the intervertebral disc. The notochord is found ventral to the neural tube.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Perichordal bone that surrounds the anterior tip of the notochord.
description_en: Perichordal bone that surrounds the anterior tip of the notochord.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Longitudinal process found in all cervical vertebrae, except the atlas, for the attachment of dorsal head musculature.
description_en: Longitudinal process found in all cervical vertebrae, except the atlas, for the attachment of dorsal head musculature.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Bony protuberance on the external surface of the occipital bone.[PHENOSCAPE:AD].
description_en: Bony protuberance on the external surface of the occipital bone.[PHENOSCAPE:AD].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A fibrous membrane, which, in the neck, represents the supraspinal ligaments of the upper vertebrae.
description_en: A fibrous membrane, which, in the neck, represents the supraspinal ligaments of the upper vertebrae.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Any of the four curved lines on the external surface of the occipital bone that serves as an attachment site for a muscle.
description_en: Any of the four curved lines on the external surface of the occipital bone that serves as an attachment site for a muscle.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that is a bony expansion in the integument anterior to or flanking the dorsal fin that is part of and at the distal end of a supraneural or dorsal fin proximal radial.
description_en: Dermal bone that is a bony expansion in the integument anterior to or flanking the dorsal fin that is part of and at the distal end of a supraneural or dorsal fin proximal radial.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The medullary or nutrient artery, usually accompanied by one or two veins, sends branches upward and downward to the bone marrow, which ramify in the medullary membrane, and give twigs to the adjoining canals.
description_en: The medullary or nutrient artery, usually accompanied by one or two veins, sends branches upward and downward to the bone marrow, which ramify in the medullary membrane, and give twigs to the adjoining canals.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Any of the passages admitting nutrient vessels to the medullary cavity of bone.
description_en: Any of the passages admitting nutrient vessels to the medullary cavity of bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein or veins draining a bone and emerging from a nutrient foramen.
description_en: A vein or veins draining a bone and emerging from a nutrient foramen.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A larval stage of that is the immature stage of some invertebrates that undergoe gradual metamorphosis (hemimetabolism) before reaching its adult stage.
description_en: A larval stage of that is the immature stage of some invertebrates that undergoe gradual metamorphosis (hemimetabolism) before reaching its adult stage.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The oblique arytenoid, the more superficial Arytenoid muscle, forms two fasciculi, which pass from the base of one cartilage to the apex of the opposite one, and therefore cross each other like the limbs of the letter X; a few fibers are continued around the lateral margin of the cartilage, and are prolonged into the aryepiglottic fold; they are sometimes described as a separate muscle, the Aryepiglotticus. The aryepiglottic muscle together with the transverse arytenoid and the thyroarytenoid work as a sphincter and close the larynx as we swallow or cough. Its innervation is by the recurrent laryngeal nerve (from vagus) just like all the intrinsic muscles of the larynx except the cricothyroid muscle.
description_en: The oblique arytenoid, the more superficial Arytenoid muscle, forms two fasciculi, which pass from the base of one cartilage to the apex of the opposite one, and therefore cross each other like the limbs of the letter X; a few fibers are continued around the lateral margin of the cartilage, and are prolonged into the aryepiglottic fold; they are sometimes described as a separate muscle, the Aryepiglotticus. The aryepiglottic muscle together with the transverse arytenoid and the thyroarytenoid work as a sphincter and close the larynx as we swallow or cough. Its innervation is by the recurrent laryngeal nerve (from vagus) just like all the intrinsic muscles of the larynx except the cricothyroid muscle.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The obturator foramen is the hole created by the ischium and pubis bones of the pelvis through which nerves and muscles pass.
description_en: The obturator foramen is the hole created by the ischium and pubis bones of the pelvis through which nerves and muscles pass.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The bone at the lower, posterior part of the skull.
description_en: The bone at the lower, posterior part of the skull.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A prominent bulge, or projection, of the occipital bone at the back of the skull[WP].
description_en: A prominent bulge, or projection, of the occipital bone at the back of the skull[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The occipital condyles are undersurface facets of the occipital bone in vertebrates, which function in articulation with the superior facets of the atlas vertebra. The condyles are oval or reniform (kidney-shaped) in shape, and their anterior extremities, directed forward and medialward, are closer together than their posterior, and encroach on the basilar portion of the bone; the posterior extremities extend back to the level of the middle of the foramen magnum. The articular surfaces of the condyles are convex from before backward and from side to side, and look downward and lateralward. To their margins are attached the capsules of the atlantoC6ccipital articulations, and on the medial side of each is a rough impression or tubercle for the alar ligament. At the base of either condyle the bone is tunnelled by a short canal, the hypoglossal canal.
description_en: The occipital condyles are undersurface facets of the occipital bone in vertebrates, which function in articulation with the superior facets of the atlas vertebra. The condyles are oval or reniform (kidney-shaped) in shape, and their anterior extremities, directed forward and medialward, are closer together than their posterior, and encroach on the basilar portion of the bone; the posterior extremities extend back to the level of the middle of the foramen magnum. The articular surfaces of the condyles are convex from before backward and from side to side, and look downward and lateralward. To their margins are attached the capsules of the atlantoC6ccipital articulations, and on the medial side of each is a rough impression or tubercle for the alar ligament. At the base of either condyle the bone is tunnelled by a short canal, the hypoglossal canal.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A belly of the occipitofrontalis muscle that is near the occipital bone.
description_en: A belly of the occipitofrontalis muscle that is near the occipital bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The occipitofrontalis or epicranius is a muscle which covers parts of the skull. It consists of two parts or bellies: The occipital belly, near the occipital bone, and the frontal belly, near the frontal bone.
description_en: The occipitofrontalis or epicranius is a muscle which covers parts of the skull. It consists of two parts or bellies: The occipital belly, near the occipital bone, and the frontal belly, near the frontal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The occipitomastoid suture is the cranial suture between the occipital bone and the mastoid portion of the temporal bone. It is continuous with the lambdoidal suture.
description_en: The occipitomastoid suture is the cranial suture between the occipital bone and the mastoid portion of the temporal bone. It is continuous with the lambdoidal suture.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Multi-tissue structure composed of enameloid and dentine surrounding a pulp cavity, and found either attached to dermal bone or freely in the skin.
description_en: Multi-tissue structure composed of enameloid and dentine surrounding a pulp cavity, and found either attached to dermal bone or freely in the skin.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Multi-tissue structure composed of enameloid, dentine surrounding a pulp cavity, and bone of attachment anchoring the element into the dermis[VSAO].
description_en: Multi-tissue structure composed of enameloid, dentine surrounding a pulp cavity, and bone of attachment anchoring the element into the dermis[VSAO].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The toothlike process on the upper surface of the axis, which articulates with the atlas above[GAID].
description_en: The toothlike process on the upper surface of the axis, which articulates with the atlas above[GAID].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Toothlike processes found on the mandible of some anurans; can be formed by dentary or dentary + mentomeckelian bones; odontoids lack enamel and dentine present in true teeth.
description_en: Toothlike processes found on the mandible of some anurans; can be formed by dentary or dentary + mentomeckelian bones; odontoids lack enamel and dentine present in true teeth.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Olecranon: the curved proximal ulnar eminence behind the elbow, receiving the triceps insertion and entering the olecranon fossa.
description_en: Olecranon: the curved proximal ulnar eminence behind the elbow, receiving the triceps insertion and entering the olecranon fossa.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A deep evacuation in the bone, into which the anconeal process of the ulna passes when the elbow joint is extended.
description_en: A deep evacuation in the bone, into which the anconeal process of the ulna passes when the elbow joint is extended.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bulbous anterior projection of the olfactory lobe that is the place of termination of the olfactory nerves and is especially well developed in lower vertebrates (as fishes)[BTO].
description_en: A bulbous anterior projection of the olfactory lobe that is the place of termination of the olfactory nerves and is especially well developed in lower vertebrates (as fishes)[BTO].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The olfactory organ of vertebrates, consisting of nares, olfactory epithelia and the structures and skeletal framework of the nasal cavity.
description_en: The olfactory organ of vertebrates, consisting of nares, olfactory epithelia and the structures and skeletal framework of the nasal cavity.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The olivocerebellar tract (olivocerebellar fibers) leaves the olivary nucleus and pass out through the hilum and decussate with those from the opposite olive in the raphé, then as internal arcuate fibers they pass partly through and partly around the opposite olive and enter the inferior peduncle to be distributed to the cerebellar hemisphere of the opposite side from which they arise. They terminate directly on Purkinje cells as the climbing fiber input system. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: The olivocerebellar tract (olivocerebellar fibers) leaves the olivary nucleus and pass out through the hilum and decussate with those from the opposite olive in the raphé, then as internal arcuate fibers they pass partly through and partly around the opposite olive and enter the inferior peduncle to be distributed to the cerebellar hemisphere of the opposite side from which they arise. They terminate directly on Purkinje cells as the climbing fiber input system. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Proximal portion of the prezonal element of the pectoral girdle. It may be a flat, midventral cartilaginous structure or a calcified or bony element elaborated into a stylum.
description_en: Proximal portion of the prezonal element of the pectoral girdle. It may be a flat, midventral cartilaginous structure or a calcified or bony element elaborated into a stylum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The omotransversarius is a straplike muscle, which advances and adducts the forelimb, as well as flexes the neck laterally. It covers the transverse processes of the cervical vertebrae, lying to their side. The omotransversarius lies ventral to the trapezius, cranial to the deltoid muscle and is covered cranially by the cleidocervicalis. It extends from the atlas to the spine of the scapula, with its origin on the transverse process of the atlas and its insertion in the distal end of the spine of the scapula. Its name can be split into omo, which is Greek for shoulder, and tranversarius which relates to its attachment to the transverse process of the atlas. This muscle is innervated by the accessory nerve.
description_en: The omotransversarius is a straplike muscle, which advances and adducts the forelimb, as well as flexes the neck laterally. It covers the transverse processes of the cervical vertebrae, lying to their side. The omotransversarius lies ventral to the trapezius, cranial to the deltoid muscle and is covered cranially by the cleidocervicalis. It extends from the atlas to the spine of the scapula, with its origin on the transverse process of the atlas and its insertion in the distal end of the spine of the scapula. Its name can be split into omo, which is Greek for shoulder, and tranversarius which relates to its attachment to the transverse process of the atlas. This muscle is innervated by the accessory nerve.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that forms the postero-dorsal part of the opercular series. The opercle articulates with the hyomandibula antero-dorsally and with the subopercle ventrally. The opercle is a paired bone.
description_en: Dermal bone that forms the postero-dorsal part of the opercular series. The opercle articulates with the hyomandibula antero-dorsally and with the subopercle ventrally. The opercle is a paired bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): One of eight distinct lateral lines in the 4-day larva positioned posteriorly to the second arch skeletal element. A sensory system on the surface of the fish, consisting of small sensory patches (neuromasts) distributed in discrete lines over the body surface. The lateral line system is stimulated by local water displacements and vibrations, and detects propulsion of the fish through the water, as well as facilitating shoaling, prey capture, and predator and obstacle avoidance. (See Anatomical Atlas entry for lateral line by T. Whitfield.).
description_en: One of eight distinct lateral lines in the 4-day larva positioned posteriorly to the second arch skeletal element. A sensory system on the surface of the fish, consisting of small sensory patches (neuromasts) distributed in discrete lines over the body surface. The lateral line system is stimulated by local water displacements and vibrations, and detects propulsion of the fish through the water, as well as facilitating shoaling, prey capture, and predator and obstacle avoidance. (See Anatomical Atlas entry for lateral line by T. Whitfield.).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Ectochordal or stegochordal vertebral centra that are convex anteriorly and concave posteriorly; they bear a condyle on the anterior end for the articulation with the posterior adjacent vertebral centrum, forming a ball-and-socket joint that allows extensive motion in most directions.
description_en: Ectochordal or stegochordal vertebral centra that are convex anteriorly and concave posteriorly; they bear a condyle on the anterior end for the articulation with the posterior adjacent vertebral centrum, forming a ball-and-socket joint that allows extensive motion in most directions.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): musculus opponens digiti minimi (Manus)
description_en: musculus opponens digiti minimi (Manus)

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Anatomical cavity at the start of the digestive tract that that is enclosed by the mouth. The boundaries and contents vary depending on the species. In vertebrates, the boundaries are the oral opening, the cheeks, the palate and (if present) the palatoglossal arch - if this is not present then the mouth and pharynx form the oropharyngeal cavity. The buccal cavity contains the teeth, tongue and palate (when present).
description_en: Anatomical cavity at the start of the digestive tract that that is enclosed by the mouth. The boundaries and contents vary depending on the species. In vertebrates, the boundaries are the oral opening, the cheeks, the palate and (if present) the palatoglossal arch - if this is not present then the mouth and pharynx form the oropharyngeal cavity. The buccal cavity contains the teeth, tongue and palate (when present).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Foramen in the bone or cartilage comprising the anterior wall of the orbit, and through which passes at least the deep ophthalmic branch of cranial nerve V (trigeminal).
description_en: Foramen in the bone or cartilage comprising the anterior wall of the orbit, and through which passes at least the deep ophthalmic branch of cranial nerve V (trigeminal).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The inferior or orbital surface of the frontal lobe is concave, and rests on the orbital plate of the frontal bone. It is divided into four orbital gyri by a well-marked H-shaped orbital sulcus. These are named, from their position, the medial, anterior, lateral, and posterior orbital gyri. The medial orbital gyrus presents a well-marked antero-posterior sulcus, the olfactory sulcus, for the olfactory tract; the portion medial to this is named the straight gyrus, and is continuous with the superior frontal gyrus on the medial surface.
description_en: The inferior or orbital surface of the frontal lobe is concave, and rests on the orbital plate of the frontal bone. It is divided into four orbital gyri by a well-marked H-shaped orbital sulcus. These are named, from their position, the medial, anterior, lateral, and posterior orbital gyri. The medial orbital gyrus presents a well-marked antero-posterior sulcus, the olfactory sulcus, for the olfactory tract; the portion medial to this is named the straight gyrus, and is continuous with the superior frontal gyrus on the medial surface.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A zone of the frontal bone that consists of two thin triangular plates, the orbital plates, which form the vaults of the orbits, and are separated from one another by a median gap, the ethmoidal notch.
description_en: A zone of the frontal bone that consists of two thin triangular plates, the orbital plates, which form the vaults of the orbits, and are separated from one another by a median gap, the ethmoidal notch.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The ossified region of endochondral and membranous bone located in the clitoris of most mammals except humans; it is homologous to the penile bone (aka as baculum, penis bone or os penis) in male mammals.
description_en: The ossified region of endochondral and membranous bone located in the clitoris of most mammals except humans; it is homologous to the penile bone (aka as baculum, penis bone or os penis) in male mammals.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Scleral element located at the posterior pole of the scleral cartilage surrounding the foramen through which the optic nerve fibers pass. the internal architecture of this bone reveals a cancellous marrow cavity with fatty tissue.
description_en: Scleral element located at the posterior pole of the scleral cartilage surrounding the foramen through which the optic nerve fibers pass. the internal architecture of this bone reveals a cancellous marrow cavity with fatty tissue.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The unique bone located in the glans penis of most mammals except humans; it is used for copulation and varies in size and shape by species.
description_en: The unique bone located in the glans penis of most mammals except humans; it is used for copulation and varies in size and shape by species.

description_en: The Latin name for the os priapium is ossa priapium.

description_en: Skeletal element that is often isolated, small, and variable in composition.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Ossicones are horn-like protuberances on the heads of giraffes, male okapis, and their extinct relatives, such as Sivatherium, and the climacoceratids, such as Climacoceras. Only giraffids have true ossicones (as opposed to horns or antlers). The base that a deer's antlers grow from is very similar to ossicones. Ossicones are similar to the horns of antelopes and cattle, save that they are derived from ossified cartilage, and that the ossicones remain covered in skin and fur, rather than horn. Antlers (such as on deer) are derived from bone tissue: when mature, the skin and fur covering of the antlers, termed 'velvet,' is sloughed and scraped off to expose the bone of the antlers.
description_en: Ossicones are horn-like protuberances on the heads of giraffes, male okapis, and their extinct relatives, such as Sivatherium, and the climacoceratids, such as Climacoceras. Only giraffids have true ossicones (as opposed to horns or antlers). The base that a deer's antlers grow from is very similar to ossicones. Ossicones are similar to the horns of antelopes and cattle, save that they are derived from ossified cartilage, and that the ossicones remain covered in skin and fur, rather than horn. Antlers (such as on deer) are derived from bone tissue: when mature, the skin and fur covering of the antlers, termed 'velvet,' is sloughed and scraped off to expose the bone of the antlers.

description_en: Membrane bone that is fused to supracleithrum and is jointed to basioccipital and exoccipital.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Endochondral bone and Weberian ossicle that is an element of the fourth vertebra that curves ventrally around the anterior head of the swim bladder.
description_en: Endochondral bone and Weberian ossicle that is an element of the fourth vertebra that curves ventrally around the anterior head of the swim bladder.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Bone tissue that is an unmineralized bone matrix deposited by osteoblasts prior to the mineralization of bone tissue.
description_en: Bone tissue that is an unmineralized bone matrix deposited by osteoblasts prior to the mineralization of bone tissue.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A circular structural unit of bone tissue. It consists of a central hole, the Haversian canal through which blood vessels run, surrounded by concentric rings, called lamellae.
description_en: A circular structural unit of bone tissue. It consists of a central hole, the Haversian canal through which blood vessels run, surrounded by concentric rings, called lamellae.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Small, broadly triangular bar of bone lying across the ventral side of the pharynx at the junction of the M. genio-hyoideus and the M. rectus cervicis superficialis.
description_en: Small, broadly triangular bar of bone lying across the ventral side of the pharynx at the junction of the M. genio-hyoideus and the M. rectus cervicis superficialis.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An accessory bone located proximal to the base of the fifth metatarsal. Its prevalence has been reported to be from 0.1% to 1.0%. This bone is found within the peroneus brevis tendon and is considered to be asymptomatic in the majority of people.
description_en: An accessory bone located proximal to the base of the fifth metatarsal. Its prevalence has been reported to be from 0.1% to 1.0%. This bone is found within the peroneus brevis tendon and is considered to be asymptomatic in the majority of people.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): One of eight distinct lateral lines in the 4-day larva positioned anterior to the ear. A sensory system on the surface of the fish, consisting of small sensory patches (neuromasts) distributed in discrete lines over the body surface. The lateral line system is stimulated by local water displacements and vibrations, and detects propulsion of the fish through the water, as well as facilitating shoaling, prey capture, and predator and obstacle avoidance. (See Anatomical Atlas entry for lateral line by T. Whitfield.).
description_en: One of eight distinct lateral lines in the 4-day larva positioned anterior to the ear. A sensory system on the surface of the fish, consisting of small sensory patches (neuromasts) distributed in discrete lines over the body surface. The lateral line system is stimulated by local water displacements and vibrations, and detects propulsion of the fish through the water, as well as facilitating shoaling, prey capture, and predator and obstacle avoidance. (See Anatomical Atlas entry for lateral line by T. Whitfield.).

description_en: The most lateral anatomical point on the mastoid process of temporal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Fused prootic and exoccipital bones.
description_en: Fused prootic and exoccipital bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The epidermis is the entire outer epithelial layer of an animal, it may be a single layer that produces an extracellular material (e.g. the cuticle of arthropods) or a complex stratified squamous epithelium, as in the case of many vertebrate species[GO].
description_en: The epidermis is the entire outer epithelial layer of an animal, it may be a single layer that produces an extracellular material (e.g. the cuticle of arthropods) or a complex stratified squamous epithelium, as in the case of many vertebrate species[GO].

description_en: A vein that carries deoxygenated blood from its corresponding ovary to inferior vena cava or one of its tributaries.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Paired fin radial element that is composed of bone tissue.
description_en: Paired fin radial element that is composed of bone tissue.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Multi-tissue structure composed of ganoine, dentine and bone; not known in extant taxa.
description_en: Multi-tissue structure composed of ganoine, dentine and bone; not known in extant taxa.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Any bone that is part of a palate.
description_en: Any bone that is part of a palate.

description_en: Line of union, in the floor of the orbit, between the orbital process of the palatine bone and the orbital surface of the maxilla.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Pancreatic juice is slightly alkaline and contains numerous enzymes and inactive enzyme precursors including alpha-amylase, chymotrypsinogen, lipase, procarboxypeptidase, proelastase, prophospholipase A2, ribonuclease, and trypsinogen. Its high concentration of bicarbonate ions helps to neutralize the acid from the stomach.
description_en: Pancreatic juice is slightly alkaline and contains numerous enzymes and inactive enzyme precursors including alpha-amylase, chymotrypsinogen, lipase, procarboxypeptidase, proelastase, prophospholipase A2, ribonuclease, and trypsinogen. Its high concentration of bicarbonate ions helps to neutralize the acid from the stomach.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The pancreatic veins consist of several small vessels which drain the body and tail of the pancreas, and open into the trunk of the great pancreatic vein. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: The pancreatic veins consist of several small vessels which drain the body and tail of the pancreas, and open into the trunk of the great pancreatic vein. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The paraaortic lymph nodes (also known as para-aortic, periaortic, and peri-aortic) are a group of lymph nodes that lie in front of the lumbar vertebral bodies near the aorta. These lymph nodes receive drainage from the lower gastrointestinal tract and the pelvic organs.
description_en: The paraaortic lymph nodes (also known as para-aortic, periaortic, and peri-aortic) are a group of lymph nodes that lie in front of the lumbar vertebral bodies near the aorta. These lymph nodes receive drainage from the lower gastrointestinal tract and the pelvic organs.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Chondrocranium chondrification center that fuses with cartilages derived from sclerotome region of occipital somites forming occipital bone, hypoglossal canals and foramen magnum.
description_en: Chondrocranium chondrification center that fuses with cartilages derived from sclerotome region of occipital somites forming occipital bone, hypoglossal canals and foramen magnum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A small collection of convoluted tubules, situated in front of the lower part of the cord above the head of the epididymis. These tubes are lined with columnar ciliated epithelium, and probably represent the remains of a part of the Wolffian body but are functionless and vestigial. The Wolffian body operates as a kidney (metanephros) in fishes and amphibians, but the corresponding tissue is co-opted to form parts of the male reproductive system in other classes of vertebrate. The paradidymis represents a remnant of an unused, atrophied part of the Wolffian body[WP,modified].
description_en: A small collection of convoluted tubules, situated in front of the lower part of the cord above the head of the epididymis. These tubes are lined with columnar ciliated epithelium, and probably represent the remains of a part of the Wolffian body but are functionless and vestigial. The Wolffian body operates as a kidney (metanephros) in fishes and amphibians, but the corresponding tissue is co-opted to form parts of the male reproductive system in other classes of vertebrate. The paradidymis represents a remnant of an unused, atrophied part of the Wolffian body[WP,modified].

description_en: Third bone of the lower leg, normally restricted to the area of the knee, in multuberculates, monotremes and some therians.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A part of the epithalamus present in some animal species. The eye may be photoreceptive and is usually associated with the pineal gland, regulating circadian rhythmicity and hormone production for thermoregulation. The parietal eye is a part of the epithalamus, which can be divided into two major parts; the epiphysis (the pineal organ, or pineal gland if mostly endocrine) and the parietal organ (often called the parietal eye, or third eye if it is photoreceptive). It arises as an anterior evagination of the pineal organ or as a separate outgrowth of the roof of the diencephalon. In some species, it protrudes through the skull.[4] The parietal eye uses a different biochemical method of detecting light than rod cells or cone cells in a normal vertebrate eye[WP].
description_en: A part of the epithalamus present in some animal species. The eye may be photoreceptive and is usually associated with the pineal gland, regulating circadian rhythmicity and hormone production for thermoregulation. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The largest sesamoid bone in the body, the patella is embedded within the quadriceps tendon and increases the mechanical advantage of the quadriceps by lengthening its lever arm for extension of the knee. Triangular in shape, it has a broad superior base and a pointed inferior apex; its posterior surface articulates with the patellar surface of the femur, and its roughened anterior surface receives the quadriceps tendon. Direct trauma or forceful contraction of the quadriceps can fracture it, and dislocation typically occurs laterally. Chondromalacia patellae, sometimes called runner's knee, causes anterior knee pain as the cartilage on its undersurface degenerates.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A subdivision of a limb or fin skeleton consisting of bones which connects the upper limb or fin to the axial skeleton on each side. It consists of the clavicle and scapula in humans and, in those species with three bones in the pectoral girdle, the coracoid. Some mammalian species (e.g. the dog and the horse) have only the scapula. In humans, the only joints between the shoulder girdle and axial skeleton are the sternoclavicular joints on each side. No joint exists between each scapula and the rib cage; instead the muscular connection between the two permits relatively great mobility of the shoulder girdle in relation to the pelvic girdle. In those species having only the scapula, no joint exists between the forelimb and the thorax, the only attachment being muscular[WP]. Examples: There are only two instances, right and left pectoral girdle skeletons.
description_en: A subdivision of a limb or fin skeleton consisting of bones which connects the upper limb or fin to the axial skeleton on each side. It consists of the clavicle and scapula in humans and, in those species with three bones in the pectoral girdle, the coracoid. Some mammalian species (e.g. the dog and the horse) have only the scapula. In humans, the only joints between the shoulder girdle and axial skeleton are the sternoclavicular joints on each side. No joint exists between each scapula and the rib cage; instead the muscular connection between the two permits relatively great mobility of the shoulder girdle in relation to the pelvic girdle. In those species having only the scapula, no joint exists between the forelimb and the thorax, the only attachment being muscular[WP]. Examples: There are only two instances, right and left pectoral girdle skeletons.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Muscles of the upper chest. The term may refer to one of two muscles, the pectoralis major and pectoralis minor. The former is a thick muscle in the anterior portion of the chest. Its action involves flexion, medial rotation, and adduction of the humerus. The latter is a thin muscle located beneath the pectoralis major. Its action involves lowering the scapula and raising the ribs.
description_en: Muscles of the upper chest. The term may refer to one of two muscles, the pectoralis major and pectoralis minor. The former is a thick muscle in the anterior portion of the chest. Its action involves lowering the scapula and raising the ribs.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The perineal artery (superficial perineal artery) arises from the internal pudendal artery, and turns upward, crossing either over or under the Transversus perinæi superficialis, and runs forward, parallel to the pubic arch, in the interspace between the Bulbocavernosus and Ischiocavernosus, both of which it supplies, and finally divides into several posterior scrotal branches which are distributed to the skin and dartos tunic of the scrotum. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The pharyngeal aponeurosis (or pharyngobasilar fascia, or fibrous coat), is situated between the mucous and muscular layers. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony element (postcoronoid bone) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.
description_en: A bony element (postcoronoid bone) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The postcranial subdivision of skeleton structural components forming the long axis of the vertebrate body; in Danio, consisting of the notochord, vertebrae, ribs, supraneurals, intermuscular bones, and unpaired median fins; in human consists of the bones of the vertebral column, the thoracic cage and the pelvis[ZFA+FMA].
description_en: The postcranial subdivision of skeleton structural components forming the long axis of the vertebrate body; in Danio, consisting of the notochord, vertebrae, ribs, supraneurals, intermuscular bones, and unpaired median fins; in human consists of the bones of the vertebral column, the thoracic cage and the pelvis[ZFA+FMA].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): In a cervical vertebra, the posterior arch forms about two-fifths of the circumference of the ring: it ends behind in the posterior tubercle, which is the rudiment of a spinous process and gives origin to the Recti capitis posteriores minores.
description_en: In a cervical vertebra, the posterior arch forms about two-fifths of the circumference of the ring: it ends behind in the posterior tubercle, which is the rudiment of a spinous process and gives origin to the Recti capitis posteriores minores.

latin: posterior articular facet for talus of calcaneus
definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Posterior-most facet on the proximal surface of the calcaneus for the articulation of the talus bone.
description_en: Posterior-most facet on the proximal surface of the calcaneus for the articulation of the talus bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The posterior auricular artery is a small artery and arises from the external carotid artery, above the Digastric muscle and Stylohyoid muscle, opposite the apex of the styloid process. It ascends posteriorly beneath the parotid gland, along the styloid process of the temporal bone, between the cartilage of the ear and the mastoid process of the temporal bone along the lateral side of the head. The posterior auricular artery supplies blood to the scalp posterior to the auricle and to the auricle itself.
description_en: The posterior auricular artery is a small artery and arises from the external carotid artery, above the Digastric muscle and Stylohyoid muscle, opposite the apex of the styloid process. It ascends posteriorly beneath the parotid gland, along the styloid process of the temporal bone, between the cartilage of the ear and the mastoid process of the temporal bone along the lateral side of the head. The posterior auricular artery supplies blood to the scalp posterior to the auricle and to the auricle itself.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The posterior auricular muscle consists of two or three fleshy fasciculi, which arise from the mastoid portion of the temporal bone by short aponeurotic fibers. They are inserted into the lower part of the cranial surface of the concha.
description_en: The posterior auricular muscle consists of two or three fleshy fasciculi, which arise from the mastoid portion of the temporal bone by short aponeurotic fibers. They are inserted into the lower part of the cranial surface of the concha.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The posterior auricular vein begins upon the side of the head, in a plexus which communicates with the tributaries of the occipital vein and superficial temporal veins. It descends behind the auricula, and joins the posterior division of the posterior facial vein to form the external jugular. It receive the stylomastoid vein, and some tributaries from the cranial surface of the auricula.
description_en: The posterior auricular vein begins upon the side of the head, in a plexus which communicates with the tributaries of the occipital vein and superficial temporal veins. It descends behind the auricula, and joins the posterior division of the posterior facial vein to form the external jugular. It receive the stylomastoid vein, and some tributaries from the cranial surface of the auricula.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Posterior cartilage of palatine - cartilage that caps the posterior end of the autopalatine bone. It is typically present in adults.
description_en: Posterior cartilage of palatine - cartilage that caps the posterior end of the autopalatine bone. It is typically present in adults.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Replacement bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates anteriorly with the anterior ceratohyal.
description_en: Replacement bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates anteriorly with the anterior ceratohyal.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony element (posterior coronoid bone) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.
description_en: A bony element (posterior coronoid bone) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The infratentorial compartment that contains the CEREBELLUM and BRAIN STEM. It is formed by the posterior third of the superior surface of the body of the sphenoid (SPHENOID BONE), by the occipital, the petrous, and mastoid portions of the TEMPORAL BONE, and the posterior inferior angle of the PARIETAL BONE.
description_en: The infratentorial compartment that contains the CEREBELLUM and BRAIN STEM. It is formed by the posterior third of the superior surface of the body of the sphenoid (SPHENOID BONE), by the occipital, the petrous, and mastoid portions of the TEMPORAL BONE, and the posterior inferior angle of the PARIETAL BONE.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that is part of the scapular complex in placoderms, located posterior to the main components of the complex.
description_en: Dermal bone that is part of the scapular complex in placoderms, located posterior to the main components of the complex.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A blood vessel (posterior external vertebral venous plexus) that returns deoxygenated blood from its drainage territory to the central venous system.
description_en: A blood vessel (posterior external vertebral venous plexus) that returns deoxygenated blood from its drainage territory to the central venous system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A gap between bones in the skull at the junction of the sagittal suture and lambdoidal suture.
description_en: A gap between bones in the skull at the junction of the sagittal suture and lambdoidal suture.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA), the largest branch of the vertebral, is one of the three main arterial blood supplies for the cerebellum.
description_en: The posterior inferior cerebellar artery (PICA), the largest branch of the vertebral, is one of the three main arterial blood supplies for the cerebellum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein that is a tributary of the superior mesenteric vein. It drains the dorsal surface of the second and third portion of the duodenum and the dorsal surface of the head and uncinate process of the pancreas.
description_en: A vein that is a tributary of the superior mesenteric vein. It drains the dorsal surface of the second and third portion of the duodenum and the dorsal surface of the head and uncinate process of the pancreas.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): venae intercostalis posterior
description_en: venae intercostalis posterior

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Indentation on the anterior margin of the pedicel. When two vertebrae articulate, the anterior notch of one vertebra and the posterior notch of the other create a bilateral intervertebral space.
description_en: Indentation on the anterior margin of the pedicel. When two vertebrae articulate, the anterior notch of one vertebra and the posterior notch of the other create a bilateral intervertebral space.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): One of eight distinct lateral lines in the 4-day larva. A sensory system on the surface of the fish, consisting of small sensory patches (neuromasts) distributed in discrete lines over the body surface. The lateral line system is stimulated by local water displacements and vibrations, and detects propulsion of the fish through the water, as well as facilitating shoaling, prey capture, and predator and obstacle avoidance.
description_en: One of eight distinct lateral lines in the 4-day larva. A sensory system on the surface of the fish, consisting of small sensory patches (neuromasts) distributed in discrete lines over the body surface. The lateral line system is stimulated by local water displacements and vibrations, and detects propulsion of the fish through the water, as well as facilitating shoaling, prey capture, and predator and obstacle avoidance.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The posterior mediastinum is an irregular triangular space running parallel with the vertebral column.
description_en: The posterior mediastinum is an irregular triangular space running parallel with the vertebral column.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Posterior tongue, or pharyngeal part, is the part of the tongue behind the terminal sulcus. At its root, it is directed backward, and connected with the hyoid bone by the Hyoglossi and Genioglossi muscles and the hyoglossal membrane; with the epiglottis by three folds (glossoepiglottic) of mucous membrane; with the soft palate by the glossopalatine arches; and with the pharynx by the Constrictores pharyngis superiores and the mucous membrane. It is derived primarily from the third pharyngeal arch. (The second arch has a substantial contribution during fetal development, but this later atrophies. The fourth arch may also contribute, depending upon how the boundaries of the tongue are defined.).
description_en: The Posterior tongue, or pharyngeal part, is the part of the tongue behind the terminal sulcus. At its root, it is directed backward, and connected with the hyoid bone by the Hyoglossi and Genioglossi muscles and the hyoglossal membrane; with the epiglottis by three folds (glossoepiglottic) of mucous membrane; with the soft palate by the glossopalatine arches; and with the pharynx by the Constrictores pharyngis superiores and the mucous membrane. It is derived primarily from the third pharyngeal arch. (The second arch has a substantial contribution during fetal development, but this later atrophies. The fourth arch may also contribute, depending upon how the boundaries of the tongue are defined.).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Sclerotic bone that is located posterior to the eye.
description_en: Sclerotic bone that is located posterior to the eye.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein that is a tributary of the internal pudendal vein and drains the skin and fascial layers of the posterior scrotum.
description_en: A vein that is a tributary of the internal pudendal vein and drains the skin and fascial layers of the posterior scrotum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A spinal artery that arises from the vertebral artery, adjacent to the medulla oblongata[WP,modified].
description_en: A spinal artery that arises from the vertebral artery, adjacent to the medulla oblongata[WP,modified].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): posterior superior alveolar branches
description_en: posterior superior alveolar branches

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein that is a tributary of the hepatic portal vein. It drains the dorsal surface of the distal first and second portion of the duodenum and the dorsal surface of the pancreatic head.
description_en: A vein that is a tributary of the hepatic portal vein. It drains the dorsal surface of the distal first and second portion of the duodenum and the dorsal surface of the pancreatic head.

latin: posterior tubercle of transverse process of cervical vertebra
english: posterior costal tubercle of transverse process of cervical vertebra
translation_uz: posterior costal tubercle of transverse process of cervical vertebra (Suyak)
definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): posterior costal tubercle of transverse process of cervical vertebra
description_en: posterior costal tubercle of transverse process of cervical vertebra

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that is part of the ventral region of scapular complex in placoderms (see also anterior ventrolateral plate). In most placoderms with a long ventral armour, the ventral wall is typically composed of two large paired lateral plates (anterior and posterior ventrolaterals).
description_en: Dermal bone that is part of the ventral region of scapular complex in placoderms (see also anterior ventrolateral plate). In most placoderms with a long ventral armour, the ventral wall is typically composed of two large paired lateral plates (anterior and posterior ventrolaterals).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The region of an anatomical structure, such as a tooth or jaw bone, oriented posteriorly and facing the lips.
description_en: The region of an anatomical structure, such as a tooth or jaw bone, oriented posteriorly and facing the lips.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bone behind and above the orbit of which it commonly forms part of the border that is present in many vertebrates and corresponds to the postorbital process of the frontal bone of various birds and mammals.
description_en: A bone behind and above the orbit of which it commonly forms part of the border that is present in many vertebrates and corresponds to the postorbital process of the frontal bone of various birds and mammals.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A strut formed from the union of the zygomatic process of the frontal bone with the frontal process of the zygomatic bone.
description_en: A strut formed from the union of the zygomatic process of the frontal bone with the frontal process of the zygomatic bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The postorbital is one of the bones in vertebrate skulls which forms a portion of the dermal skull roof and, sometimes, a ring about the orbit. Generally, it is located behind the postfrontal and posteriorly to the orbital fenestra. In some vertebrates, the postorbital is fused with the postfrontal to create a postorbitofrontal.
description_en: The postorbital is one of the bones in vertebrate skulls which forms a portion of the dermal skull roof and, sometimes, a ring about the orbit. Generally, it is located behind the postfrontal and posteriorly to the orbital fenestra. In some vertebrates, the postorbital is fused with the postfrontal to create a postorbitofrontal.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Postorbital Process marks the rear, upper edge of the eye socket and is a projection from the frontal bone.
description_en: The Postorbital Process marks the rear, upper edge of the eye socket and is a projection from the frontal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bones (postparietals, supratemporals, intertemporals, extrascapulars) posterior to the intracranial joint. Forey 1997.
description_en: Dermal bones (postparietals, supratemporals, intertemporals, extrascapulars) posterior to the intracranial joint. Forey 1997.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony element (postrostral bone) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.
description_en: A bony element (postrostral bone) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The posterior portion of the sphenoid bone developed in five separate parts consisting of a central basisphenoid, the two alisphenoids, and the two medial pterygoid laminae.
description_en: The posterior portion of the sphenoid bone developed in five separate parts consisting of a central basisphenoid, the two alisphenoids, and the two medial pterygoid laminae.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone of the lower jaw.
description_en: Dermal bone of the lower jaw.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone of the secondary pectoral girdle that attaches the girdle to the skull. Its dorsal process attaches to the epiotic or epioccipital, the ventral process to the intercalar and the body articulates with the supracleithrum. The postotic sensory canal or lateral line runs within or lateral to bone.
description_en: Dermal bone of the secondary pectoral girdle that attaches the girdle to the skull. Its dorsal process attaches to the epiotic or epioccipital, the ventral process to the intercalar and the body articulates with the supracleithrum. The postotic sensory canal or lateral line runs within or lateral to bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that results from the fusion of the dermal posttemporal and the dermal supracleithrum. Forms the upper skeletal element of the pectoral girdle between the cleithrum and neurocranium. Posttemporal-supracleithrum is paired.
description_en: Dermal bone that results from the fusion of the dermal posttemporal and the dermal supracleithrum. Forms the upper skeletal element of the pectoral girdle between the cleithrum and neurocranium. Posttemporal-supracleithrum is paired.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): caudal articular process of vertebra
description_en: caudal articular process of vertebra

english: inferior articular process of cervical vertebra
translation_uz: inferior articular process of cervical vertebra (Suyak)
definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An postzygapophysis that is part of a cervical vertebra.
description_en: An postzygapophysis that is part of a cervical vertebra.

english: caudal articular process of lumbar vertebra
translation_uz: caudal articular process of lumbar vertebra (Suyak)
definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An postzygapophysis that is part of a lumbar vertebra.
description_en: An postzygapophysis that is part of a lumbar vertebra.

english: caudal articular process of thoracic vertebra
translation_uz: caudal articular process of thoracic vertebra (Suyak)
definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An postzygapophysis that is part of a thoracic vertebra.
description_en: An postzygapophysis that is part of a thoracic vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Osseous element of intramembranous origin that extends along the lingual margin of Meckel's cartilage.
description_en: Osseous element of intramembranous origin that extends along the lingual margin of Meckel's cartilage.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Vertebral bone lacking hemal spines (Weitzman, 1962), refers generally to the anterior vertebral region bounding the abdominal cavity. Alternate but not quite synonymous terms are abdominal or trunk vertebrae, which bear parapophyses and ribs. In many actinopterygians dorsal to the posterior abdominal cavity there are transitional vertebrae lacking ribs but also without hemal spines or sometimes even enclosed hemal arches. The primary definition would identify these vertebrae as precaudal. Bird and Mabee, 2003.
description_en: Vertebral bone lacking hemal spines (Weitzman, 1962), refers generally to the anterior vertebral region bounding the abdominal cavity. Alternate but not quite synonymous terms are abdominal or trunk vertebrae, which bear parapophyses and ribs. In many actinopterygians dorsal to the posterior abdominal cavity there are transitional vertebrae lacking ribs but also without hemal spines or sometimes even enclosed hemal arches. The primary definition would identify these vertebrae as precaudal. Bird and Mabee, 2003.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Vertebral cartilage elements lacking hemal spines (Weitzman, 1962), refers generally to the anterior vertebral region bounding the abdominal cavity. Alternate but not quite synonymous terms are abdominal or trunk vertebrae, which bear parapophyses and ribs. In many actinopterygians dorsal to the posterior abdominal cavity there are transitional vertebrae lacking ribs but also without hemal spines or sometimes even enclosed hemal arches. The primary definition would identify these vertebrae as precaudal.(Bird and Mabee, 2003).
description_en: Vertebral cartilage elements lacking hemal spines (Weitzman, 1962), refers generally to the anterior vertebral region bounding the abdominal cavity. Alternate but not quite synonymous terms are abdominal or trunk vertebrae, which bear parapophyses and ribs. In many actinopterygians dorsal to the posterior abdominal cavity there are transitional vertebrae lacking ribs but also without hemal spines or sometimes even enclosed hemal arches. The primary definition would identify these vertebrae as precaudal.(Bird and Mabee, 2003).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Vertebral elements lacking hemal spines (Weitzman, 1962), refers generally to the anterior vertebral region bounding the abdominal cavity. Alternate but not quite synonymous terms are abdominal or trunk vertebrae, which bear parapophyses and ribs. In many actinopterygians dorsal to the posterior abdominal cavity there are transitional vertebrae lacking ribs but also without hemal spines or sometimes even enclosed hemal arches. The primary definition would identify these vertebrae as precaudal.(Bird and Mabee, 2003).
description_en: Vertebral elements lacking hemal spines (Weitzman, 1962), refers generally to the anterior vertebral region bounding the abdominal cavity.
