In many actinopterygians dorsal to the posterior abdominal cavity there are transitional vertebrae lacking ribs but also without hemal spines or sometimes even enclosed hemal arches. The primary definition would identify these vertebrae as precaudal.(Bird and Mabee, 2003).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A horseshoe-shaped thickening of the endoderm at the cranial (rostral) end of the primitive streak formed by the involution of Spemann's organizer cells which, together with the notochord, induces the formation of the neural plate from the overlying ectodermal cells and contributes mesodermal type cells to the surrounding tissue.
description_en: A horseshoe-shaped thickening of the endoderm at the cranial (rostral) end of the primitive streak formed by the involution of Spemann's organizer cells which, together with the notochord, induces the formation of the neural plate from the overlying ectodermal cells and contributes mesodermal type cells to the surrounding tissue.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony element (precoronoid bone) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.
description_en: A bony element (precoronoid bone) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Odontogenic tissue that is collagen-rich and characteristic of vertebrate teeth and tooth-like structures (e.g., odontodes) deposited by preodontoblasts and odontoblasts that are typically excluded from the matrix.
description_en: Odontogenic tissue that is collagen-rich and characteristic of vertebrate teeth and tooth-like structures (e.g., odontodes) deposited by preodontoblasts and odontoblasts that are typically excluded from the matrix.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Vertebra that is positioned between the vertebra immediately anterior to the first dorsal-fin pterygiophore to the anteriormost vertebra.
description_en: Vertebra that is positioned between the vertebra immediately anterior to the first dorsal-fin pterygiophore to the anteriormost vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Small rounded to egg-shaped cartilage bone that sits in an anterolateral depression on the prevomer. Articulates with the autopalatine in all cypriniforms.
description_en: Small rounded to egg-shaped cartilage bone that sits in an anterolateral depression on the prevomer. Articulates with the autopalatine in all cypriniforms.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bone separating the lacrimal and frontal bones in many tetrapod skulls.
description_en: A bone separating the lacrimal and frontal bones in many tetrapod skulls.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): preganglionic autonomic fibre
description_en: preganglionic autonomic fibre

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): One of the bones of the upper jaw situated between and in front of the maxillae[VHOG].
description_en: One of the bones of the upper jaw situated between and in front of the maxillae[VHOG].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Pharyngeal arch bone immediately posterior to the ascending process, the medial surface of which articulates with the anterior end of the maxillary.
description_en: Pharyngeal arch bone immediately posterior to the ascending process, the medial surface of which articulates with the anterior end of the maxillary.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A dermal bone that forms anterior to the premaxillae between the maxillae and articulates with the nasals posteriorly.
description_en: A dermal bone that forms anterior to the premaxillae between the maxillae and articulates with the nasals posteriorly.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Tubular ossifications around extension of nasal lateral line canal in fishes; typically one or two.
description_en: Tubular ossifications around extension of nasal lateral line canal in fishes; typically one or two.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that is part of the opercular series and bears the preopercular sensory canal. The preopercle is a paired bone and typically L-shaped, with the horizontal limb overlying the interopercle and the vertical limb overlying the opercle.
description_en: Dermal bone that is part of the opercular series and bears the preopercular sensory canal. The preopercle is a paired bone and typically L-shaped, with the horizontal limb overlying the interopercle and the vertical limb overlying the opercle.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A dermal bone that is the lower, horizontal portion of the preopercle bone.
description_en: A dermal bone that is the lower, horizontal portion of the preopercle bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A dermal bone that is the upper, vertical portion of the preopercle bone.
description_en: A dermal bone that is the upper, vertical portion of the preopercle bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Sensory canal lateral or ventral to and in close proximity with the otic and post-otic sensory canals at their union, and anteroventrally with the mandibular sensory canal. The preopercular sensory canal is bilaterally paired and associated with the preopercle bone.
description_en: Sensory canal lateral or ventral to and in close proximity with the otic and post-otic sensory canals at their union, and anteroventrally with the mandibular sensory canal. The preopercular sensory canal is bilaterally paired and associated with the preopercle bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): preoperculo-mandibular canal
description_en: preoperculo-mandibular canal

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Part of the orbital plate formed by the jugal (part of the zygomatic), lacrimal (which is sometimes fused), sometimes nasal (typically in species with elongated rostra), and maxilla bones anterior to the orbit.
description_en: Part of the orbital plate formed by the jugal (part of the zygomatic), lacrimal (which is sometimes fused), sometimes nasal (typically in species with elongated rostra), and maxilla bones anterior to the orbit.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A hollow (fossa) in the preorbital region, typically lying on the maxillary bone, although sometimes can touch nasal bones (e.g., modern Equus).
description_en: A hollow (fossa) in the preorbital region, typically lying on the maxillary bone, although sometimes can touch nasal bones (e.g., modern Equus).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Rib located anterior to the sacral region.
description_en: Rib located anterior to the sacral region.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dorsal, dermal plate of bone that overlies the presacral vertebrae. Such shield usually has irregular, sculptured surfaces, frequently is broadly expanded, and may be composed of several separate plates.
description_en: Dorsal, dermal plate of bone that overlies the presacral vertebrae. Such shield usually has irregular, sculptured surfaces, frequently is broadly expanded, and may be composed of several separate plates.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The anterior part of the body of the sphenoid bone in front of the basisphenoid. It is usually a separate bone in the young or fetus, but becomes a part of the sphenoid in the adult.
description_en: The anterior part of the body of the sphenoid bone in front of the basisphenoid. It is usually a separate bone in the young or fetus, but becomes a part of the sphenoid in the adult.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The rhombencephalon (or hindbrain) is a developmental categorization of portions of the central nervous system in vertebrates. The rhombencephalon can be subdivided in a variable number of transversal swellings called rhombomeres. In the human embryo eight rhombomeres can be distinguished, from caudal to rostral: Rh7-Rh1 and the isthmus (the most rostral rhombomere). A rare disease of the rhombencephalon, 'rhombencephalosynapsis' is characterized by a missing vermis resulting in a fused cerebellum. Patients generally present with cerebellar ataxia. The caudal rhombencephalon has been generally considered as the initiation site for neural tube closure.
description_en: The rhombencephalon (or hindbrain) is a developmental categorization of portions of the central nervous system in vertebrates. The rhombencephalon can be subdivided in a variable number of transversal swellings called rhombomeres. In the human embryo eight rhombomeres can be distinguished, from caudal to rostral: Rh7-Rh1 and the isthmus (the most rostral rhombomere). A rare disease of the rhombencephalon, 'rhombencephalosynapsis' is characterized by a missing vermis resulting in a fused cerebellum. Patients generally present with cerebellar ataxia. The caudal rhombencephalon has been generally considered as the initiation site for neural tube closure.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An skeletal element of the upper pectoral girdle overlapped by the opercular and posttemporal bones.
description_en: An skeletal element of the upper pectoral girdle overlapped by the opercular and posttemporal bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Last caudal vertebra identified as the point at which the caudal vessels bifurcate, leaving the protection of the haemal arches of the caudal vertebrae and running laterally to the hypurals. This vertebra bears, commonly, a well-developed haemal arch and its spine (parhypural).
description_en: Last caudal vertebra identified as the point at which the caudal vessels bifurcate, leaving the protection of the haemal arches of the caudal vertebrae and running laterally to the hypurals. This vertebra bears, commonly, a well-developed haemal arch and its spine (parhypural).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Vertebra anterior to preural centrum 1; sometimes termed the 'antepenultimate' vertebra. Mabee and Bird, 2001.
description_en: Vertebra anterior to preural centrum 1; sometimes termed the 'antepenultimate' vertebra. Mabee and Bird, 2001.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony element (preural 3 vertebra) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.
description_en: A bony element (preural 3 vertebra) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Caudal vertebra that is one of the last caudal vertebrae anterior to the ural vertebrae that with its neural and haemal spines supports the procurrent caudal fin rays or lepidotrichia. The numbering of preural vertebrae is from caudal to rostral direction.
description_en: Caudal vertebra that is one of the last caudal vertebrae anterior to the ural vertebrae that with its neural and haemal spines supports the procurrent caudal fin rays or lepidotrichia. The numbering of preural vertebrae is from caudal to rostral direction.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A complex muscular and bony clasping and copulatory organ derived mainly from the pelvic fins, found under the head of male Phallostethoidea with the anus opening on one side and the genital pore on the other. The structure varies among family members. Hook-like ctenactia articulate basally with the aproctal axial which is movably articulated with the proctal axial bone itself, suspended anteriorly by the outer (and sometimes inner) pulvinular bone from the cleithrum and perhaps the urohyal. Other elements are the priapal ribs, the anteplural cartilage (supporting elements along with the cleithrum and the pulvinar), the toxactinium, the infrasulcar and the uncus (forming the claspers along with the ctenactinium), the penial, basipenial, papillary, prepapillary and cristate bones (forming the papillary unit).

The structure varies among family members. Hook-like ctenactia articulate basally with the aproctal axial which is movably articulated with the proctal axial bone itself, suspended anteriorly by the outer (and sometimes inner) pulvinular bone from the cleithrum and perhaps the urohyal. Other elements are the priapal ribs, the anteplural cartilage (supporting elements along with the cleithrum and the pulvinar), the toxactinium, the infrasulcar and the uncus (forming the claspers along with the ctenactinium), the penial, basipenial, papillary, prepapillary and cristate bones (forming the papillary unit).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Organizer for gastrulation in vertebrates. The primitive knot starts as a regional knot of cells that forms on the blastodisc immediately anterior to where the outer layer of cells will begin to migrate inwards - an area known as the primitive streak. Posterior to the node is the primitive pit, where the cells of the epiblast (the upper layer of embryonic cells) initially begin to invaginate. This invagination expands posteriorly into the primitive groove as the cells layers continue to move into the space between the embryonic cells and the yolk. This differentiates the embryo into the germ layers - endoderm, mesoderm, and ectoderm. The primitive knot migrates posteriorly as gastrulation proceeds, eventually being absorbed into the tail bud.[WP]. the regional thickening of cells at the rostral tip of the vertebrate primitive streak through which gastrulating cells migrate anteriorally to form tissues in the future head and neck; this region organizes the formation of the three embryonic layers and establishes the longitudinal axis and the polarity of the embryo[MP].
description_en: Organizer for gastrulation in vertebrates. The primitive knot starts as a regional knot of cells that forms on the blastodisc immediately anterior to where the outer layer of cells will begin to migrate inwards - an area known as the primitive streak. Posterior to the node is the primitive pit, where the cells of the epiblast (the upper layer of embryonic cells) initially begin to invaginate. This invagination expands posteriorly into the primitive groove as the cells layers continue to move into the space between the embryonic cells and the yolk. This differentiates the embryo into the germ layers - endoderm, mesoderm, and ectoderm. The primitive knot migrates posteriorly as gastrulation proceeds, eventually being absorbed into the tail bud.[WP]. the regional thickening of cells at the rostral tip of the vertebrate primitive streak through which gastrulating cells migrate anteriorally to form tissues in the future head and neck; this region organizes the formation of the three embryonic layers and establishes the longitudinal axis and the polarity of the embryo[MP].

The proatlas apparently develops from the ossified neural part of the sclerotome. Externally it resembles the neural arch of the vertebra, since it articulates anteriorly with the lateral occipital bone and posteriorly with the anterior articular process of the atlas.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The pudendal plexus (vesicoprostatic plexus) lies behind the arcuate pubic ligament and the lower part of the pubic symphysis, and in front of the bladder and prostate. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The lateral bone of the forearm, the radius rotates around the ulna during pronation and supination and articulates with the carpal bones at the wrist, bearing most of the load passed to the hand. Shorter than the ulna, it widens toward its distal end. Its head articulates with the capitulum of the humerus and the radial notch of the ulna, the radial tuberosity anchors the tendon of the biceps brachii, and a styloid process marks its distal end. Distal fractures, known as Colles' fractures, are the most common fractures of the upper extremity, and radial head fractures follow falls onto an outstretched hand. At the wrist, the radial artery provides the pulse commonly used for measurement.
description_en: The lateral bone of the forearm, the radius rotates around the ulna during pronation and supination and articulates with the carpal bones at the wrist, bearing most of the load passed to the hand. Shorter than the ulna, it widens toward its distal end. Its head articulates with the capitulum of the humerus and the radial notch of the ulna, the radial tuberosity anchors the tendon of the biceps brachii, and a styloid process marks its distal end. Distal fractures, known as Colles' fractures, are the most common fractures of the upper extremity, and radial head fractures follow falls onto an outstretched hand. At the wrist, the radial artery provides the pulse commonly used for measurement.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A flight feather that lies along a single horizontal row on the rear margin of the anatomical tail. Only the central pair are attached (via ligaments) to the tail bones; the remaining rectrices are embedded into the rectricial bulbs, complex structures of fat and muscle that surround those bones. Rectrices are always paired, with a vast majority of species having six pairs. They are absent in grebes and some ratites, and greatly reduced in size in penguins.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A muscle situated immediately behind the upper part of the Longus capitis that arises from the anterior surface of the lateral mass of the atlas, and from the root of its transverse process that inserts into the inferior surface of the basilar part of the occipital bone immediately in front of the foramen magnum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Rectus femoris muscle is one of the four quadriceps muscles of the human body. (The others are the vastus medialis, the vastus intermedius, and the vastus lateralis. All four combine to form the quadriceps tendon, which inserts into the patella and continues as the patellar ligament. ) The Rectus femoris is situated in the middle of the front of the thigh; it is fusiform in shape, and its superficial fibers are arranged in a bipenniform manner, the deep fibers running straight down to the deep aponeurosis. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The red vascular substance consisting of connective tissue and blood vessels, containing primitive blood cells, macrophages, megakaryocytes, and fat cells. Red marrow is found in the cavities of many bones. It manufactures and releases leukocytes and erythrocytes into the bloodstream.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): One of two laterally paired arteries that supplies the kidneys. These are large arteries that branch from the dorsal aorta in primitive vertebrates.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The renal plexus is formed by filaments from the celiac plexus, the aorticorenal ganglion, and the aortic plexus . It is joined also by the least splanchnic nerve. The nerves from these sources, fifteen or twenty in number, have a few ganglia developed upon them. They accompany the branches of the renal artery into the kidney; some filaments are distributed to the spermatic plexus and, on the right side, to the inferior vena cava.
description_en: The renal plexus is formed by filaments from the celiac plexus, the aorticorenal ganglion, and the aortic plexus . It is joined also by the least splanchnic nerve. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A rete mirabile (Latin for 'wonderful net'; plural retia mirabilia) is a complex of arteries and veins lying very close to each other, found in some vertebrates. The rete mirabile utilizes countercurrent blood flow within the net (blood flowing in opposite directions. ) It exchanges heat, ions, or gases between vessel walls so that the two bloodstreams within the rete maintain a gradient with respect to temperature, or concentration of gases or solutes.
description_en: A rete mirabile (Latin for 'wonderful net'; plural retia mirabilia) is a complex of arteries and veins lying very close to each other, found in some vertebrates. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The posterior section of the developing metencephalon recognized transiently within the vertebrate embryo; the rhombic lip extends posteriorly from the roof of the fourth ventricle to dorsal neuroepithelial cell and can be divided into eight structural units based on rhombomeres 1-8 (r1-r8), recognized at early stages of hindbrain development; producing granule cells and five brainstem nuclei, the rhombic lip plays an important role in developing a complex cerebellar neural system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The sacrococcygeal symphysis (sacrococcygeal articulation, articulation of the sacrum and coccyx) is an amphiarthrodial joint, formed between the oval surface at the apex of the sacrum, and the base of the coccyx. It is a slightly moveable joint which is frequently, partially or completely, obliterated in old age, homologous with the joints between the bodies of the vertebrae.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The sacrum forms the posterior wall of the pelvis. The sacral promontory projects anteriorly at the lumbosacral junction. Four pairs of sacral foramina transmit sacral nerves. The sacral canal is the inferior continuation of the vertebral canal.
description_en: The sacrum forms the posterior wall of the pelvis. The sacral promontory projects anteriorly at the lumbosacral junction. Four pairs of sacral foramina transmit sacral nerves. The sacral canal is the inferior continuation of the vertebral canal.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A ridge of bone running lengthwise along the midline of the top of the skull of many mammalian and reptilian skulls and serves as an attachment site for the temporailis muscle[WP,modified].
description_en: A ridge of bone running lengthwise along the midline of the top of the skull of many mammalian and reptilian skulls and serves as an attachment site for the temporailis muscle[WP,modified].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Sagittal keel (torus) is a thickening of bone on part or all of the midline of the frontal bone, or parietal bones where they meet along the sagittal suture, or on both bones..
description_en: The Sagittal keel (torus) is a thickening of bone on part or all of the midline of the frontal bone, or parietal bones where they meet along the sagittal suture, or on both bones..

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The dense, fibrous connective tissue joint between the tetrapod parietal bones.
description_en: The dense, fibrous connective tissue joint between the tetrapod parietal bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Scalenus anterior (Scalenus anticus), also known as anterior scalene muscle, lies deeply at the side of the neck, behind the Sternocleidomastoideus. It arises from the anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the third, fourth, fifth, and sixth cervical vertebrC&, and descending, almost vertically, is inserted by a narrow, flat tendon into the scalene tubercle on the inner border of the first rib, and into the ridge on the upper surface of the rib in front of the subclavian groove.
description_en: The Scalenus anterior (Scalenus anticus), also known as anterior scalene muscle, lies deeply at the side of the neck, behind the Sternocleidomastoideus. It arises from the anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the third, fourth, fifth, and sixth cervical vertebrC&, and descending, almost vertically, is inserted by a narrow, flat tendon into the scalene tubercle on the inner border of the first rib, and into the ridge on the upper surface of the rib in front of the subclavian groove.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Scalenus medius, the largest and longest of the three scalene muscles, arises from the posterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the lower six cervical vertebræ. It descendes along the side of the vertebral column to insert by a broad attachment into the upper surface of the first rib, between the tubercle and the subclavian groove. The brachial plexus and the subclavian artery pass anterior to it. Because it elevates the upper ribs, the middle scalene muscle is also one of the accessory muscles of respiration. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Flat and triangular, the scapula forms the posterior part of the shoulder girdle, articulating with the clavicle and the humerus and giving attachment to numerous muscles. It rests on the posterolateral thorax between the second and seventh ribs. Its surface features include the spine, the acromion, the coracoid process, the glenoid cavity that receives the head of the humerus, the supraspinous and infraspinous fossae, and the subscapular fossa. Fractures usually follow high-energy trauma and often accompany injuries within the thorax. Palsy of the long thoracic nerve causes scapular winging, in which the medial border lifts away from the chest wall, and the acromion may impinge on the rotator cuff.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Enlarged and broad extension of the scapula distal to the glenoid region that conforms to the contour of the ribs. Origin for the major shoulder muscles including the deltoid group.
description_en: Enlarged and broad extension of the scapula distal to the glenoid region that conforms to the contour of the ribs. Origin for the major shoulder muscles including the deltoid group.

description_en: Skeletal subdivision of dermal bones that may include the anterolateral plate (AL), the spinal process (Sp), and anteroventral plate (AV) and other dermal bones that are part of the pectoral girdle.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Foramen that is located in the scapula. The scapular foramen is paired and formed by a ring of bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Either of two notches on the dorsal border of the hip bone on each side that when closed off by ligaments form the corresponding sciatic foramina.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony plate around the eyes, are situated at the corneal-scleral limbus. They do not articulate with other elements of the skull. Typically, the scleral ossicles overlap the rim of a cup of scleral cartilage that supports the eyeball. Situated near the equator of the eye and may slightly overlap the rim of scleral cartilage.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A sesamoid bone that lies adjacent to the tendon of one of the muscles responsible for adducting the nictitating membrane (the pyramidal nictitating muscle).
description_en: A sesamoid bone that lies adjacent to the tendon of one of the muscles responsible for adducting the nictitating membrane (the pyramidal nictitating muscle).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Sclerotic rings are rings of bone found in the eyes of several groups of vertebrate animals, except for mammals and crocodilians. They can be made up of single bones or small bones together. They are believed to have a role in supporting the eye, especially in animals whose eyes are not spherical, or which live underwater. Fossil sclerotic rings are known for a variety of extinct animals, including ichthyosaurs, pterosaurs, and dinosaurs, but are often not preserved[WP].
description_en: Sclerotic rings are rings of bone found in the eyes of several groups of vertebrate animals, except for mammals and crocodilians. They can be made up of single bones or small bones together. They are believed to have a role in supporting the eye, especially in animals whose eyes are not spherical, or which live underwater. Fossil sclerotic rings are known for a variety of extinct animals, including ichthyosaurs, pterosaurs, and dinosaurs, but are often not preserved[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Ventral somitic compartment that is a precursor of the axial skeleton[XAO]. Sclerotomes eventually differentiate into the vertebrae and most of the skull. The caudal (posterior) half of one sclerotome fuses with the rostral (anterior) half of the adjacent one to form each vertebra. From their initial location within the somite, the sclerotome cells migrate medially towards the notochord. These cells meet the sclerotome cells from the other side to form the vertebral body. From this vertebral body, sclerotome cells move dorsally and surround the developing spinal cord, forming the vertebral arch[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony external plate or scale, as on the shell of a turtle, the skin of crocodilians, the feet of some birds. Scutes are similar to scales and serve the same function. Unlike the scales of fish and snakes, which are formed from the epidermis, scutes are formed in the lower vascular layer of the skin and the epidermal element is only the top surface. Forming in the living dermis, the scutes produce a horny outer layer, that is superficially similar to that of scales. Scutes will usually not overlap as snake scales (but see the pangolin). The outer keratin layer is shed piecemeal, and not in one continuous layer of skin as seen in snakes or lizards. The dermal base may contain bone and produce dermal armour. Scutes with a bony base are properly called osteoderms. Dermal scutes are also found in the feet of birds and tails of some mammals, and are believed to be the primitive form of dermal armour in reptiles. The term is also used to describe the heavy armour of the armadillo and the extinct glyptodon, and is occasionally used as an alternative to scales in describing snakes or certain fishes, such as sturgeons[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Cartilage tissue that is part of the exoskeleton, deposited adjacent to bone after bone formation.
description_en: Cartilage tissue that is part of the exoskeleton, deposited adjacent to bone after bone formation.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): centrum ossificationis secundarium
description_en: centrum ossificationis secundarium

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A functional part of the visual cortex that plays a crucial role in the integration of information from various visual modalities and contribute to higher-order visual functions, including colour, object recognition and spatial awareness.
description_en: A functional part of the visual cortex that plays a crucial role in the integration of information from various visual modalities and contribute to higher-order visual functions, including colour, object recognition and spatial awareness.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Endochondral bone found between the preethmoid and maxilla.
description_en: Endochondral bone found between the preethmoid and maxilla.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The tertiary bronchi (also known as the segmental bronchi) arise from the secondary bronchi. The respiratory epithelium lining their lumen is surrounded by a layer of smooth muscle. This layer is composed of two ribbons of smooth muscle that spiral in opposite directions. The smooth muscle layer is surrounded by irregular plates of hyaline cartilage which help maintain the patency of the airway. Each of the tertiary bronchi serves a specific bronchopulmonary segment. There are 10 tertiary bronchi in the right lung, and eight in the left. The tertiary bronchi get smaller and divide into primary bronchioles. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: The tertiary bronchi (also known as the segmental bronchi) arise from the secondary bronchi. The respiratory epithelium lining their lumen is surrounded by a layer of smooth muscle. This layer is composed of two ribbons of smooth muscle that spiral in opposite directions. The smooth muscle layer is surrounded by irregular plates of hyaline cartilage which help maintain the patency of the airway. Each of the tertiary bronchi serves a specific bronchopulmonary segment. There are 10 tertiary bronchi in the right lung, and eight in the left. The tertiary bronchi get smaller and divide into primary bronchioles. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein that is tributary of the main pulmonary veins and drains oxygenated blood from a segment of the lung.
description_en: A vein that is tributary of the main pulmonary veins and drains oxygenated blood from a segment of the lung.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein that is a tributary of the renal vein and drains blood from a segment of the kidney.
description_en: A vein that is a tributary of the renal vein and drains blood from a segment of the kidney.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Any segmental subdivision of a nervous system. Includes metameric developmental segments, such as vertebrates neuromeres.
description_en: Any segmental subdivision of a nervous system. Includes metameric developmental segments, such as vertebrates neuromeres.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The sella turcica is a saddle-shaped depression in the sphenoid bone at the base of the human skull. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: The sella turcica is a saddle-shaped depression in the sphenoid bone at the base of the human skull. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Semispinalis capitis (Complexus) is situated at the upper and back part of the neck, deep to the Splenius, and medial to the Longissimus cervicis and capitis. It arises by a series of tendons from the tips of the transverse processes of the upper six or seven thoracic and the seventh cervical vertebræ, and from the articular processes of the three cervical above this. The tendons, uniting, form a broad muscle, which passes upward, and is inserted between the superior and inferior nuchal lines of the occipital bone. The medial part, usually more or less distinct from the remainder of the muscle, is frequently termed the Spinalis capitis; it is also named the Biventer cervicis since it is traversed by an imperfect tendinous inscription. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: The Semispinalis capitis (Complexus) is situated at the upper and back part of the neck, deep to the Splenius, and medial to the Longissimus cervicis and capitis. It arises by a series of tendons from the tips of the transverse processes of the upper six or seven thoracic and the seventh cervical vertebræ, and from the articular processes of the three cervical above this. The tendons, uniting, form a broad muscle, which passes upward, and is inserted between the superior and inferior nuchal lines of the occipital bone. The medial part, usually more or less distinct from the remainder of the muscle, is frequently termed the Spinalis capitis; it is also named the Biventer cervicis since it is traversed by an imperfect tendinous inscription. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): musculus semispinalis dorsi
description_en: musculus semispinalis dorsi

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Multi-tissue structure that is a fluid-filled canal in the integument and usually dermal bones, and contains one or more neuromast organs.
description_en: Multi-tissue structure that is a fluid-filled canal in the integument and usually dermal bones, and contains one or more neuromast organs.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that is ring-shaped or cylindrical and surrounds a sensory canal.
description_en: Dermal bone that is ring-shaped or cylindrical and surrounds a sensory canal.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Paired, intramembranous bones located within the nasal capsules and embedded in the nasal cartilages; it is pierced by the ductus nasolacrimalis.
description_en: Paired, intramembranous bones located within the nasal capsules and embedded in the nasal cartilages; it is pierced by the ductus nasolacrimalis.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A piece of dead bone that has become separated during the process of necrosis from normal/sound bone..
description_en: A piece of dead bone that has become separated during the process of necrosis from normal/sound bone..

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A muscle that originates from the vertebrae and inserts in the ribs.
description_en: A muscle that originates from the vertebrae and inserts in the ribs.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): serratus dorsalis cranialis
description_en: serratus dorsalis cranialis

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The serratus ventralis is a muscle that originates on the surface of the upper eight or nine ribs at the side of the chest and inserts along the entire anterior length of the medial border of the scapula. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: The serratus ventralis is a muscle that originates on the surface of the upper eight or nine ribs at the side of the chest and inserts along the entire anterior length of the medial border of the scapula. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A sesamoid element that is composed of bone tissue.
description_en: A sesamoid element that is composed of bone tissue.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A small sesamoid bone situated behind a condyle of the femur.
description_en: A small sesamoid bone situated behind a condyle of the femur.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A sesamoid bone that is part of a manus.
description_en: A sesamoid bone that is part of a manus.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A sesamoid bone that is part of a pes.
description_en: A sesamoid bone that is part of a pes.

latin: sesamoid bone of the peroneus longus muscle
definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A skeletal muscle (sesamoid bone of the peroneus longus muscle) that produces movement through contraction at its anatomical site.
description_en: A skeletal muscle (sesamoid bone of the peroneus longus muscle) that produces movement through contraction at its anatomical site.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Ossicle that develops within bands of dense, regular connective tissue (e.g., tendons and ligaments). Sesamoids are generally located proximate to a bony prominence, over which the dense regular connective tissue wraps, and/or a joint or articulation.
description_en: Ossicle that develops within bands of dense, regular connective tissue (e.g., tendons and ligaments). Sesamoids are generally located proximate to a bony prominence, over which the dense regular connective tissue wraps, and/or a joint or articulation.

latin: set of muscles of vertebral column
definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A skeletal muscle (set of muscles of vertebral column) that produces movement through contraction at its anatomical site.
description_en: A skeletal muscle (set of muscles of vertebral column) that produces movement through contraction at its anatomical site.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Sharpey's fibres (bone fibres, or perforating fibres) are a matrix of connective tissue consisting of bundles of strong collagenous fibres connecting periosteum to bone. They are part of the outer fibrous layer of periosteum, entering into the outer circumferential and interstitial lamellae of bone tissue.
description_en: Sharpey's fibres (bone fibres, or perforating fibres) are a matrix of connective tissue consisting of bundles of strong collagenous fibres connecting periosteum to bone. They are part of the outer fibrous layer of periosteum, entering into the outer circumferential and interstitial lamellae of bone tissue.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Short bones are designated as those bones that are as wide as they are long. Their primary function is to provide support and stability with little to no movement. They are one of five types of bones: long, short, flat, irregular and sesamoid. Examples of these bones include the tarsals in the foot and the carpals in the hand.
description_en: Short bones are designated as those bones that are as wide as they are long. Their primary function is to provide support and stability with little to no movement. They are one of five types of bones: long, short, flat, irregular and sesamoid. Examples of these bones include the tarsals in the foot and the carpals in the hand.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The middle phalanx of digit 3 in a horse.
description_en: The middle phalanx of digit 3 in a horse.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A subdivision of the pectoral complex consisting of the structures in the region of the shoulder joint (which connects the humerus, scapula and clavicle).
description_en: A subdivision of the pectoral complex consisting of the structures in the region of the shoulder joint (which connects the humerus, scapula and clavicle).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The bone of the upper arm, the humerus connects the shoulder to the elbow and provides the attachment points for muscles of the shoulder and arm that enable a wide range of upper limb movement. Proximally it articulates with the scapula at the glenohumeral joint, and distally with the radius and ulna at the elbow. Its surface landmarks include the greater and lesser tubercles, the deltoid tuberosity, and the medial and lateral epicondyles. Fractures of the surgical neck are common in elderly patients, while midshaft fractures may damage the radial nerve and cause wrist drop. In children, supracondylar fractures are the most common fractures at the elbow.
description_en: The bone of the upper arm, the humerus connects the shoulder to the elbow and provides the attachment points for muscles of the shoulder and arm that enable a wide range of upper limb movement. Proximally it articulates with the scapula at the glenohumeral joint, and distally with the radius and ulna at the elbow. Its surface landmarks include the greater and lesser tubercles, the deltoid tuberosity, and the medial and lateral epicondyles. Fractures of the surgical neck are common in elderly patients, while midshaft fractures may damage the radial nerve and cause wrist drop. In children, supracondylar fractures are the most common fractures at the elbow.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The joint that is formed by the union of the humerus, the scapula (or shoulder blade), and the clavicle (or collarbone). Commonly thought of as a single joint, the shoulder is actually made up of two separate joints - the glenohumeral and acromioclavicular joints.
description_en: The joint that is formed by the union of the humerus, the scapula (or shoulder blade), and the clavicle (or collarbone). Commonly thought of as a single joint, the shoulder is actually made up of two separate joints - the glenohumeral and acromioclavicular joints.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A wavy crest externally on the tympanic bone of cetaceans.
description_en: A wavy crest externally on the tympanic bone of cetaceans.

english: endothelium of irregular blood filled space
translation_uz: endothelium of irregular blood filled space (Suyak)
definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): endothelium of irregular blood filled space
description_en: endothelium of irregular blood filled space

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The group of nerve cell bodies located on the dorsal spinal roots within the vertebral column at the level of the sixth lumbar vertebra.
description_en: The group of nerve cell bodies located on the dorsal spinal roots within the vertebral column at the level of the sixth lumbar vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Organ consisting of skeletal tissue. Encompasses whole bones, fused bones, cartilaginious elements, teeth, dermal denticles.
description_en: Organ consisting of skeletal tissue. Encompasses whole bones, fused bones, cartilaginious elements, teeth, dermal denticles.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Anatomical projection that is composed of bone or cartilage tissue.
description_en: Anatomical projection that is composed of bone or cartilage tissue.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A muscle organ that consists of skeletal muscle tissue ensheathed in epimysium, that develops from myotome and that is innervated by some somatic motor neuron. Skeletal muscles are typically attached (via a tendon) to a bone but there are exceptions (e.g. intrinsic tongue muscles).
description_en: A muscle organ that consists of skeletal muscle tissue ensheathed in epimysium, that develops from myotome and that is innervated by some somatic motor neuron. Skeletal muscles are typically attached (via a tendon) to a bone but there are exceptions (e.g. intrinsic tongue muscles).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Anatomical cluster that consists of all the skeletal elements (eg., bone, cartilage, and teeth) of the body.
description_en: Anatomical cluster that consists of all the skeletal elements (eg., bone, cartilage, and teeth) of the body.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A subdivision of the skeleton that corresponds to the lower part of the mouth. The lower jaw skeleton includes the following elements, when present: lower jaw teeth, the mandible and other lower jaw bones, and Meckel's cartilage.
description_en: A subdivision of the skeleton that corresponds to the lower part of the mouth. The lower jaw skeleton includes the following elements, when present: lower jaw teeth, the mandible and other lower jaw bones, and Meckel's cartilage.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): all phalanges in forelimb autopod
description_en: all phalanges in forelimb autopod

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): all phalanges in hindlimb autopod
description_en: all phalanges in hindlimb autopod

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A subdivision of the skeleton that corresponds to the upper part of the mouth. The lower jaw skeleton includes the following elements, when present: upper jaw teeth, the maxilla and other lower jaw bones.
description_en: A subdivision of the skeleton that corresponds to the upper part of the mouth. The lower jaw skeleton includes the following elements, when present: upper jaw teeth, the maxilla and other lower jaw bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A zone of skin that is above the clavicle zone in the pectoral girdle region.
description_en: A zone of skin that is above the clavicle zone in the pectoral girdle region.

english: skin of posterior iliac crest region
translation_uz: skin of posterior iliac crest region (Suyak)
definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A zone of skin that is above the iliac crest in the pelvic girdle bone/zone.
description_en: A zone of skin that is above the iliac crest in the pelvic girdle bone/zone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A muscle structure of invertebrates whose origin and insertion sites are in basal side of the epidermis or structures derived from it. The simplest somatic muscles consist of a single cell and associated extracellular structures.
description_en: A muscle structure of invertebrates whose origin and insertion sites are in basal side of the epidermis or structures derived from it. The simplest somatic muscles consist of a single cell and associated extracellular structures.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Any anatomical space that is part of a vertebral column.
description_en: Any anatomical space that is part of a vertebral column.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Endochondral bone that forms the anterior portion of the braincase and forms from one ossification center on each side of the orbital cartilage.
description_en: Endochondral bone that forms the anterior portion of the braincase and forms from one ossification center on each side of the orbital cartilage.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Sphenofrontal suture is the cranial suture between the sphenoid bone and the frontal bone.
description_en: The Sphenofrontal suture is the cranial suture between the sphenoid bone and the frontal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): One of the paired paranasal sinuses, located in the body of the sphenoid bone and communicating with the highest meatus of the nasal cavity on the same side[MESH]. The sphenoidal sinuses (or sphenoid) contained within the body of the sphenoid vary in size and shape; owing to the lateral displacement of the intervening septum they are rarely symmetrical. The following are their average measurements: vertical height, 2.2 cm. ; transverse breadth, 2 cm. ; antero-posterior depth, 2.2 cm. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: One of the paired paranasal sinuses, located in the body of the sphenoid bone and communicating with the highest meatus of the nasal cavity on the same side[MESH]. The sphenoidal sinuses (or sphenoid) contained within the body of the sphenoid vary in size and shape; owing to the lateral displacement of the intervening septum they are rarely symmetrical. The following are their average measurements: vertical height, 2.2 cm. ; transverse breadth, 2 cm. ; antero-posterior depth, 2.2 cm. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Sphenoid bone: unpaired butterfly-shaped bone at the skull base, in front of the temporal bone and one of seven forming the orbit.
description_en: Sphenoid bone: unpaired butterfly-shaped bone at the skull base, in front of the temporal bone and one of seven forming the orbit.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A sphenoid endochondral element that is composed primarily of a pre-cartilage condensation.
description_en: A sphenoid endochondral element that is composed primarily of a pre-cartilage condensation.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The process projecting downward from either side of the sphenoid bone, in vertebrates divided into two plates, an inner and an outer (sometimes called the lateral and medial); the posterior nares pass through the space, called the pterygoid fossa, between the processes.
description_en: The process projecting downward from either side of the sphenoid bone, in vertebrates divided into two plates, an inner and an outer (sometimes called the lateral and medial); the posterior nares pass through the space, called the pterygoid fossa, between the processes.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A sphenoid bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.
description_en: A sphenoid bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The speno-maxillary fossa is a small triangular space situated at the angle of the junction of the spheno-maxillary and pterygo-maxillary fissures, and placed beneath the apex of the orbit. It is formed above by the under surface of the body of the sphenoid and by the orbital process of the palate bone.
description_en: The speno-maxillary fossa is a small triangular space situated at the angle of the junction of the spheno-maxillary and pterygo-maxillary fissures, and placed beneath the apex of the orbit. It is formed above by the under surface of the body of the sphenoid and by the orbital process of the palate bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An inconstant suture between the pterygoid process of the sphenoid bone and the body of the maxilla.
description_en: An inconstant suture between the pterygoid process of the sphenoid bone and the body of the maxilla.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The cartilaginous junction between the basisphenoid and basioccipital bones of the mammalian skull.
description_en: The cartilaginous junction between the basisphenoid and basioccipital bones of the mammalian skull.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Sphenoparietal suture is the cranial suture between the sphenoid bone and the parietal bone.
description_en: The Sphenoparietal suture is the cranial suture between the sphenoid bone and the parietal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The sphenopetrosal fissure (or sphenopetrosal suture) is the cranial suture between the sphenoid bone and the petrous portion of the temporal bone. It is in the middle cranial fossa.
description_en: The sphenopetrosal fissure (or sphenopetrosal suture) is the cranial suture between the sphenoid bone and the petrous portion of the temporal bone. It is in the middle cranial fossa.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Endochondral bone that sutures with the pterosphenoid anteriorly, the prootic ventrally, the frontal bone dorso-medially, and the pterotic dorso-posteriorly. Occasionally the sphenotic sutures with the parietal bone. The sphenotic separates the orbital from the otic region. The sphenotic bears a large antero-lateral or lateral or ventro-lateral process that borders the postero-dorsal margin of the orbit. The sphenotic is a paired bone.
description_en: Endochondral bone that sutures with the pterosphenoid anteriorly, the prootic ventrally, the frontal bone dorso-medially, and the pterotic dorso-posteriorly. Occasionally the sphenotic sutures with the parietal bone. The sphenotic separates the orbital from the otic region. The sphenotic bears a large antero-lateral or lateral or ventro-lateral process that borders the postero-dorsal margin of the orbit. The sphenotic is a paired bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A suture joining a sphenoid bone with the alae of a vomer to form a schindylesis type of joint.
description_en: A suture joining a sphenoid bone with the alae of a vomer to form a schindylesis type of joint.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Sphenozygomatic suture is the cranial suture between the sphenoid bone and the zygomatic bone.
description_en: The Sphenozygomatic suture is the cranial suture between the sphenoid bone and the zygomatic bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A median bony point projecting from the anterior and ventral margin of the sternum of a bird. From http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/spina%20externa.
description_en: A median bony point projecting from the anterior and ventral margin of the sternum of a bird. From http://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/spina%20externa.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): cerebro-cerebellar fissure
description_en: cerebro-cerebellar fissure

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The subclasses of motor neurons which project their axons to axial muscles that lie close to the vertebral column; motor neurons in the lateral subdivision of the MMC project their axons to body wall muscles.
description_en: The subclasses of motor neurons which project their axons to axial muscles that lie close to the vertebral column; motor neurons in the lateral subdivision of the MMC project their axons to body wall muscles.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A neural crest that has_potential_to_developmentally_contribute_to a spinal cord.
description_en: A neural crest that has_potential_to_developmentally_contribute_to a spinal cord.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): alba anterior medullae spinalis
description_en: alba anterior medullae spinalis

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Origin: spines of upper thoracic and lower cervical vertebrae; insertion: occipital bone; innervation: spinal nerves; action, extends head.
description_en: Origin: spines of upper thoracic and lower cervical vertebrae; insertion: occipital bone; innervation: spinal nerves; action, extends head.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): musculus spinalis cervicis
description_en: musculus spinalis cervicis

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Origin: spinous processes of two upper lumbar and two lower thoracic; insertion: spines of upper thoracic vertebrae; innervation: branches of spinal nerves; action: extends vertebral column.
description_en: Origin: spinous processes of two upper lumbar and two lower thoracic; insertion: spines of upper thoracic vertebrae; innervation: branches of spinal nerves; action: extends vertebral column.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dermal bone that is part of the scapular complex in placoderms, and located lateral to the anterior ventrolateral (AVL) plate.
description_en: Dermal bone that is part of the scapular complex in placoderms, and located lateral to the anterior ventrolateral (AVL) plate.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein that is part of a vertebral column.
description_en: A vein that is part of a vertebral column.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Spinotrapezius, also called thoracic trapezius, is the most posterior of the three trapezius muscles. It is triangular shaped. Posterior to the acromiotrapezius and overlaps latissimus dorsi on the front. Its origin is the neural spines of the thoracic vertebrae and its insertion is the scapular fascia. Its action is to draw the scapula to the dorsal and caudal regions.
description_en: Spinotrapezius, also called thoracic trapezius, is the most posterior of the three trapezius muscles. It is triangular shaped. Posterior to the acromiotrapezius and overlaps latissimus dorsi on the front. Its origin is the neural spines of the thoracic vertebrae and its insertion is the scapular fascia. Its action is to draw the scapula to the dorsal and caudal regions.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A small hole behind each eye that opens to the mouth in some fish. In the primitive jawless fish the first gill opening immediately behind the mouth is essentially similar to the other gill openings.
description_en: A small hole behind each eye that opens to the mouth in some fish. In the primitive jawless fish the first gill opening immediately behind the mouth is essentially similar to the other gill openings.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The major nerves supplying sympathetic innervation to the abdomen, including the greater, lesser, and lowest (or smallest) splanchnic nerves that are formed by preganglionic fibers from the spinal cord which pass through the paravertebral ganglia and then to the celiac ganglia and plexuses and the lumbar splanchnic nerves carry fibers which pass through the lumbar paravertebral ganglia to the mesenteric and hypogastric ganglia.
description_en: The major nerves supplying sympathetic innervation to the abdomen, including the greater, lesser, and lowest (or smallest) splanchnic nerves that are formed by preganglionic fibers from the spinal cord which pass through the paravertebral ganglia and then to the celiac ganglia and plexuses and the lumbar splanchnic nerves carry fibers which pass through the lumbar paravertebral ganglia to the mesenteric and hypogastric ganglia.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The splenial is a small bone in the lower jaw of reptiles, amphibians and birds, usually located on the lingual side (closest to the tongue) between the angular and suprangular.
description_en: The splenial is a small bone in the lower jaw of reptiles, amphibians and birds, usually located on the lingual side (closest to the tongue) between the angular and suprangular.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A superficial postvertebral muscle innervated by the posterior ramus of the cervical spinal nerve with origins in the upper thoracic and lower cervical spinous processes whose actions are to extend and ipsilaterally rotate the head and neck. Examples: splenius capitis, splenius cervicis.
description_en: A superficial postvertebral muscle innervated by the posterior ramus of the cervical spinal nerve with origins in the upper thoracic and lower cervical spinous processes whose actions are to extend and ipsilaterally rotate the head and neck. Examples: splenius capitis, splenius cervicis.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A muscle that arises from the lower half of the ligamentum nuchæ, from the spinous process of the seventh cervical vertebra, and from the spinous processes of the upper three or four thoracic vertebræ and inserts the mastoid process of the temporal bone, and into the rough surface on the occipital bone just below the lateral third of the superior nuchal line[WP,modified].
description_en: A muscle that arises from the lower half of the ligamentum nuchæ, from the spinous process of the seventh cervical vertebra, and from the spinous processes of the upper three or four thoracic vertebræ and inserts the mastoid process of the temporal bone, and into the rough surface on the occipital bone just below the lateral third of the superior nuchal line[WP,modified].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): musculus splenius cervicis
description_en: musculus splenius cervicis

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The articulation of the squamous portion of the temporal bones with the parietal bones[MP]. The squamosal suture arches backward from the pterion and connects the temporal squama with the lower border of the parietal: this suture is continuous behind with the short, nearly horizontal parietomastoid suture, which unites the mastoid process of the temporal with the region of the mastoid angle of the parietal[WP].
description_en: The articulation of the squamous portion of the temporal bones with the parietal bones[MP]. The squamosal suture arches backward from the pterion and connects the temporal squama with the lower border of the parietal: this suture is continuous behind with the short, nearly horizontal parietomastoid suture, which unites the mastoid process of the temporal with the region of the mastoid angle of the parietal[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The squama of the occipital bone, situated above and behind the foramen magnum, is curved from above downward and from side to side.
description_en: The squama of the occipital bone, situated above and behind the foramen magnum, is curved from above downward and from side to side.

The stapedius emerges from a pinpoint foramen in the apex of the pyramidal eminence (a hollow, cone-shaped prominence in the posterior wall of the tympanic cavity), and inserts into the neck of the stapes. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The stapes or stirrup is the stirrup-shaped small bone or ossicle in the middle ear which is attached to the incus laterally and to the fenestra ovalis, the 'oval window' medially. The oval window is adjacent to the vestibule of the inner ear. The stapes is the smallest and lightest bone in the human body. The stapes transmits the sound vibrations from the incus to the membrane of the inner ear inside the fenestra ovalis. The stapes is also stabilized by the stapedius muscle, which is innervated by the facial nerve. In non-mammalian vertebrates, the bone homologous to the stapes is usually called the columella; however, in reptiles, either term may be used[WP,unvetted].
description_en: The stapes or stirrup is the stirrup-shaped small bone or ossicle in the middle ear which is attached to the incus laterally and to the fenestra ovalis, the 'oval window' medially. The oval window is adjacent to the vestibule of the inner ear. The stapes is the smallest and lightest bone in the human body. The stapes transmits the sound vibrations from the incus to the membrane of the inner ear inside the fenestra ovalis. The stapes is also stabilized by the stapedius muscle, which is innervated by the facial nerve. In non-mammalian vertebrates, the bone homologous to the stapes is usually called the columella; however, in reptiles, either term may be used[WP,unvetted].

The stegural is a paired bone.

The stegural is a paired bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The sternocephalicus is a flat muscle and its caudal border is adjacent to the ventral border of the brachiocephalicus. The lateral aspect of this muscle is crossed obliquely by the external jugular vein. It originates as a unit on the first sternebrae. The cranial portion of the muscle divides into two separate sections with different insertion points. These are the sternomastoideus and the sterno-occipitalis. The ventral portion, the sternomastiodeus is the stronger and main continuation of the sternocephalicus, which inserts on the mastoid part of the temporal bone. The thin but wide dorsal segment, the sterno-occipitalis attaches to the dorsal nuchal crest by a thin aponeurosis. The main action provided by the sternocephalicus is movement of the head and neck to the side. Ventral branches of the cervical nerves are attached to this muscle.
description_en: The sternocephalicus is a flat muscle and its caudal border is adjacent to the ventral border of the brachiocephalicus. The lateral aspect of this muscle is crossed obliquely by the external jugular vein. It originates as a unit on the first sternebrae. The cranial portion of the muscle divides into two separate sections with different insertion points. These are the sternomastoideus and the sterno-occipitalis. The ventral portion, the sternomastiodeus is the stronger and main continuation of the sternocephalicus, which inserts on the mastoid part of the temporal bone. The thin but wide dorsal segment, the sterno-occipitalis attaches to the dorsal nuchal crest by a thin aponeurosis. The main action provided by the sternocephalicus is movement of the head and neck to the side. Ventral branches of the cervical nerves are attached to this muscle.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The sternohyoid muscle is a thin, narrow muscle attaching the hyoid bone to the sternum, one of the paired strap muscles of the infrahyoid muscles serving to depress the hyoid bone. It is innervated by the ansa cervicalis. The muscle arises from the posterior border of the medial end of the clavicle, the posterior sternoclavicular ligament, and the upper and posterior part of the manubrium sterni. Passing upward and medially, it is inserted by short tendinous fibers into the lower border of the body of the hyoid bone. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: The sternohyoid muscle is a thin, narrow muscle attaching the hyoid bone to the sternum, one of the paired strap muscles of the infrahyoid muscles serving to depress the hyoid bone. It is innervated by the ansa cervicalis. The muscle arises from the posterior border of the medial end of the clavicle, the posterior sternoclavicular ligament, and the upper and posterior part of the manubrium sterni. Passing upward and medially, it is inserted by short tendinous fibers into the lower border of the body of the hyoid bone. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Sternothyreoideus (or Sternothyroid muscle) is shorter and wider than the Sternohyoideus, beneath which it is situated. It arises from the posterior surface of the manubrium sterni, below the origin of the Sternohyoideus, and from the edge of the cartilage of the first rib, and sometimes that of the second rib, it is inserted into the oblique line on the lamina of the thyroid cartilage. This muscle is in close contact with its fellow at the lower part of the neck, but diverges somewhat as it ascends; it is occasionally traversed by a transverse or oblique tendinous inscription. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: The Sternothyreoideus (or Sternothyroid muscle) is shorter and wider than the Sternohyoideus, beneath which it is situated. It arises from the posterior surface of the manubrium sterni, below the origin of the Sternohyoideus, and from the edge of the cartilage of the first rib, and sometimes that of the second rib, it is inserted into the oblique line on the lamina of the thyroid cartilage. This muscle is in close contact with its fellow at the lower part of the neck, but diverges somewhat as it ascends; it is occasionally traversed by a transverse or oblique tendinous inscription. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The flat bone at the center of the anterior chest wall, the sternum shields the heart and great vessels and anchors the costal cartilages of the upper seven ribs and the clavicles; its interior is a site of red bone marrow production. It is built from three parts: the manubrium above, the body in the middle, and the xiphoid process below. The jugular notch lies at the superior border of the manubrium, and the sternal angle, or angle of Louis, marks the junction of the manubrium and body at the level of the second rib. Direct trauma, such as a steering-wheel impact, can fracture it. Median sternotomy is the standard surgical approach to the heart, and sternal marrow aspiration and biopsy are common diagnostic procedures.
description_en: The flat bone at the center of the anterior chest wall, the sternum shields the heart and great vessels and anchors the costal cartilages of the upper seven ribs and the clavicles; its interior is a site of red bone marrow production. It is built from three parts: the manubrium above, the body in the middle, and the xiphoid process below. The jugular notch lies at the superior border of the manubrium, and the sternal angle, or angle of Louis, marks the junction of the manubrium and body at the level of the second rib. Direct trauma, such as a steering-wheel impact, can fracture it. Median sternotomy is the standard surgical approach to the heart, and sternal marrow aspiration and biopsy are common diagnostic procedures.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The stroma of the bone marrow is all tissue not directly involved in the primary function of hematopoiesis. The yellow bone marrow belongs here, and makes the majority of the bone marrow stroma, in addition to stromal cells located in the red bone marrow. Yellow bone marrow is found in the Medullary cavity. Still, the stroma is indirectly involved in hematopoiesis, since it provides the hematopoietic microenvironment that facilitates hematopoiesis by the parenchymal cells. For instance, they generate colony stimulating factors, affecting hematopoiesis.
description_en: The stroma of the bone marrow is all tissue not directly involved in the primary function of hematopoiesis. The yellow bone marrow belongs here, and makes the majority of the bone marrow stroma, in addition to stromal cells located in the red bone marrow. Still, the stroma is indirectly involved in hematopoiesis, since it provides the hematopoietic microenvironment that facilitates hematopoiesis by the parenchymal cells. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Subclavius is a small triangular muscle, placed between the clavicle and the first rib. Along with the pectoralis major and pectoralis minor muscles, the subclavius muscle makes up the anterior wall of the axilla.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An artery that runs along the bottom of the lowest rib. They constitute the lowest pair of branches derived from the thoracic aorta, and are in series with the intercostal arteries. Each passes along the lower border of the twelfth rib behind the kidney and in front of the Quadratus lumborum muscle, and is accompanied by the twelfth thoracic nerve. It then pierces the posterior aponeurosis of the Transversus abdominis, and, passing forward between this muscle and the Obliquus internus, anastomoses with the superior epigastric, lower intercostal, and lumbar arteries. Each subcostal artery gives off a posterior branch which has a similar distribution to the posterior ramus of an intercostal artery. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: An artery that runs along the bottom of the lowest rib. They constitute the lowest pair of branches derived from the thoracic aorta, and are in series with the intercostal arteries. Each passes along the lower border of the twelfth rib behind the kidney and in front of the Quadratus lumborum muscle, and is accompanied by the twelfth thoracic nerve. It then pierces the posterior aponeurosis of the Transversus abdominis, and, passing forward between this muscle and the Obliquus internus, anastomoses with the superior epigastric, lower intercostal, and lumbar arteries. Each subcostal artery gives off a posterior branch which has a similar distribution to the posterior ramus of an intercostal artery. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Subcostales (Infracostales) consist of muscular and aponeurotic fasciculi, which are usually well-developed only in the lower part of the thorax; each originates from the inner surface of one rib, and is inserted into the inner surface of the second or third rib above, near its angle. Their fibers run in the same direction as those of the Intercostales interni.
description_en: The Subcostales (Infracostales) consist of muscular and aponeurotic fasciculi, which are usually well-developed only in the lower part of the thorax; each originates from the inner surface of one rib, and is inserted into the inner surface of the second or third rib above, near its angle. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The superior ophthalmic vein begins at the inner angle of the orbit in a vein named the nasofrontal which communicates anteriorly with the angular vein; it pursues the same course as the ophthalmic artery, and receives tributaries corresponding to the branches of that vessel. The ethmoidal veins drain into the superior ophthalmic vein. Vorticose veins also drain into the superior ophthalmic vein.
description_en: The superior ophthalmic vein begins at the inner angle of the orbit in a vein named the nasofrontal which communicates anteriorly with the angular vein; it pursues the same course as the ophthalmic artery, and receives tributaries corresponding to the branches of that vessel. Forming a short single trunk, it passes between the two heads of the Rectus lateralis and through the medial part of the superior orbital fissure, and ends in the cavernous sinus. The ethmoidal veins drain into the superior ophthalmic vein. Vorticose veins also drain into the superior ophthalmic vein.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The surangular is a dermal bone of the lower jaw. It typically covers much of the dorsal and lateral surface of the posterior jaw and variably extends onto the medial (inside) surface. The surangular articulates with and supports the articular, which forms the jaw joint with the quadrate in most vertebrates, and is in turn supported by the angular. More distally, the surangular bridges the mandibular fenestra, if one is present. It may also bear a raised dorsal coronoid process, an important attachment site for the mandibular adductors. At its distal (or rostral) end, the surangular meets the dentary, the main tooth-bearing bone of the lower jaw in most vertebrates.
description_en: The surangular is a dermal bone of the lower jaw. It typically covers much of the dorsal and lateral surface of the posterior jaw and variably extends onto the medial (inside) surface. The surangular articulates with and supports the articular, which forms the jaw joint with the quadrate in most vertebrates, and is in turn supported by the angular. More distally, the surangular bridges the mandibular fenestra, if one is present. It may also bear a raised dorsal coronoid process, an important attachment site for the mandibular adductors. At its distal (or rostral) end, the surangular meets the dentary, the main tooth-bearing bone of the lower jaw in most vertebrates.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The tail of the pancreas, located anatomically left near the hilum of the spleen, is not simply an anatomical distinction. The tail is the only part of the pancreas which contains Pancreatic Polypeptide (PP) cells, which are responsible for secreting pancreatic polypeptide to coordinate exocrine and islet enzyme release. PP cells are found in the tail's periphery. Beta cells and delta cells are found in the central part of the tail as with the rest of the pancreas. The cells described above are located exclusively in the islet cells; their secretions reach exocrine portions of the pancreas via the capillary network surrounding the islet cell populations. [WP,unvetted].

PP cells are found in the tail's periphery. Beta cells and delta cells are found in the central part of the tail as with the rest of the pancreas.
