definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bone that is part of the tarsal skeleton. Examples: calcaneus, talus, centralia.
description_en: A bone that is part of the tarsal skeleton. Examples: calcaneus, talus, centralia.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The tarsometatarsus is a bone that is found in the lower leg of certain tetrapods, namely birds. It is formed from the fusion of several bones found in other types of animals, and homologous to the mammalian tarsal (ankle) and metatarsal (pes) bones. Despite this, the tarsometatarsus of birds is often referred to as just the tarsus or metatarsus.
description_en: The tarsometatarsus is a bone that is found in the lower leg of certain tetrapods, namely birds. It is formed from the fusion of several bones found in other types of animals, and homologous to the mammalian tarsal (ankle) and metatarsal (pes) bones. Despite this, the tarsometatarsus of birds is often referred to as just the tarsus or metatarsus.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A tarsometatarsus bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.
description_en: A tarsometatarsus bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A cartilaginous condensation that has the potential to develop into a tarsal bone.
description_en: A cartilaginous condensation that has the potential to develop into a tarsal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A tarsus bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.
description_en: A tarsus bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A pre-cartilage condensation that has the potential to develop into a tarsal bone.
description_en: A pre-cartilage condensation that has the potential to develop into a tarsal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Tegmental Wall or Roof (paries tegmentalis) is formed by a thin plate of bone, the tegmen tympani, which separates the cranial and tympanic cavities. It is situated on the anterior surface of the petrous portion of the temporal bone close to its angle of junction with the squama temporalis; it is prolonged backward so as to roof in the tympanic antrum, and forward to cover in the semicanal for the Tensor tympani muscle. Its lateral edge corresponds with the remains of the petrosquamous suture[Grays] .
description_en: The Tegmental Wall or Roof (paries tegmentalis) is formed by a thin plate of bone, the tegmen tympani, which separates the cranial and tympanic cavities. It is situated on the anterior surface of the petrous portion of the temporal bone close to its angle of junction with the squama temporalis; it is prolonged backward so as to roof in the tympanic antrum, and forward to cover in the semicanal for the Tensor tympani muscle. Its lateral edge corresponds with the remains of the petrosquamous suture[Grays] .

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A neural crest that has_potential_to_developmentally_contribute_to a telencephalon.
description_en: A neural crest that has_potential_to_developmentally_contribute_to a telencephalon.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The region where the frontal, parietal, temporal, and sphenoid bones fuse.
description_en: The region where the frontal, parietal, temporal, and sphenoid bones fuse.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The large, irregular bone located at the base and side of the skull; consists of three parts at birth: squamous, tympanic, and petrous.
description_en: The large, irregular bone located at the base and side of the skull; consists of three parts at birth: squamous, tympanic, and petrous.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): One of two bilaterally symmetrical holes (fenestrae) in the temporal bone.
description_en: One of two bilaterally symmetrical holes (fenestrae) in the temporal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): facies temporalis ossis zygomatici
description_en: facies temporalis ossis zygomatici

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A synovial joint of the jaw that connects the mandible to the temporal bone.
description_en: A synovial joint of the jaw that connects the mandible to the temporal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Dense regular connective tissue that connects muscle to bone[VSAO].
description_en: Dense regular connective tissue that connects muscle to bone[VSAO].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The tensor veli palatini (tensor palati) is a broad, thin, ribbon-like muscle in the head that tenses the soft palate.
description_en: The tensor veli palatini (tensor palati) is a broad, thin, ribbon-like muscle in the head that tenses the soft palate.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The bone forming the forehead and roof of the eye orbit.
description_en: The bone forming the forehead and roof of the eye orbit.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony element (tetrapod frontal bone primordium) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.
description_en: A bony element (tetrapod frontal bone primordium) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): In humans: bone forming side and roof of cranium. Each bone is irregularly quadrilateral in form, and has two surfaces, four borders, and four angles.
description_en: In humans: bone forming side and roof of cranium. Each bone is irregularly quadrilateral in form, and has two surfaces, four borders, and four angles.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony element (tetrapod parietal bone primordium) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.
description_en: A bony element (tetrapod parietal bone primordium) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Cellular receptors which mediate the sense of temperature. Thermoreceptors in vertebrates are mostly located under the skin. In mammals there are separate types of thermoreceptors for cold and for warmth and NOCICEPTORS which detect cold or heat extreme enough to cause pain.
description_en: Cellular receptors which mediate the sense of temperature. Thermoreceptors in vertebrates are mostly located under the skin. In mammals there are separate types of thermoreceptors for cold and for warmth and NOCICEPTORS which detect cold or heat extreme enough to cause pain.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The third phalangeal bone in a digit ray.
description_en: The third phalangeal bone in a digit ray.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The thoracic ganglia are paravertebral ganglia. The thoracic portion of the sympathetic trunk typically has 12 thoracic ganglia. Emerging from the ganglia are thoracic splancic nerves (the cardiopulmonary, the greater, lesser, and least splanchic nerves) that help provide sympathetic innervation to abdominal structures. Also, the ganglia of the thoracic sympathetic trunk have both white and gray rami communicantes. The white rami carry sympathetic fibers arising in the spinal cord into the sympathetic trunk. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: The thoracic ganglia are paravertebral ganglia. The thoracic portion of the sympathetic trunk typically has 12 thoracic ganglia. Emerging from the ganglia are thoracic splancic nerves (the cardiopulmonary, the greater, lesser, and least splanchic nerves) that help provide sympathetic innervation to abdominal structures. Also, the ganglia of the thoracic sympathetic trunk have both white and gray rami communicantes. The white rami carry sympathetic fibers arising in the spinal cord into the sympathetic trunk. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): That part of the spine comprising the thoracic vertebrae.
description_en: That part of the spine comprising the thoracic vertebrae.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Subdivision of skeletal system that consists of all ribs in an organism connected to the sternum and the vertebrae. Some vertebrates have abdominal ribs (gastrialia), not connected to the vertebrate - these are not considered part of the rib case.
description_en: Subdivision of skeletal system that consists of all ribs in an organism connected to the sternum and the vertebrae. Some vertebrates have abdominal ribs (gastrialia), not connected to the vertebrate - these are not considered part of the rib case.

description_en: A bone that is part of a thorax [Automatically generated definition].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Subdivision of skeletal system that consists of all skeletal elements in the thoracic region of the trunk. In most vertebrates this is the rib cage and sternum.
description_en: Subdivision of skeletal system that consists of all skeletal elements in the thoracic region of the trunk. In most vertebrates this is the rib cage and sternum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The thoracic nerves are the spinal nerves emerging from the thoracic vertebrae. [WP,unvetted].

description_en: A vein that is tributary of the axillary vein and drains blood from the thoracoacromial region, including the pectoral, shoulder, and clavicular regions.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): In anatomy, the throat is the anterior part of the neck, in front of the vertebral column. It consists of the pharynx and larynx. An important feature of the throat is the epiglottis, a flap which separates the esophagus from the trachea and prevents inhalation of food or drink. The throat contains various blood vessels, various pharyngeal muscles, the trachea (windpipe) and the esophagus. The hyoid bone and the clavicle are the only bones located in the throat of mammals. It is sometimes considered a synonym for fauces. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: In anatomy, the throat is the anterior part of the neck, in front of the vertebral column. It consists of the pharynx and larynx. An important feature of the throat is the epiglottis, a flap which separates the esophagus from the trachea and prevents inhalation of food or drink. The throat contains various blood vessels, various pharyngeal muscles, the trachea (windpipe) and the esophagus. The hyoid bone and the clavicle are the only bones located in the throat of mammals. It is sometimes considered a synonym for fauces. [WP,unvetted].

description_en: thymic cortico-medullary boundary

description_en: Is a laterally bowed, sagittally compressed, slender element that extends from dorsocaudally from the lateral parts of the basihyoid. It connects the basiohyoid with the rostral corner of the thyroid cartlilage of the larynx.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): This small finger of cartilage completes the connection between the thyrohyoid bone and the thyroid cartilage (rostral cornu).
description_en: This small finger of cartilage completes the connection between the thyrohyoid bone and the thyroid cartilage (rostral cornu).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The thyrohyoid muscle is a small, quadrilateral muscle appearing like an upward continuation of the Sternothyreoideus. It belongs to the infrahyoid muscles group. It arises from the oblique line on the lamina of the thyroid cartilage, and is inserted into the lower border of the greater cornu of the hyoid bone. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: The thyrohyoid muscle is a small, quadrilateral muscle appearing like an upward continuation of the Sternothyreoideus. It belongs to the infrahyoid muscles group. It arises from the oblique line on the lamina of the thyroid cartilage, and is inserted into the lower border of the greater cornu of the hyoid bone. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The larger of the two leg bones, the tibia carries most of the weight transmitted from the femur to the foot and forms part of both the knee and the ankle. It lies medially in the leg. Its proximal end widens into the medial and lateral condyles, separated by the tibial plateau, and the tibial tuberosity below them anchors the patellar ligament; at the distal end, the medial malleolus contributes to the ankle joint. Fractures of the tibial plateau involve the knee surface, and shaft fractures are the most common long-bone fractures. Stress fractures of the tibia occur frequently in athletes and in military personnel.
description_en: The larger of the two leg bones, the tibia carries most of the weight transmitted from the femur to the foot and forms part of both the knee and the ankle. It lies medially in the leg. Its proximal end widens into the medial and lateral condyles, separated by the tibial plateau, and the tibial tuberosity below them anchors the patellar ligament; at the distal end, the medial malleolus contributes to the ankle joint. Fractures of the tibial plateau involve the knee surface, and shaft fractures are the most common long-bone fractures. Stress fractures of the tibia occur frequently in athletes and in military personnel.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The anterior and posterior arteries created at the bifurcation of the popliteal artery. The anterior tibial artery begins at the lower border of the popliteus muscle and lies along the tibia at the distal part of the leg to surface superficially anterior to the ankle joint. Its branches are distributed throughout the leg, ankle, and pes. The posterior tibial artery begins at the lower border of the popliteus muscle, lies behind the tibia in the lower part of its course, and is found situated between the medial malleolus and the medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity. Its branches are distributed throughout the leg and foot.
description_en: The anterior and posterior arteries created at the bifurcation of the popliteal artery. The anterior tibial artery begins at the lower border of the popliteus muscle and lies along the tibia at the distal part of the leg to surface superficially anterior to the ankle joint. Its branches are distributed throughout the leg, ankle, and pes. The posterior tibial artery begins at the lower border of the popliteus muscle, lies behind the tibia in the lower part of its course, and is found situated between the medial malleolus and the medial process of the calcaneal tuberosity. Its branches are distributed throughout the leg and foot.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A muscle that originates in the upper two-thirds of the lateral surface of the tibia and inserts into the medial cuneiform and first metatarsal bones of the foot. Its acts to invert the foot. It is situated on the lateral side of the tibia; it is thick and fleshy above, tendinous below. This muscle overlaps the anterior tibial vessels and deep peroneal nerve in the upper part of the leg. [WP,unvetted]. The M. tibialis cranialis is a muscle that flexes the tarsometatarsus. It originates on the craniodistal aspect of the femur and proximal tibiotarsus and inserts on the cranial surface of the tarsometarsus[EvoWiki].
description_en: A muscle that originates in the upper two-thirds of the lateral surface of the tibia and inserts into the medial cuneiform and first metatarsal bones of the foot. Its acts to invert the foot. It is situated on the lateral side of the tibia; it is thick and fleshy above, tendinous below. This muscle overlaps the anterior tibial vessels and deep peroneal nerve in the upper part of the leg. [WP,unvetted]. The M. tibialis cranialis is a muscle that flexes the tarsometatarsus. It originates on the craniodistal aspect of the femur and proximal tibiotarsus and inserts on the cranial surface of the tarsometarsus[EvoWiki].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The tibial tuberosity is on the anterior side of a tibia and is where a patella ligament attaches.
description_en: The tibial tuberosity is on the anterior side of a tibia and is where a patella ligament attaches.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Paired, endochondral bones formed by the fusion of the tibia and fibula. They form the shanks, extending from the knees to the ankles.
description_en: Paired, endochondral bones formed by the fusion of the tibia and fibula. They form the shanks, extending from the knees to the ankles.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The tibiotarsus is the large bone between the femur and the tarsometatarsus in the leg of a bird. It is the fusion of the proximal part of the tarsus with the tibia. A similar structure also occurred in the Mesozoic Heterodontosauridae. These small ornithischian dinosaurs were unrelated to birds and the similarity of their pes bones is best explained by convergent evolution.
description_en: The tibiotarsus is the large bone between the femur and the tarsometatarsus in the leg of a bird. It is the fusion of the proximal part of the tarsus with the tibia. A similar structure also occurred in the Mesozoic Heterodontosauridae. These small ornithischian dinosaurs were unrelated to birds and the similarity of their pes bones is best explained by convergent evolution.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A tibiotarsus bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.
description_en: A tibiotarsus bone or its cartilage or pre-cartilage precursor.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A circumscribed mass of ectodermal cells which bud off from the dental lamina; it becomes cup-shaped and develops on its internal face the ameloblast layer of cells that produces the enamel cap of a developing tooth.
description_en: A circumscribed mass of ectodermal cells which bud off from the dental lamina; it becomes cup-shaped and develops on its internal face the ameloblast layer of cells that produces the enamel cap of a developing tooth.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A tooth that is attached to a palatine bone.
description_en: A tooth that is attached to a palatine bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The part of a tooth that is implanted in the gum; the root is normally located below the neck of the tooth, covered by cementum rather than enamel, and attached by the periodontal ligament to the alveolar bone.
description_en: The part of a tooth that is implanted in the gum; the root is normally located below the neck of the tooth, covered by cementum rather than enamel, and attached by the periodontal ligament to the alveolar bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A small, often microscopic, tissue element in the form of a small beam, strut or rod, generally having a mechanical function, and usually but not necessarily composed of dense collagenous tissue. On histological section, a trabecula can look like a septum, but in three dimensions they are topologically distinct, with trabeculae being roughly rod or pillar-shaped and septa being sheet-like. Trabeculae are usually composed of dense fibrous tissue, i.e. mainly of collagen, and in most cases provide mechanical strengthening or stiffening to a soft solid organ, such as the spleen. They can be composed of other materials, such as bone or muscle[WP].
description_en: A small, often microscopic, tissue element in the form of a small beam, strut or rod, generally having a mechanical function, and usually but not necessarily composed of dense collagenous tissue. On histological section, a trabecula can look like a septum, but in three dimensions they are topologically distinct, with trabeculae being roughly rod or pillar-shaped and septa being sheet-like. Trabeculae are usually composed of dense fibrous tissue, i.e. mainly of collagen, and in most cases provide mechanical strengthening or stiffening to a soft solid organ, such as the spleen. They can be composed of other materials, such as bone or muscle[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Bone tissue that has a lattice-like or spongy structure; it is highly vascular and contains intercommunicating spaces filled with bone marrow.
description_en: Bone tissue that has a lattice-like or spongy structure; it is highly vascular and contains intercommunicating spaces filled with bone marrow.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The network of intersecting plates and spicules in cancellous bone which form a meshwork of intercommunicating spaces filled with blood vessels and marrow; in mature bone, the trabeculae are aligned in parallel with the lines of major compressive or tensile force.
description_en: The network of intersecting plates and spicules in cancellous bone which form a meshwork of intercommunicating spaces filled with blood vessels and marrow; in mature bone, the trabeculae are aligned in parallel with the lines of major compressive or tensile force.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein that is tributary of the external jugular vein and drains blood from the superficial muscles of the back, mainly the trapezius muscle.
description_en: A vein that is tributary of the external jugular vein and drains blood from the superficial muscles of the back, mainly the trapezius muscle.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A tributary of the superficial temporal or retromandibular veins, anastomosing with the facial vein.
description_en: A tributary of the superficial temporal or retromandibular veins, anastomosing with the facial vein.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Foramen that pierces the transverse processes of the seven cervical vertebrae. In the upper six vertebrae, the foramen gives passage to the vertebral artery, vertebral vein, and a plexus of sympathetic nerves. The seventh foramen lacks the artery, but contains the vein and sympathetic nerves.
description_en: Foramen that pierces the transverse processes of the seven cervical vertebrae. In the upper six vertebrae, the foramen gives passage to the vertebral artery, vertebral vein, and a plexus of sympathetic nerves. The seventh foramen lacks the artery, but contains the vein and sympathetic nerves.

description_en: A transverse foramen that is part of a vertebral bone 1.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A transverse foramen that is part of a vertebral bone 2.
description_en: A transverse foramen that is part of a vertebral bone 2.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein that is tributary of the angular veins and drains blood from the bridge of the nose.
description_en: A vein that is tributary of the angular veins and drains blood from the bridge of the nose.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The line of junction between the processes of the maxilla and the horizontal parts of the palatine bones that form the hard palate.
description_en: The line of junction between the processes of the maxilla and the horizontal parts of the palatine bones that form the hard palate.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vertebra that has a transverse process.
description_en: A vertebra that has a transverse process.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A transverse process of vertebra that is part of a vertebral bone 1.
description_en: A transverse process of vertebra that is part of a vertebral bone 1.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A transverse process that is part of a caudal vertebra.
description_en: A transverse process that is part of a caudal vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A transverse process that is part of a cervical vertebra.
description_en: A transverse process that is part of a cervical vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A transverse process that is part of a lumbar vertebra.
description_en: A transverse process that is part of a lumbar vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Endochondral bone that is the anterodorsally oriented process of the third neural arch.
description_en: Endochondral bone that is the anterodorsally oriented process of the third neural arch.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The transverse or costal processes of a vertebra, two in number, project one at either side from the point where the lamina joins the pedicle, between the superior and inferior articular processes. They serve for the attachment of muscles and ligaments. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: The transverse or costal processes of a vertebra, two in number, project one at either side from the point where the lamina joins the pedicle, between the superior and inferior articular processes. They serve for the attachment of muscles and ligaments. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Endochondral bone, which may be ossified or not in adults, located immediately anteriorly to the pterygiophore series of the anal fin. The structure is usually cylindrical, and its plane of symmetry is transverse to that of pterygiophores and fin rays.
description_en: Endochondral bone, which may be ossified or not in adults, located immediately anteriorly to the pterygiophore series of the anal fin. The structure is usually cylindrical, and its plane of symmetry is transverse to that of pterygiophores and fin rays.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The transversospinal muscles are a group of muscles of the human back. Their combined action is rotation and extension of the vertebral column. They include: semispinalis, spanning 4-6 vertebral segments semispinalis dorsi semispinalis cervicis semispinalis capitis multifidus, spanning 2-4 vertebral segments rotatores, spanning 1-2 vertebral segments rotatores cervicis rotatores thoracis rotatores lumborum.
description_en: The transversospinal muscles are a group of muscles of the human back. Their combined action is rotation and extension of the vertebral column. They include: semispinalis, spanning 4-6 vertebral segments semispinalis dorsi semispinalis cervicis semispinalis capitis multifidus, spanning 2-4 vertebral segments rotatores, spanning 1-2 vertebral segments rotatores cervicis rotatores thoracis rotatores lumborum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Transversus thoracis: thin muscular sheet on the inner anterior chest wall running from sternum and xiphoid to the second to sixth costal cartilages.
description_en: Transversus thoracis: thin muscular sheet on the inner anterior chest wall running from sternum and xiphoid to the second to sixth costal cartilages.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A large superficial muscle that extends longitudinally from the occipital bone to the lower thoracic vertebrae and laterally to the spine of the scapula (shoulder blade). Its functions are to move the scapulae and support the arm. The trapezius has three functional regions: the superior region (descending part), which supports the weight of the arm; the intermediate region (transverse part), which retracts the scapulae; and the inferior region (ascending part), which medially rotates and depresses the scapulae. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: A large superficial muscle that extends longitudinally from the occipital bone to the lower thoracic vertebrae and laterally to the spine of the scapula (shoulder blade). Its functions are to move the scapulae and support the arm. The trapezius has three functional regions: the superior region (descending part), which supports the weight of the arm; the intermediate region (transverse part), which retracts the scapulae; and the inferior region (ascending part), which medially rotates and depresses the scapulae. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A blood vessel (tributary of central retinal vein) that returns deoxygenated blood from its drainage territory to the central venous system.
description_en: A blood vessel (tributary of central retinal vein) that returns deoxygenated blood from its drainage territory to the central venous system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The triceps surae is a pair of muscles located at the calf - the gastrocnemius and the soleus. These muscles both insert into the calcaneus, the bone of the heel of the human foot, and form the major part of the muscle of the back part of the lower leg, commonly known as the calf muscle. The triceps surae is connected to the foot through the Achilles tendon, and has 3 heads deriving from the 2 major masses of muscle. The superficial portion (the gastrocnemius) gives off 2 heads attaching to the base of the femur directly above the knee. The deep (profundis) mass of muscle (the soleus) forms the remaining head which attaches to the superior posterior area of the tibia. The triceps surae is innervated by the tibial nerve, specifically, nerve roots L5-S2. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: The triceps surae is a pair of muscles located at the calf - the gastrocnemius and the soleus. These muscles both insert into the calcaneus, the bone of the heel of the human foot, and form the major part of the muscle of the back part of the lower leg, commonly known as the calf muscle. The triceps surae is connected to the foot through the Achilles tendon, and has 3 heads deriving from the 2 major masses of muscle. The superficial portion (the gastrocnemius) gives off 2 heads attaching to the base of the femur directly above the knee. The deep (profundis) mass of muscle (the soleus) forms the remaining head which attaches to the superior posterior area of the tibia. The triceps surae is innervated by the tibial nerve, specifically, nerve roots L5-S2. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Endochondral bone, membrane bone, and Weberian ossicle that is an element of third vertebra. Anteriorly it attaches to the interosseus ligament and posteriorly it extends as a transformator process embedded in the tunica externa of the swimbladder.
description_en: Endochondral bone, membrane bone, and Weberian ossicle that is an element of third vertebra. Anteriorly it attaches to the interosseus ligament and posteriorly it extends as a transformator process embedded in the tunica externa of the swimbladder.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The mesectodermal cell layer arising from the trophectoderm that erodes the uterine mucosa and contributes to the formation of the placenta.
description_en: The mesectodermal cell layer arising from the trophectoderm that erodes the uterine mucosa and contributes to the formation of the placenta.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A rib that is ventrally connected to the sternum.
description_en: A rib that is ventrally connected to the sternum.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bone that is part of a trunk [Automatically generated definition].
description_en: A bone that is part of a trunk [Automatically generated definition].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vertebra in the trunk or cervical region. Includes all cervical, thoracic and lumbar vertebrae, but excludes caudal vertebra.
description_en: A vertebra in the trunk or cervical region. Includes all cervical, thoracic and lumbar vertebrae, but excludes caudal vertebra.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Subdivision of vertebral column that corresponds to the trunk of the body, containing the trunk/presacral vertebrae. In organisms that have a thoracic and lumbar distinction, this corresponds to the sum of both of these regions.
description_en: Subdivision of vertebral column that corresponds to the trunk of the body, containing the trunk/presacral vertebrae. In organisms that have a thoracic and lumbar distinction, this corresponds to the sum of both of these regions.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Rib located in the trunk (ribcage) area (i.e. excluding cervical and caudal axial series.
description_en: Rib located in the trunk (ribcage) area (i.e. excluding cervical and caudal axial series.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vertebra in the trunk region. For tetrapods, includes lumbar and thoracic vertebrae. Excludes caudal/coccygeal vertebra, which are located posteriorly. In tetrapods this includes thoracic, lumbar and sacral vertebrae, and excludes the cervical vertebrae, which are located anteriorly.
description_en: A vertebra in the trunk region. For tetrapods, includes lumbar and thoracic vertebrae. Excludes caudal/coccygeal vertebra, which are located posteriorly. In tetrapods this includes thoracic, lumbar and sacral vertebrae, and excludes the cervical vertebrae, which are located anteriorly.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A round nodule, small eminence, or warty outgrowth on an anatomical surface, such as bones, skin, or within the lungs (in the case of tuberculosis). They are also found on the leading edge of Humpback Whale's flippers, improving fluid flow over the flipper's surface[WP].
description_en: A round nodule, small eminence, or warty outgrowth on an anatomical surface, such as bones, skin, or within the lungs (in the case of tuberculosis). They are also found on the leading edge of Humpback Whale's flippers, improving fluid flow over the flipper's surface[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The tubercle of a rib is an eminence on the posterior surface, at the junction of the neck and body of the rib, and nearer the lower than the upper border. It consists of an articular and a non-articular portion. The articular portion, the lower and more medial of the two, presents a small, oval surface for articulation with the end of the transverse process of the lower of the two vertebrae to which the head is connected. The non-articular portion is a rough elevation, and affords attachment to the ligament of the tubercle. The tubercle is much more prominent in the upper than in the lower ribs[WP].
description_en: The tubercle of a rib is an eminence on the posterior surface, at the junction of the neck and body of the rib, and nearer the lower than the upper border. It consists of an articular and a non-articular portion. The articular portion, the lower and more medial of the two, presents a small, oval surface for articulation with the end of the transverse process of the lower of the two vertebrae to which the head is connected. The non-articular portion is a rough elevation, and affords attachment to the ligament of the tubercle. The tubercle is much more prominent in the upper than in the lower ribs[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The small curved bones that extends horizontally along the lateral wall of the nasal passage.
description_en: The small curved bones that extends horizontally along the lateral wall of the nasal passage.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A highly complicated shield for the ventral and dorsal parts of the turtle, completely enclosing all the vital organs of the turtle and in some cases even the head. It is constructed of modified bony elements such as the ribs, parts of the pelvis and other bones found in most reptiles. The bone of the shell consists of both skeletal and dermal bone, showing that the complete enclosure of the shell probably evolved by including dermal armor into the rib cage.[WP].
description_en: A highly complicated shield for the ventral and dorsal parts of the turtle, completely enclosing all the vital organs of the turtle and in some cases even the head. It is constructed of modified bony elements such as the ribs, parts of the pelvis and other bones found in most reptiles. The bone of the shell consists of both skeletal and dermal bone, showing that the complete enclosure of the shell probably evolved by including dermal armor into the rib cage.[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A minute canal that passes from the petrous portion of the temporal bone between the jugular fossa and carotid canal to the floor of the tympanic cavity and transmits the tympanic branch of the glossopharyngeal nerve.
description_en: A minute canal that passes from the petrous portion of the temporal bone between the jugular fossa and carotid canal to the floor of the tympanic cavity and transmits the tympanic branch of the glossopharyngeal nerve.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Small cavity surrounding the bones of the middle ear.
description_en: Small cavity surrounding the bones of the middle ear.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A thin membrane that separates the external ear from the middle ear, consisting of two epithelia (one part of the the external accoustic meatus epithelium, the other part of the tympanic cavity epithelium) with a fibrous layer between them. Its function is to transmit sound from the air to the ossicles inside the middle ear. The malleus bone bridges the gap between the eardrum and the other ossicles. Rupture or perforation of the eardrum can lead to conductive hearing loss. [WP,unvetted].
description_en: A thin membrane that separates the external ear from the middle ear, consisting of two epithelia (one part of the the external accoustic meatus epithelium, the other part of the tympanic cavity epithelium) with a fibrous layer between them. Its function is to transmit sound from the air to the ossicles inside the middle ear. The malleus bone bridges the gap between the eardrum and the other ossicles. Rupture or perforation of the eardrum can lead to conductive hearing loss. [WP,unvetted].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The tympanic part of the temporal bone is a curved plate of bone lying below the squama and in front of the mastoid process.
description_en: The tympanic part of the temporal bone is a curved plate of bone lying below the squama and in front of the mastoid process.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A C-shaped membranous bone that provides physical support to the tympanic membrane. The tympanic ring develops sequentially from an initial primordium in the first branchial arch growing in a circumferential fashion around the first pharyngeal cleft into the second branchial arch (Mallo and Gridley, 1996). In most mammals, the tympanic ring exists only during embryonic life, when it coordinates proper development and positioning of the eardrum (see below), and then becomes integrated into the temporal bone[PMID].
description_en: A C-shaped membranous bone that provides physical support to the tympanic membrane. The tympanic ring develops sequentially from an initial primordium in the first branchial arch growing in a circumferential fashion around the first pharyngeal cleft into the second branchial arch (Mallo and Gridley, 1996). In most mammals, the tympanic ring exists only during embryonic life, when it coordinates proper development and positioning of the eardrum (see below), and then becomes integrated into the temporal bone[PMID].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The terminal segment in the chain of skeletal elements of the hyoid apparatus. One of a pair of rods of cartilage that connect the hyoid bone to the styloid process of the petrous part of the temporal bone.
description_en: The terminal segment in the chain of skeletal elements of the hyoid apparatus. One of a pair of rods of cartilage that connect the hyoid bone to the styloid process of the petrous part of the temporal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Central, funnel-shaped, ossified portion of the tympanic annulus fused to the squamosal bone.
description_en: Central, funnel-shaped, ossified portion of the tympanic annulus fused to the squamosal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Odontode that is attached to dermal bone.
description_en: Odontode that is attached to dermal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Odontode that is attached to the skin and without association to dermal bone.
description_en: Odontode that is attached to the skin and without association to dermal bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The ulna is the longer forearm bone with a prominent olecranon process at its proximal end. The trochlear notch articulates with the trochlea of the humerus. The coronoid process prevents posterior dislocation. The head and styloid process are at the distal end.
description_en: The ulna is the longer forearm bone with a prominent olecranon process at its proximal end. The trochlear notch articulates with the trochlea of the humerus. The coronoid process prevents posterior dislocation. The head and styloid process are at the distal end.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Ulnar artery: larger terminal branch of the brachial artery, running the medial forearm to form the superficial and deep palmar arches.
description_en: Ulnar artery: larger terminal branch of the brachial artery, running the medial forearm to form the superficial and deep palmar arches.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The postaxial bone of the proximal carpal region. Found in close approximation to the ulna, often in articulation[PHENOSCAPE:ad].
description_en: The postaxial bone of the proximal carpal region. Found in close approximation to the ulna, often in articulation[PHENOSCAPE:ad].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bony element (ulnar sesamoid bone) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.
description_en: A bony element (ulnar sesamoid bone) that provides structural support and protection in the skeletal system.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): His roughened area of bone sits distomedially at the base of the coronoid process. It is the attachment site for the brachialis muscle. From http://www.anatomyexpert.com/.
description_en: His roughened area of bone sits distomedially at the base of the coronoid process. It is the attachment site for the brachialis muscle. From http://www.anatomyexpert.com/.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein that is tributary of the brachial vein and drains blood from the hand and medial and posterior aspect of forearm.
description_en: A vein that is tributary of the brachial vein and drains blood from the hand and medial and posterior aspect of forearm.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Pathway arising from the fastigial nucleus to the vestibular nuclei, reticular formation, motor neurons of brainstem and cervical spinal cord (Butler and Hodos, Comparative Vertebrate Neuroanatomy, 2nd ed., 2005, pg 261).
description_en: Pathway arising from the fastigial nucleus to the vestibular nuclei, reticular formation, motor neurons of brainstem and cervical spinal cord (Butler and Hodos, Comparative Vertebrate Neuroanatomy, 2nd ed., 2005, pg 261).

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): In the ethmoid bone, a curved lamina, the uncinate process, projects downward and backward from this part of the labyrinth; it forms a small part of the medial wall of the maxillary sinus, and articulates with the ethmoidal process of the inferior nasal concha.
description_en: In the ethmoid bone, a curved lamina, the uncinate process, projects downward and backward from this part of the labyrinth; it forms a small part of the medial wall of the maxillary sinus, and articulates with the ethmoidal process of the inferior nasal concha.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A posterior projection from proximal rib segments. Offers attachment sites for respiratory and shoulder muscles as well as adding structural support to the trunk skeleton[Kardong 2012].
description_en: A posterior projection from proximal rib segments. Offers attachment sites for respiratory and shoulder muscles as well as adding structural support to the trunk skeleton[Kardong 2012].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Free nerve endings are widely distributed throughout the body, and are found as branches of unmyelinated, or lightly myelinated fibres grouped in bundles beneath the epithelium. As they penetrate the epithelium, they lose their myelin, and branch among the epithelial cells. Branches of one nerve may cover a wide area and overlap the territories of other nerves. The free nerve endings detect pain, touch, pressure and temperature, and are associated with C fibres.
description_en: Free nerve endings are widely distributed throughout the body, and are found as branches of unmyelinated, or lightly myelinated fibres grouped in bundles beneath the epithelium. As they penetrate the epithelium, they lose their myelin, and branch among the epithelial cells. Branches of one nerve may cover a wide area and overlap the territories of other nerves. The free nerve endings detect pain, touch, pressure and temperature, and are associated with C fibres.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bone surface that is not smooth and periosteal.  The usual implication is that the bone was still growing, was covered in cartilage, or both. From Paleos.com.
description_en: A bone surface that is not smooth and periosteal.  The usual implication is that the bone was still growing, was covered in cartilage, or both. From Paleos.com.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The bone of the upper arm, the humerus connects the shoulder to the elbow and provides the attachment points for muscles of the shoulder and arm that enable a wide range of upper limb movement. Proximally it articulates with the scapula at the glenohumeral joint, and distally with the radius and ulna at the elbow. Its surface landmarks include the greater and lesser tubercles, the deltoid tuberosity, and the medial and lateral epicondyles. Fractures of the surgical neck are common in elderly patients, while midshaft fractures may damage the radial nerve and cause wrist drop. In children, supracondylar fractures are the most common fractures at the elbow.
description_en: The bone of the upper arm, the humerus connects the shoulder to the elbow and provides the attachment points for muscles of the shoulder and arm that enable a wide range of upper limb movement. Proximally it articulates with the scapula at the glenohumeral joint, and distally with the radius and ulna at the elbow. Its surface landmarks include the greater and lesser tubercles, the deltoid tuberosity, and the medial and lateral epicondyles. Fractures of the surgical neck are common in elderly patients, while midshaft fractures may damage the radial nerve and cause wrist drop. In children, supracondylar fractures are the most common fractures at the elbow.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Anatomical cluster including hypural 3 and more dorsal hypurals that supports the dorsal series of principal caudal lepidotrichia or rays. The upper hypural set articulates or fuses to ural centra 3, 4 or 5 (polyural terminology) or ural centrum 2 (diural terminology) depending on the teleost subgroup. The upper hypural set is composed of unpaired median bones.
description_en: Anatomical cluster including hypural 3 and more dorsal hypurals that supports the dorsal series of principal caudal lepidotrichia or rays. The upper hypural set articulates or fuses to ural centra 3, 4 or 5 (polyural terminology) or ural centrum 2 (diural terminology) depending on the teleost subgroup. The upper hypural set is composed of unpaired median bones.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An anatomical space that is part of a bone of upper jaw.
description_en: An anatomical space that is part of a bone of upper jaw.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A bone that is part of a hindlimb stylopod [Automatically generated definition].
description_en: A bone that is part of a hindlimb stylopod [Automatically generated definition].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vertebral centrum that is posterior to preural vertebra 1 and consequently the most posterior vertebral centra. Ural centrum is a unpaired median bone.
description_en: A vertebral centrum that is posterior to preural vertebra 1 and consequently the most posterior vertebral centra. Ural centrum is a unpaired median bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vertebral centrum that is immediately posterior to preural vertebra 1. Ural centrum 1 is an unpaired median bone.
description_en: A vertebral centrum that is immediately posterior to preural vertebra 1. Ural centrum 1 is an unpaired median bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vertebral centrum that is located immediately posterior to ural centrum 1. Ural centrum 2 is an unpaired median bone.
description_en: A vertebral centrum that is located immediately posterior to ural centrum 1. Ural centrum 2 is an unpaired median bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vertebral centrum that is located immediately posterior to ural centrum 2 (polyural terminology). Ural centrum 3 articulates with hypural 3 ventrally. Ural centrum 3 is an unpaired median bone.
description_en: A vertebral centrum that is located immediately posterior to ural centrum 2 (polyural terminology). Ural centrum 3 articulates with hypural 3 ventrally. Ural centrum 3 is an unpaired median bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vertebral centrum that is located immediately posterior to ural centrum 3 (polyural terminology) and may fuse to ural centrum 3 early in ontogeny. Ural centrum 4 articulates with hypural 4 ventrally. Ural centrum 4 is an unpaired median bone.
description_en: A vertebral centrum that is located immediately posterior to ural centrum 3 (polyural terminology) and may fuse to ural centrum 3 early in ontogeny. Ural centrum 4 articulates with hypural 4 ventrally. Ural centrum 4 is an unpaired median bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Vertebra that is incomplete or rudimentary and may bear a rudimentary neural arch and sometimes a rudimentary spine or the neural arch and spine are completely absent. Ural vertebrae are one of the last bony elements of the vertebral column, usually smaller than the preural centra. Ural vertebrae are numbered beginning from anterior (1) to posterior (2, 3, 4, etc.). Ural vertebra is an unpaired median bone.
description_en: Vertebra that is incomplete or rudimentary and may bear a rudimentary neural arch and sometimes a rudimentary spine or the neural arch and spine are completely absent. Ural vertebrae are one of the last bony elements of the vertebral column, usually smaller than the preural centra. Ural vertebrae are numbered beginning from anterior (1) to posterior (2, 3, 4, etc.). Ural vertebra is an unpaired median bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Ural vertebra that is located directly posterior to preural centrum 1. It may bear a rudimentary neural arch and sometimes a rudimentary spine or the neural arch and spine are completely absent and it may articulate or fuse with hypural 1 (polyural terminology). Ural vertebra 1 is an unpaired median bone.
description_en: Ural vertebra that is located directly posterior to preural centrum 1. It may bear a rudimentary neural arch and sometimes a rudimentary spine or the neural arch and spine are completely absent and it may articulate or fuse with hypural 1 (polyural terminology). Ural vertebra 1 is an unpaired median bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Ural vertebra that is the second vertebra posterior to preural centrum 1. It may bear a rudimentary neural arch and sometimes a rudimentary spine or the neural arch and spine are completely absent and it may articulate or fuse with hypural 2 (polyural terminology). Ural vertebra 2 is an unpaired median bone.
description_en: Ural vertebra that is the second vertebra posterior to preural centrum 1. It may bear a rudimentary neural arch and sometimes a rudimentary spine or the neural arch and spine are completely absent and it may articulate or fuse with hypural 2 (polyural terminology). Ural vertebra 2 is an unpaired median bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The portion of the ureteric bud that contributes to the morphogenesis of the ureter. The ureter ureteric bud is the initial structure that forms the ureter[GO].
description_en: The portion of the ureteric bud that contributes to the morphogenesis of the ureter. The ureter ureteric bud is the initial structure that forms the ureter[GO].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Paired, thin dermal bones at the rear of the caudal fin skeleton, derived from scales.
description_en: Paired, thin dermal bones at the rear of the caudal fin skeleton, derived from scales.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Tendon bone that forms in the tendon of the sternohyoid muscles ventral to the anterior end of copula 1. The urohyal associates by ligaments to the ventral hypohyals or it articulates with the ventral hypohyals. The urohyal is an unpaired bone.
description_en: Tendon bone that forms in the tendon of the sternohyoid muscles ventral to the anterior end of copula 1. The urohyal associates by ligaments to the ventral hypohyals or it articulates with the ventral hypohyals. The urohyal is an unpaired bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Neural arch that extends along the dorso-lateral surface of the last preural centra and/or ural centra and the notochord (Arratia & Schultze, 1992). An uroneural develops as a modification of the neural arch of an ural centrum (Patterson, 1968). The series of uroneurals may include from 7 to 1 elements that are numbered from rostrad to caudad. An uroneural is a paired membrane bone.
description_en: Neural arch that extends along the dorso-lateral surface of the last preural centra and/or ural centra and the notochord (Arratia & Schultze, 1992). An uroneural develops as a modification of the neural arch of an ural centrum (Patterson, 1968). The series of uroneurals may include from 7 to 1 elements that are numbered from rostrad to caudad. An uroneural is a paired membrane bone.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein that is tributary of the internal iliac vein and drains the uterus.
description_en: A vein that is tributary of the internal iliac vein and drains the uterus.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The musculus uvulae (azygos uvulae) is a muscle of the soft palate. It arises from the posterior nasal spine of the palatine bones and from the palatine aponeurosis. It descends to be inserted into the uvula and functions to move and shape it. It is innervated by the pharyngeal branch of the vagus nerve via the pharyngeal plexus[WP].
description_en: The musculus uvulae (azygos uvulae) is a muscle of the soft palate. It arises from the posterior nasal spine of the palatine bones and from the palatine aponeurosis. It descends to be inserted into the uvula and functions to move and shape it. It is innervated by the pharyngeal branch of the vagus nerve via the pharyngeal plexus[WP].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Vastus intermedius (Cruraeus) arises from the front and lateral surfaces of the body of the femur in its upper two-thirds, sitting under Rectus Femoris and from the lower part of the lateral intermuscular septum. Its fibers end in a superficial aponeurosis, which forms the deep part of the Quadriceps femoris tendon. The Vastus medialis and Vastus intermedius appear to be inseparably united, but when the Rectus femoris has been reflected a narrow interval will be observed extending upward from the medial border of the patella between the two muscles, and the separation may be continued as far as the lower part of the intertrochanteric line, where, however, the two muscles are frequently continuous.
description_en: The Vastus intermedius (Cruraeus) arises from the front and lateral surfaces of the body of the femur in its upper two-thirds, sitting under Rectus Femoris and from the lower part of the lateral intermuscular septum. Its fibers end in a superficial aponeurosis, which forms the deep part of the Quadriceps femoris tendon. The Vastus medialis and Vastus intermedius appear to be inseparably united, but when the Rectus femoris has been reflected a narrow interval will be observed extending upward from the medial border of the patella between the two muscles, and the separation may be continued as far as the lower part of the intertrochanteric line, where, however, the two muscles are frequently continuous.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Vastus lateralis: the largest quadriceps head, arising by a broad femoral aponeurosis and inserting on the lateral border of the patella.
description_en: Vastus lateralis: the largest quadriceps head, arising by a broad femoral aponeurosis and inserting on the lateral border of the patella.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A portion of vein that is part of a trabecular bone tissue [Automatically generated definition].
description_en: A portion of vein that is part of a trabecular bone tissue [Automatically generated definition].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): A vein that leaves the vestibule through an individual bone canal running parallel to the vestibular aqueduct up to the dura of the posterior side of the petrosa in the area of the endolymphatic sac. It then opens in the inferior petrosal sinus or the jugular bulb. The vein receives other branches from the bone, dura and sac.
description_en: A vein that leaves the vestibule through an individual bone canal running parallel to the vestibular aqueduct up to the dura of the posterior side of the petrosa in the area of the endolymphatic sac. It then opens in the inferior petrosal sinus or the jugular bulb. The vein receives other branches from the bone, dura and sac.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The part of the cardiovascular system consisting of all venous vessels. In vertebrates with a double circulation, this can be divided into systemic and pulmonary portions.
description_en: The part of the cardiovascular system consisting of all venous vessels. In vertebrates with a double circulation, this can be divided into systemic and pulmonary portions.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Ventral head of a bicapitate rib. It articulates with the parapophysis[AAO].
description_en: Ventral head of a bicapitate rib. It articulates with the parapophysis[AAO].

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Replacement bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates with the ceratohyal bone posteriorly and the dorsal hypohyal bone dorsally.
description_en: Replacement bone that is bilaterally paired and articulates with the ceratohyal bone posteriorly and the dorsal hypohyal bone dorsally.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Joint that articulates the ventral hypohyal and urohyal bones. Ventral hypohyal-urohyal joint is paired.
description_en: Joint that articulates the ventral hypohyal and urohyal bones. Ventral hypohyal-urohyal joint is paired.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The ventral lateral sacrocaudal is a long strong muscle consisting of numerous individual parts. Its first segment originates from the last lumbar vertebrae and the remainder from the transverse processes of the caudal vertebrae. From the segmented bellies arise long tendons which are embedded in caudal fascia. The first of these tendons inserts onto the sixth caudal vertebrae, the second onto the seventh and so on until the last caudal vertebrae. The ventral lateral sacrocaudal acts to flex the tail and occasionally assists with lateral movement.
description_en: The ventral lateral sacrocaudal is a long strong muscle consisting of numerous individual parts. Its first segment originates from the last lumbar vertebrae and the remainder from the transverse processes of the caudal vertebrae. From the segmented bellies arise long tendons which are embedded in caudal fascia. The first of these tendons inserts onto the sixth caudal vertebrae, the second onto the seventh and so on until the last caudal vertebrae. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): In protostomes (such as insects, snails and worms) as well as deuterostomes (vertebrates), the midline is an embryonic region that functions in patterning of the adjacent nervous tissue. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The vertebral vein is formed in the suboccipital triangle, from numerous small tributaries which spring from the internal vertebral venous plexuses and issue from the vertebral canal above the posterior arch of the atlas. definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Paired processes at the cephalic and caudal ends of the neural arch. They function as interlocking structures between adjacent vertebrae, and limit dorsoventral flexion and lateral movement of the column in the trunk region[AAO]. The articular processes or zygapophyses of a vertebra, in human anatomy contain two superior and two inferior, spring from the junctions of the pedicles and laminae. These stick out of an end of a vertebra to lock with a zygapophysis on the next vertebra, to make the backbone more stable. The superior processes project upward from a lower vertebra, and their articular surfaces are directed more or less backward. The inferior processes project downward from a higher vertebra, and their articular surfaces are directed more or less forward and outward. The articular surfaces are coated with hyaline cartilage.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): The Zygomatic Fossa is an irregularly shaped cavity, situated below and on the inner side of the zygoma; bounded, in front, by the zygomatic surface of the superior maxillary bone and the ridge which descends from its malar process; behind, by the posterior border of the external pterygoid plate and the eminentia articularis; above, by the pterygoid ridge on the outer surface of the great wing of the sphenoid and the under part of the squamous portion of the temporal; below by the alveolar border of the superior maxilla; internally, by the external pterygoid plate; and externally, by the zygomatic arch ramus of the lower jaw. It contains the lower part of the temporal, the External and Internal pterygoid muscles, the internal maxillary artery and vein, and inferior maxillary nerve and their branches. At its upper and inner part may be observed two fissures, the spheno-maxillary and pterygo-maxillary.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): In rodent anatomy, the zygomatic plate is a bony plate derived from the flattened front part of the zygomatic arch (cheekbone). At the back, it connects to the front (maxillary) root of the zygomatic arch, and at the top it is connected to the rest of the skull via the antorbital bridge. It is part of the maxillary bone, or upper jaw, which also contains the upper cheekteeth. Primitively, rodents have a nearly horizontal zygomatic plate. In association with specializations in zygomasseteric system, several distinct morphologies have developed across the order. The term is also used for an analogous structure in some South American typotheres, including Pseudotypotherium and Medistylus.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Facial muscle attached to the modiolus, corner (angle) of the mouth, and zygomatic bone. See Diogo 2008; Diogo et al., 2009; Burrows et al.., 2011., also DuBrul, 1980.
description_en: Facial muscle attached to the modiolus, corner (angle) of the mouth, and zygomatic bone. See Diogo 2008; Diogo et al., 2009; Burrows et al.., 2011., also DuBrul, 1980.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): Facial muscle attached to the modiolus, corner (angle) of the mouth, and zygomatic bone. This muscle is ventral to the zygomaticus minor and dorsal to the platysma muscle. In many mammals this muscle also has an attachment to the cartilage of the external ear, in which case it is called the auriculolabialis inferior. See Diogo 2008; Diogo et al., 2009; Burrows et al.., 2011., also DuBrul, 1980.
description_en: Facial muscle attached to the modiolus, corner (angle) of the mouth, and zygomatic bone. This muscle is ventral to the zygomaticus minor and dorsal to the platysma muscle. In many mammals this muscle also has an attachment to the cartilage of the external ear, in which case it is called the auriculolabialis inferior. See Diogo 2008; Diogo et al., 2009; Burrows et al.., 2011., also DuBrul, 1980.

definition_uz: Anatomik ta'rif (Suyak): An articular process on anterior surface of neural arch of vertebrae which fits into zygantrum. Modified from Henderson's dictionary of Biological terms 12th Edition.
description_en: An articular process on anterior surface of neural arch of vertebrae which fits into zygantrum. Modified from Henderson's dictionary of Biological terms 12th Edition.
